value_domain: Dollar amount of non-refundable tax offsets applied at assessment
value_source: ATO, About tax offsets
variable_description: How much of a person's non-refundable tax offset entitlement the ATO actually applied against their tax for the year. It is an assessment outcome, not a label the taxpayer filled in, and it is capped by the tax they owed: the ATO says "Most offsets aren't refundable, which means they can't reduce your tax below zero." The neighbouring 'available' offset columns carry entitlement, so the two together show how much of an entitlement was wasted.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount computed at assessment, summing the non-refundable offsets that were used across every offset type claimed on the return. It is bounded below by zero and above by tax payable before offsets.
limitation: It cannot measure entitlement or eligibility. A zero here is as likely to mean the person had no tax to reduce as it is to mean they claimed nothing, so an offset take-up rate built from this column will understate claims among low-income filers.
rationale: The label names the used, rather than available, total of non-refundable offsets, and the ATO's own explanation of tax offsets sets out exactly why a used amount differs from an entitlement.
evidence_quote: Most offsets aren't refundable, which means they can't reduce your tax below zero.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Non refundable offsets used' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said that the amount is capped by tax payable rather than by entitlement.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at Spouse details label S
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, IT1 Total reportable fringe benefits amounts and Spouse details
variable_description: The reportable fringe benefits the taxpayer's spouse received from employers that are not exempt from fringe benefits tax under section 57A. The lodger copies the figure their spouse reports at IT1 label W into the spouse details section, and the ATO treats the two as one quantity: "We don't adjust the amounts at question IT1 - label W, and question Spouse details - married or de facto - label S, when we calculate the following offsets." The exempt-employer half of the spouse's benefits sits in the neighbouring column.
value_definition: A whole-dollar grossed-up taxable value of fringe benefits, originally reported by the spouse's employer on an income statement or payment summary, with benefits below the reporting threshold (currently $3,773) excluded.
limitation: It is one side of a split the return did not always have, so it cannot be joined to the single spouse fringe benefits total that earlier years carried without breaking the series. It is also third-hand: the lodger is describing someone else's income, and the instructions permit a reasonable estimate.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the section 57A non-exempt half of the spouse's reportable fringe benefits, and the ATO instruction for IT1 defines that half and states that the spouse details label carries the same amount.
evidence_quote: We don't adjust the amounts at question IT1 - label W, and question Spouse details - married or de facto - label S, when we calculate the following offsets
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the long custodian label and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said where the figure comes from, that a spouse's employer reports it, or that it is only half of the spouse's reportable benefits.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 13 label Y
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Deductions the taxpayer claims against non-primary production distributions from partnerships and trusts. The ATO instruction is to "Write at question 13 - label Y the total of other deductions (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) you can claim in relation to your share of both: non-primary production income or loss from a partnership; non-primary production income of a trust". It is subtracted, with the landcare deduction at label J, when the net non-primary production amount is worked out.
value_definition: Whole dollars, self-assessed, covering residual deductions against flow-through income: it excludes the landcare expenditure claimed at label J and the primary production equivalent claimed at label X.
limitation: It does not separate a current-year expense from a business loss deferred out of an earlier year, and the only thing that distinguishes them is the Type code beside it, which reports all, part or none rather than an amount.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the non-primary production other deductions against distributions, which is the ATO's own description of item 13 label Y, and the instruction defines what may and may not go there.
evidence_quote: Write at question 13 - label Y the total of other deductions (including non-commercial business losses deferred from a prior income year) you can claim in relation to your share of both:
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence in both the value definition and the limitation, so it never identified the label or said that deferred prior-year losses are folded into the same number.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 13 label C
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Franked distributions a beneficiary received from trusts, shown apart from the rest of their trust income. The ATO says: "If your statement of distribution or advice shows your share of franked distributions from trusts separately, write this amount at label C, together with any share of franking credits referrable to those franked distributions." A partner in a partnership never uses this label, because the same instruction sends partnership franked distributions to label O.
value_definition: Whole dollars, grossed up to include the attached franking credits, and confined to non-primary production trust income.
limitation: It captures only the trust channel, so it understates a person's franked income from flow-through entities whenever a partnership is in the chain. The credits themselves are claimed again at label Q, so adding this column to label Q counts the gross-up twice.
rationale: The custodian's wording is the ATO's own name for item 13 label C, and the instruction states what goes in the label, what it must include and which taxpayers must use a different label instead.
evidence_quote: If your statement of distribution or advice shows your share of franked distributions from trusts separately, write this amount at label C, together with any share of franking credits referrable to those franked distributions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label name and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it never said the amount includes franking credits or that partnership distributions are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 16 label J
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 16 Deferred non-commercial business losses
variable_description: Losses from non-primary production business activities that the taxpayer was not allowed to use this year and had to defer. The ATO is explicit that the number does no work in the current year: "You can't use the amount at question 16 to reduce your 2024-25 taxable income." It is a subtotal, formed by adding the non-primary production part of the partnership losses at label F to the non-primary production part of the sole trader losses at label G.
value_definition: Whole dollars of net loss deferred under the non-commercial business loss rules, split from the primary production deferral at label I.
limitation: It cannot tell you whether the loss came from a partnership or from a sole trader activity, because the split by legal form lives in labels F and G. Nor is it a loss written off: the amount stays available against the same or a similar activity in a later year, and bankruptcy is the main way it disappears.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the non-primary production deferred loss total, which the ATO instruction defines as label J and builds from labels F and G.
evidence_quote: Add up any amounts of non-primary production deferred losses at question 16 - labels F and G. Write the total of non-primary production deferred losses at question 16 - label J.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said that the amount is quarantined from taxable income or that it is a subtotal of two other labels.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 13 label J
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: A partner's share of landcare operations spending, claimed against non-primary production distributions at item 13 label J. The deduction is pushed out to the partners rather than taken by the entity: "If a partnership incurs eligible expenditure on landcare operations, the partnership can't claim the expenditure. Costs the partnership incurs are allocated to each partner who can then claim the deduction." The primary production version of the same claim sits at label I and is wider, taking in water facilities, fencing and fodder storage assets.
value_definition: Whole dollars, being the taxpayer's allocated share of eligible landcare expenditure that is deductible in the year of the return.
limitation: It is a partner's claim only. A trust beneficiary can never appear here, because the instruction reserves the deduction to the trustee, so a zero says nothing about whether the underlying entity spent money on landcare.
rationale: The custodian's wording names non-primary production landcare operations expenses, which the ATO instruction places at item 13 label J and defines by who may claim it.
evidence_quote: Write your share of the total of any such expenditure that relates to non-primary production income or loss from partnerships that you can deduct in 2024-25 at question 13 - label J in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained that only partners can use the label or how it differs from the primary production landcare column.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at L1 label R
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question L1 Tax losses of earlier income years
variable_description: The stock of non-primary production tax losses from earlier years that the taxpayer brought into this return. The worksheet reaches it by taking losses from earlier years and reducing them by net exempt income: "Non-primary production losses available for use in 2024-25. Subtract row f from row c." How much of that stock was actually deducted is the claimed column at label Z, not this one.
value_definition: Whole dollars of prior-year losses available for use, already net of exempt income and split from the primary production stock at label Q.
limitation: It is the opening balance, not the closing one. The instructions tell the taxpayer to keep their own record of what carries forward to the next year, so the amount still unused at year end cannot be read off the return and has to be reconstructed from this column and the claimed column.
rationale: The custodian's wording names non-primary production losses carried forward at L1, and the instruction gives the worksheet row that feeds label R and the deduction for net exempt income.
evidence_quote: Transfer the amount at row i to question L1 - label R.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing distinguished the available stock from the amount claimed, which is the confusion this pair of columns invites.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at L1 label Z
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question L1 Tax losses of earlier income years
variable_description: How much of the taxpayer's earlier-year non-primary production losses was actually deducted against this year's income. The amount is mechanical rather than chosen: the instruction says the steps "will help you work out what to write at question L1 - labels F and Z, if the amount at Subtotal isn't a loss", and primary production losses at label F are applied before any non-primary production loss reaches label Z. The stock the claim draws on is the carried-forward column at label R.
value_definition: Whole dollars, bounded above by the losses available at label R and by the income left after the primary production claim at label F.
limitation: A zero does not mean the person had no losses. It usually means there was no income left to absorb them, so this column measures the interaction of losses with income rather than the existence of losses, which only label R can show.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the non-primary production losses claimed this year, and the L1 instruction sets out the ordering rule that determines the amount at label Z.
evidence_quote: The following steps will help you work out what to write at question L1 - labels F and Z, if the amount at Subtotal isn't a loss.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the claim is forced by a worksheet or that it is capped by the primary production claim on the same row.

value_domain: Type code beside item 13 label Y (D, P or blank)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: A one-letter code saying how much of the deduction at item 13 label Y is a business loss deferred out of an earlier year. The ATO sets only two codes: "Print D if the entire amount at label Y is a deferred non-commercial business loss from a prior income year" and "Print P if only part of the amount at label Y is a deferred non-commercial business loss from a prior income year", with the box left blank otherwise. It qualifies the non-primary production deduction column beside it and nothing else.
value_definition: A single character: D where the whole label Y amount is a deferred loss, P where only part of it is, and blank where none of it is.
limitation: P gives no fraction, so the deferred component cannot be recovered from the code and the amount together. The matching code for primary production sits in the Type box at label X and is a separate column, so this one says nothing about farm activities.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a type code for other deductions against non-primary production distributions, and the instruction publishes the two-value code list for the Type box at label Y.
evidence_quote: Print D if the entire amount at label Y is a deferred non-commercial business loss from a prior income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, even though the ATO publishes a two-value code list for this exact box.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at IT6 Net rental property loss
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question IT6 Net rental property loss
variable_description: A person's total loss from renting out property, collected for the income tests rather than for working out taxable income. The ATO defines it plainly: "Net property loss is the amount of net loss from any rental property you own", and says "We'll calculate the amount of your net rental property loss for you using the information you provide in your tax return." It pulls together net rent, net foreign rent, partnership rental distributions and rental business income, less low-value pool and other rental deductions.
value_definition: A whole-dollar loss amount, written as zero whenever the rental position is a profit, and covering Australian and foreign rent together.
limitation: It is censored at zero, so it cannot measure rental profit, the number of properties or the scale of a portfolio, and a zero cannot be read as 'no rental property'. Capital gains and losses on rental properties are excluded, so it is not a measure of how a property investment performed.
rationale: The custodian's wording is the ATO's own name for the income test item, and the instruction defines the quantity and lists the components its worksheet adds and subtracts.
evidence_quote: Net property loss is the amount of net loss from any rental property you own.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Net rental property loss' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the value is censored at zero or that it is an income test measure rather than a deduction.

value_domain: ATO salary and wage occupation code
value_source: ATO, Salary and wage occupation codes
variable_description: The coded occupation the taxpayer gave for the salary and wage job that earned them the most during the year. The coverage rule is narrow: "the occupation description and codes apply to salary and wage income only and not to other types of income such as pensions and business or investment income". Where nothing fits, the ATO directs the filer to "use the 'Occupation not listed' code 999000", so that value is a residual rather than an occupation.
value_definition: A numeric code drawn from the ATO's published salary and wage occupation list, six digits in the current edition and grouped by the leading digits, with 999000 reserved for occupations not on the list.
limitation: It is not a labour force classification and not a person's main activity. A wage earner who also runs a business is coded on the wage job alone, a person with no salary or wages has no code at all, and the code is entered by the filer or their agent rather than derived from an employer record.
rationale: The custodian's wording names an occupation group code on the individual return, and the ATO publishes the code list, the label it is written at and the rule for choosing between multiple jobs.
evidence_quote: the occupation description and codes apply to salary and wage income only and not to other types of income such as pensions and business or investment income
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the misspelt custodian wording 'Ocupation group code' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which job is coded, that the list is the ATO's own, or that 999000 means not listed.

value_domain: Dollar cost reported at P18 label J
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P17 to P20 Depreciating assets
variable_description: The cost of tangible depreciating assets the business began claiming decline in value on for the first time this year. The ATO says: "At P18 Other depreciating assets first deducted you need to include the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) that you're claiming a business deduction for the decline in value for the first time." Assets costing under $1,000 that went into a low-value pool are counted here too, and the cost is not scaled back for private use.
value_definition: Whole dollars of asset cost, summed across all of the person's businesses, and covering everything except the intangible assets that are reported at P17.
limitation: It is not depreciation and not investment in the year. An asset bought in an earlier year but first deducted now lands here, and an asset the business bought and immediately wrote off under a small business concession may be reported elsewhere, so this column will not reconcile to capital spending.
rationale: The custodian's wording is the ATO's own name for P18, and the instruction defines what the label counts, how pooled assets are treated and that cost is not reduced for non-taxable use.
evidence_quote: At P18 Other depreciating assets first deducted you need to include the cost of all depreciating assets (other than intangible depreciating assets) that you're claiming a business deduction for the decline in value for the first time.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said the figure is a cost rather than a deduction or how it differs from the intangible column.

value_domain: Dollar termination value reported at P20 label K
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P17 to P20 Depreciating assets
variable_description: What the business received for tangible depreciating assets it stopped holding or using during the year. The ATO defines the amount as "the amount you receive or are deemed to receive for the asset that you stop holding or using", including the market value of non-cash benefits, and substitutes market value where the parties do not deal at arm's length. Assets sold, lost or destroyed are all treated the same way, and the intangible equivalent is reported separately at P19.
value_definition: Whole dollars, summed across the person's businesses, and including assets that had been allocated to a low-value pool.
limitation: It is gross proceeds, not a gain or a loss on disposal: working out the balancing adjustment needs the asset's adjustable value, which the schedule never collects. It also gives no count of assets, so a single large disposal and many small ones look identical.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the termination value of other depreciating assets, which is the ATO's own name for P20, and the instruction defines termination value and the non-arm's length rule.
evidence_quote: Generally, the termination value is the amount you receive or are deemed to receive for the asset that you stop holding or using.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what termination value means or that it is not a measure of profit on disposal.

value_domain: Dollar amount of baby bonus claimed as a refundable tax offset
value_source: ATO Legal database, Explanatory Memorandum, Taxation Laws Amendment (Baby Bonus) Act 2002
variable_description: A parent's claim for the first-child baby bonus in a year after the year they first claimed it. This was a tax measure rather than a welfare payment: "The Baby Bonus is available as a refundable tax offset" and "Taxpayers will be able to make a claim for the Baby Bonus as part of their annual income tax return process." The explanatory memorandum sets the size and duration of the entitlement: "The repayment of tax will occur over a maximum period of 5 years with a maximum entitlement of $2,500 per year", with a $500 minimum for people on $25,000 or less.
value_definition: Whole dollars, refundable, generally derived from the claimant's gross tax paid in a base year spread over five years and capped at $2,500 a year.
limitation: It is not the maternity payment that later took the same popular name, so it cannot be used as a measure of birth-related assistance across the 2000s. The entitlement could also be transferred to a spouse, so the person carrying the amount is not necessarily the parent who gave birth.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a baby bonus claim in a year of the individual return when the first-child refundable tax offset was in force, and the explanatory memorandum gives the offset's nature, ceiling, floor and five-year run.
evidence_quote: The Baby Bonus is available as a refundable tax offset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Baby bonus claim' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said which baby bonus this is or that it was a refundable offset claimed through the return.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at P8 Expenses label K
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P8 Expenses
variable_description: The value of trading stock the business held at the start of the income year, across primary and non-primary production together. The figure is tied to the year before rather than independently measured: "The opening value of an item of stock must equal its closing value in the previous year." Stock of a business that started up during the year is deliberately left out and shows up in purchases instead.
value_definition: Whole dollars, being the sum of the primary production and non-primary production opening stock columns of the P8 expenses section.
limitation: It is not an independent inventory count, and where the change in stock over the year is $5,000 or less the taxpayer may repeat the opening value as closing stock, so a zero change between the two columns can mean a genuine reconciliation or an election not to count.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the opening stock total, which the ATO instruction places at P8 Expenses label K and defines by reference to last year's closing stock.
evidence_quote: The opening value of an item of stock must equal its closing value in the previous year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Opening stock - total' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said the value is constrained to equal last year's closing stock or that new businesses are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar compulsory study and training loan repayment raised on an overseas resident
value_source: ATO, Overseas obligations when repaying loans
variable_description: The compulsory Trade Support Loan repayment worked out for a person who was living overseas, based on their worldwide income rather than their Australian income. Leaving the country does not suspend the debt: "You must repay your HELP (previously known as HECS), AASL (previously known as TSL) and VSL if you live overseas and are not an Australian resident for tax purposes." The Trade Support Loan has since been renamed the Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan, so the column and the current ATO wording use different names for the same debt.
value_definition: A whole-dollar obligation raised at assessment, calculated from repayment income plus non-resident foreign sourced income against the published minimum repayment thresholds.
limitation: It only exists where the person reported worldwide income, so a zero mixes a genuine below-threshold year with a year of non-reporting. It is an amount raised, not an amount collected, and voluntary payments made from overseas do not reduce it.
rationale: The custodian's wording names an overseas Trade Support Loan compulsory repayment, and the ATO's overseas repayment guidance sets out the obligation, the income base and the compulsory-versus-levy split.
evidence_quote: You must repay your HELP (previously known as HECS), AASL (previously known as TSL) and VSL if you live overseas and are not an Australian resident for tax purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Overseas TSL compulsory repayment due' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount rests on self-reported worldwide income or that the loan has been renamed.

value_domain: Dollar HELP repayment obligation raised on an overseas resident
value_source: ATO, Overseas obligations when repaying loans
variable_description: The Higher Education Loan Program repayment obligation raised on a person who lived overseas and reported their worldwide income. The obligation is not always the same instrument: "Repayments may be a compulsory repayment or an overseas levy depending on how your worldwide income is made up", so this column and the overseas levy column beside it describe two routes to the same debt. The Trade Support Loan and VET Student Loan columns on the same row carry the equivalent amounts for those loan types.
value_definition: Whole dollars raised against a HELP account at assessment, worked out from repayment income plus non-resident foreign sourced income converted to Australian dollars.
limitation: It says nothing about the loan balance behind it, which keeps being indexed whether or not a repayment is raised. A person with a HELP debt who never lodged a worldwide income report simply has no row, so absence is not evidence of no debt.
rationale: The custodian's wording names an overseas HELP repayment, and the ATO's overseas repayment guidance defines the income base and distinguishes a compulsory repayment from an overseas levy.
evidence_quote: Repayments may be a compulsory repayment or an overseas levy depending on how your worldwide income is made up.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Overseas HELP repayment' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing distinguished it from the levy and Trade Support Loan columns beside it.

value_domain: Dollar VET Student Loan overseas repayment obligation
value_source: ATO, Overseas obligations when repaying loans
variable_description: The VET Student Loan repayment obligation raised on a person living overseas, charged as an overseas levy where the income behind it was foreign sourced. The ATO explains the split: "Repayments may be a compulsory repayment or an overseas levy depending on how your worldwide income is made up." A levy is worked out on net non-resident foreign sourced income after a standard deduction under the simple self-assessment method, which is why it can differ from an ordinary compulsory repayment on the same income.
value_definition: Whole dollars raised against a VET Student Loan account, derived from worldwide income converted to Australian dollars under one of the three published income assessment methods.
limitation: The column cannot show which assessment method produced the figure, and the three methods give different answers on the same underlying income. It also covers only the VET loan, so a person with several study debts has their obligation spread across the neighbouring loan columns.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a VET Support Loan overseas compulsory repayable amount, and the ATO's overseas repayment guidance defines the overseas levy, the income base and the assessment methods.
evidence_quote: Repayments may be a compulsory repayment or an overseas levy depending on how your worldwide income is made up.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained what an overseas levy is or why it sits apart from a compulsory repayment.

value_domain: Dollar amount of assessable Australian pension and annuity income
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuities and superannuation income streams
variable_description: The assessable amount of Australian pensions and annuities other than government pensions and allowances, which are reported at their own item. The ATO describes the private side of this income as follows: "Australian annuities (or non-super annuities) are a series of regular payments you receive from a life insurance company or friendly society in return for a lump sum payment." The amount is net of the deductible part of any undeducted purchase price, so it is smaller than the gross pension shown on the payer's payment summary.
value_definition: Whole dollars of assessable pension or annuity income, taken from a payment summary issued by a super fund, retirement savings account provider or life office, and reduced by the deductible amount of the undeducted purchase price.
limitation: It is not a measure of retirement income across time. From 1 July 2007 superannuation income streams from a taxed source stopped being assessable for people aged 60 and over, so the same person with the same pension can drop out of this column entirely without any change in what they receive.
rationale: The custodian's wording names other Australian pensions or annuities on an early individual return, and the current instruction for the successor item defines the income, its source documents and the undeducted purchase price adjustment.
evidence_quote: Australian annuities (or non-super annuities) are a series of regular payments you receive from a life insurance company or friendly society in return for a lump sum payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other Australian pensions or annuities' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said what the amount excludes or that the 2007 superannuation changes break the series.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at P8 Income label J
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P8 Income
variable_description: Business income from non-primary production activities that none of the named payment labels picked up, which for most sole traders is the bulk of their turnover. It is defined by exclusion: "Your 'other business income' excludes amounts shown at labels C, D, B, E, F, N, O, G and H in your schedule." What is left includes gross sales of trading stock, gross earnings from services, recouped expenses, bad debts recovered, profit on sale of depreciating assets, royalties, insurance recoveries, subsidies and foreign exchange gains.
value_definition: Whole dollars of gross income, before expenses, and able to be a loss; the primary production equivalent is label I on the same row.
limitation: Because it is a residual, its meaning shifts with the labels around it: a change in withholding or reporting arrangements moves money between labels without anything changing in the business. It is turnover, not profit, so it cannot be compared with the net business income figures on the return.
rationale: The custodian's wording names other business income for non-primary production, which the ATO instruction places at P8 Income label J and defines by what the label excludes and includes.
evidence_quote: Your 'other business income' excludes amounts shown at labels C, D, B, E, F, N, O, G and H in your schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said the label is a residual defined against the other income labels.

value_domain: Loss indicator beside P8 Income label J
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P8 Income
variable_description: The one-character box beside non-primary production other business income, which marks the amount as a loss rather than income. The instruction for the label reads: "If you make a loss, print L in the box at the right of the amount at label J." Its counterpart beside the primary production label works the same way, so the two code columns carry the sign for the two amount columns.
value_definition: A single character, L where the label J amount is a loss and blank otherwise, with the amount column itself stored unsigned.
limitation: Ignoring it turns every loss into income of the same size, so a total built from the amount column alone is biased upwards. It carries no information about the kind of business or the source of the income.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a code accompanying non-primary production other business income, and the only code the ATO attaches to that label is the loss indicator described in the instruction.
evidence_quote: If you make a loss, print L in the box at the right of the amount at label J.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Other business income - non-primary production code' and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the code is a sign marker for the amount beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at P8 Income label I
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P8 Income
variable_description: Farm business income that none of the named payment labels picked up, reported at P8 Income label I. For a primary producer the amount is built from a separate worksheet: the instruction is to "add the amounts shown at PP1, PP2, PP6, PP7 and PP10 on your Gross income from primary production worksheet" and add any other primary production business income to that total. Livestock killed for rations and livestock exchanged for goods or services are counted at value here, so the label reaches beyond cash sales.
value_definition: Whole dollars of gross primary production business income, before expenses and able to be a loss, with the non-primary production equivalent at label J.
limitation: It cannot identify the farm activity behind the money, and it will not agree with farm cash receipts because non-cash items such as rations and barter are included at valuation. A person running a farm and a shop has both split across this label and label J by their own judgement.
rationale: The custodian's wording names other business income for primary production, which the ATO instruction places at P8 Income label I and builds from the primary production gross income worksheet.
evidence_quote: You show the total of all other income from the business of primary production at P8 Income - label I in your schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount comes off a separate primary production worksheet or that it includes non-cash items.

value_domain: Loss indicator beside P8 Income label I
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P8 Income
variable_description: The one-character box beside primary production other business income, marking that amount as a loss. The instruction is: "If you make a loss, print L in the box at the right of the amount at label I." Because primary producers can swing between a strong year and a loss year, this flag decides whether the farm income column on the same row adds to or subtracts from total business income.
value_definition: A single character, L where the label I amount is a loss and blank otherwise; the paired amount is stored without a sign.
limitation: It flags the sign of one label only, not the overall farm result, which also depends on the expense side of P8. A blank is not evidence of a profit: it is equally consistent with the label being unused.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a code accompanying primary production other business income, and the only code the ATO attaches to that label is the loss indicator in the instruction.
evidence_quote: If you make a loss, print L in the box at the right of the amount at label I.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Other business income - primary production code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the code carries the sign of the farm income amount.

value_domain: Dollar total of P8 Income labels I and J
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule 2025 instructions, P8 Income
variable_description: The combined other business income of a sole trader, taking the primary and non-primary production labels together. The instruction is to "Add up your 'other' primary production and non-primary production business income or loss and write the total in the adjacent Totals box", with an L printed beside it where the combined figure is a loss. It is the widest of the three other-income columns on the row and the one that feeds total business income.
value_definition: Whole dollars, the arithmetic sum of P8 Income labels I and J, and able to be a loss.
limitation: It nets a farm loss against shop income, so a person can show a modest total while running one profitable and one loss-making business. Using it alongside the two component columns in the same model counts the same dollars twice.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the total of other business income, which the ATO instruction defines as the Totals box beside P8 Income labels I and J.
evidence_quote: Add up your 'other' primary production and non-primary production business income or loss and write the total in the adjacent Totals box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other business income - total' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said it is a subtotal of the two columns beside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at D15 label E
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question D15 Other deductions
variable_description: What a candidate spent contesting an election, claimed as a deduction on their own tax return. The ATO says "Election expenses include a candidate's costs of contesting an election at a local, territory, state or federal level of government", and caps the local government version: "A deduction for local government election expenses can't exceed $1,000 for each election you contest, even if you incur the expenditure in more than one income year." It has its own label so that it is separated from the general other deductions total beside it.
value_definition: Whole dollars, self-assessed by the candidate, with local government claims capped at $1,000 per election and entertainment costs deductible only in narrow circumstances.
limitation: It counts candidates who lodged a claim, not everyone who stood for office, so it is a poor census of candidacy. A reimbursement of the expenses is taxed as income at the other income item rather than netted off here, so the column overstates what the candidate finally bore.
rationale: The custodian's wording names election expenses within other deductions, which the ATO instruction places at D15 label E and defines, including the local government cap.
evidence_quote: Election expenses include a candidate's costs of contesting an election at a local, territory, state or federal level of government.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other deduction election expenses' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said who can claim it or that a cap applies to local government elections.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at D15 label J
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question D15 Other deductions
variable_description: Deductions the taxpayer could not claim at any other question, totalled into one figure. The instruction is to "Add up all the other expenses that you're claiming at this question (excluding election expenses)" and write the result at D15 label J, so the election expenses column beside it is deliberately kept out. It is the catch-all of the deduction section, and debt deductions attributable to a rental property are among the items pushed into it.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a total of unlike residual deductions with no category attached, and separate from the election expenses total at label E on the same item.
limitation: The column names nothing, so it cannot support a claim about what people deduct. It also overlaps other parts of the return: rental debt deductions claimed here are added back in the net rental property loss worksheet, so the same dollars appear twice in one return.
rationale: The custodian's wording names other deductions within the other deductions question, which is the ATO's D15 label J, and the instruction states what the total covers and what it excludes.
evidence_quote: Add up all the other expenses that you're claiming at this question (excluding election expenses).
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Other deduction other deductions' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the total excludes election expenses or that it overlaps the rental income test.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 20 label T
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
variable_description: Net foreign employment income that arrived without an Australian payment summary behind it, which in practice means wages paid by a foreign employer. The instruction sets the boundary: "Add up all your gross foreign employment income amounts before any foreign tax is withheld. Don't include any exempt income or foreign employment income on an income statement or PAYG payment summary - foreign employment." Foreign employment income that did come with an Australian payment summary is reported at label U instead.
value_definition: Whole dollars, grossed up for foreign tax withheld and then reduced by deductible work expenses; it can be a loss, in which case an L is printed beside it.
limitation: It is not total foreign wages. Income covered by an Australian payment summary and exempt foreign employment income sit in different labels, so a person working overseas for an Australian employer can show nothing here. Debt deductions are also left out of the netting and claimed elsewhere.
rationale: The custodian's wording names other net foreign employment income within the foreign source income question, and the instruction defines the worksheet that fills item 20 label T and what it must exclude.
evidence_quote: Transfer the amount at worksheet 1 - row c to question 20 - label T. If you make a loss, print L in the Loss box at question 20 - label T.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing explained why 'other' foreign employment income is a separate label from the payment summary one.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 20 label M
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
variable_description: Foreign income left over once foreign employment, pensions, annuities and rent have been reported at their own labels, which is mostly foreign business and investment income. The instruction builds it from two worksheet rows: "Add up the amounts at row q and row t in Worksheet 1. Write this total at question 20 - label M. If the total is a loss, print L in the Loss box at question 20 - label M." Attributed income from foreign entities is folded in here as well.
value_definition: Whole dollars, net of deductible expenses incurred in earning the income but not of debt deductions, and able to be a loss.
limitation: It is a residual and so mixes interest, dividends, business profits and attributed amounts in one figure that cannot be split apart. Its 'net' is also incomplete: interest and borrowing costs are excluded from the netting and claimed at the other deductions question instead.
rationale: The custodian's wording names other net foreign source income, which the ATO instruction places at item 20 label M and builds from the foreign income worksheet.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts at row q and row t in Worksheet 1. Write this total at question 20 - label M.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the residual contains or that debt deductions sit outside it.

value_domain: Dollar amount of other refundable tax offsets applied at assessment
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T9 Other refundable tax offsets
variable_description: The refundable offsets that did not have a question of their own, as applied in the assessment. The ATO's residual refundable offset question covers a short list: "You can claim the following as other refundable tax offsets: tax the trustee of a special disability trust pays where you're the principal beneficiary; exploration credits." Being refundable matters for how the amount behaves: unlike the non-refundable offsets on the same row it is paid out even when it exceeds the tax owed.
value_definition: Whole dollars applied at assessment against tax payable and then refunded to the extent of any excess, drawn from the offsets grouped under the residual refundable offset question.
limitation: The list of offsets behind the label is rewritten as measures come and go, so the same column in two years can describe different entitlements. The code column beside it is the only thing that says which offset was claimed, and it collapses a mixed claim into a single letter.
rationale: The custodian's wording names other refundable tax offsets as used, and the ATO's T9 instruction lists exactly which offsets that residual question collects.
evidence_quote: You can claim the following as other refundable tax offsets: tax the trustee of a special disability trust pays where you're the principal beneficiary
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other refundable tax offsets - used' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what the residual covers or how a refundable offset differs from a non-refundable one.

value_domain: Dollar amount of non-primary production partnership income or loss
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: A partner's share of partnership income or loss from activities other than farming, on an early edition of the return. The successor label carries the same idea: "Write the total of your share of non-primary production partnership income or loss (excluding any attributed foreign income or other foreign source income) at question 13 - label O." The amount is a share of the partnership's net income for tax purposes, which is not the same thing as cash the partner drew out.
value_definition: Whole dollars, a share of net income or loss taken from the partnership's statement of distribution, and excluding attributed and other foreign source income, which are reported at the foreign income question.
limitation: It is not cash received and not a measure of a business's size. What sits inside the label has also moved: franked distributions and their credits were later brought into the partnership label while trusts got a separate franked distribution label, so early and late years do not cover the same income.
rationale: The custodian's wording names other partnership income on the 2000-01 return, which corresponds to the non-primary production partnership distribution label that the current instruction defines.
evidence_quote: Write the total of your share of non-primary production partnership income or loss (excluding any attributed foreign income or other foreign source income) at question 13 - label O.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Other Partnership Income Amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the figure is a share of taxable net income rather than a distribution.

value_domain: Code box beside the other refundable tax offsets label
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T9 Other refundable tax offsets
variable_description: A single letter saying which refundable offset made up the residual offset amount beside it. In the current edition of the return the ATO publishes three values: print "S in the Code box" for a special disability trust claim, "E in the Code box" for exploration credits, and "M in the Code box" where both are claimed. The code is the only thing on the return that identifies the offset, since the amount column is a single total.
value_definition: A single character from the code list published for the year of the return, with a value reserved for a mixed claim covering more than one offset type.
limitation: The list is reissued each year as offsets are created and repealed, so a letter cannot be read across years as the same entitlement, and the mixed-claim code hides the composition entirely. It also gives no amounts, so a mixed claim cannot be apportioned.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a code for other refundable tax offsets, and the ATO instruction publishes the code box values that accompany that label.
evidence_quote: only a tax offset as the principal beneficiary of a special disability trust under Part A, print S in the Code box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other refundable tax offsets code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, even though the ATO publishes a short code list for the box, and it never warned that the list changes between years.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 17 label R
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 17 Net farm management deposits or repayments
variable_description: Farm management deposits a primary producer withdrew in the ordinary way, after holding them for at least twelve months. The instruction is to "Add up the FMDs that you hold for 12 months or more and that are repaid during 2024-25. Write the total at label R." The withdrawal is income, not a transfer: "You must include repayments of previously deducted deposits as assessable income in the income year they are repaid."
value_definition: Whole dollars of deposits repaid during the year, which are added to the early repayment label and then reduced by the year's deductible deposits to give the net farm management deposit position.
limitation: It leaves out early withdrawals made under the natural disaster or drought exception, which have their own label, so it understates farm withdrawals in exactly the years when drawdowns spike. Deposits that were never claimed as a deduction are also outside it.
rationale: The custodian's wording names other repayments within the farm management deposit question, which the ATO instruction places at item 17 label R and defines by the twelve-month holding rule.
evidence_quote: Add up the FMDs that you hold for 12 months or more and that are repaid during 2024-25. Write the total at label R.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said the repayment is assessable income or that drought withdrawals are reported elsewhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount of other non-refundable tax offsets applied at assessment
value_source: ATO, About tax offsets
variable_description: How much of the residual non-refundable offset entitlement was actually applied against the taxpayer's tax. The ATO's rule for these offsets explains why used and available differ: "If you don't have any tax to pay, you don't receive any offset." Read against the available column on the same row, the gap between the two is the entitlement that expired unused.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount worked out at assessment for the offsets that have no question of their own, capped at the tax remaining after other offsets have been applied.
limitation: The order in which offsets are applied decides how much of this one is used, so the amount reflects the rest of the return as much as the entitlement itself. It cannot be compared across people with different offset mixes without also reading the available column.
rationale: The custodian's wording marks this as the used counterpart of the available other non-refundable offsets column, and the ATO's explanation of offsets gives the rule that caps a used amount at tax payable.
evidence_quote: If you don't have any tax to pay, you don't receive any offset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other non-refundable tax offsets - used' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished it from the available column sitting next to it.

value_domain: Dollar entitlement to other non-refundable tax offsets
value_source: ATO, About tax offsets
variable_description: The non-refundable offset entitlement a taxpayer had for offsets with no question of their own, before any of it was applied. The ATO describes what an offset does: "A tax offset (also sometimes known as a tax rebate) reduces the tax you pay on your taxable income (known as your tax payable)." Because the entitlement is not capped by tax payable, this column can be larger, sometimes much larger, than the used column on the same row.
value_definition: Whole dollars of entitlement, covering the offsets grouped as residual on the return rather than any single named concession.
limitation: It says nothing about the benefit received, since a non-refundable entitlement is worth nothing to a person with no tax to pay. It also gives no breakdown, so an entitlement worth several separate concessions arrives as one number.
rationale: The custodian's wording marks this as the available, rather than used, other non-refundable offset amount, and the ATO page defines what a tax offset is and why availability and benefit differ.
evidence_quote: A tax offset (also sometimes known as a tax rebate) reduces the tax you pay on your taxable income (known as your tax payable).
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Other non-refundable tax offsets - available' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said an available amount is an entitlement rather than a benefit.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator at item 20 label P
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property
variable_description: A yes or no answer to whether the taxpayer held overseas assets worth at least fifty thousand dollars at any time in the year. The ATO instruction is to "Print X in the Yes box at question 20 - label P if the value of your overseas assets is A$50,000 or more", valuing assets at "historical cost or market value, whichever is greater" and converting at the 30 June exchange rate. Interests held legally or beneficially, and directly or through interposed entities, all count.
value_definition: A two-value indicator, with the yes box marked once the combined value of overseas assets reaches the threshold at any point during the year.
limitation: It is a threshold flag and carries no value, so a person just over the line and a person with millions offshore look identical. A No is also not proof of nothing offshore: the instruction says the answer is No where the foreign entities question already covers all the assets held overseas.
rationale: The custodian's wording is the ATO's own question text for item 20 label P, and the instruction gives the threshold, the valuation basis and the interaction with the foreign entities question.
evidence_quote: Print X in the Yes box at question 20 - label P if the value of your overseas assets is A$50,000 or more.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long custodian question as its description and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the answer is a flag, how assets are valued, or when a No is consistent with holding assets abroad.

value_domain: Dollar franking credits reported at item 13 label Q
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Franking credits that reached the taxpayer through a partnership or trust rather than from shares they held directly. The instruction reads: "Write the amount of your share of any allowable franking credits which you're entitled to claim as a franking tax offset through a partnership or trust at question 13 - label Q. Show cents." The credits are only claimable where the matching franked income is also on the return, at label O for a partnership or label C for a trust.
value_definition: A dollars and cents amount, unusually for the return, being the person's share of the company tax already paid on distributions received through flow-through entities.
limitation: It is not the person's total imputation credits, since credits from directly held shares are reported at the dividends question. Entitlement can also fail even where the credit exists, because the holding period and related payments rules require the claimant and the entity to be qualified persons.
rationale: The custodian's wording names partnership and trust imputation credits, which the ATO instruction places at item 13 label Q and qualifies with the linked-income and qualified person rules.
evidence_quote: Write the amount of your share of any allowable franking credits which you're entitled to claim as a franking tax offset through a partnership or trust at question 13 - label Q. Show cents.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Partnership and Trust Imputation Credit Amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the credits are only the flow-through share or that the label reports cents.

value_domain: Dollar entitlement to the dependant tax offset for an invalid or carer
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T5 Invalid and invalid carer
variable_description: The offset a taxpayer was entitled to for maintaining an adult dependant who could not support themselves. The current question describes it as follows: "You can claim a tax offset for an income year if you maintain certain people who are 16 years old or older and who receive particular government payments." The column name preserves the older form of the concession, for a parent, a spouse's parent or an invalid relative, while the custodian's description uses the later consolidated dependant name, so one column spans both wordings.
value_definition: Whole dollars of entitlement, worked out from the dependant's own income and the period of maintenance, and claimable only once for each person maintained.
limitation: Entitlement is not receipt: the offset is non-refundable, so a carer with little tax to pay records an amount here and gets nothing from it. The column also identifies no dependant, so it cannot count how many people were being maintained.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the dependant invalid and carer tax offset as available, and the ATO's current question for that offset defines who can be maintained and on what basis.
evidence_quote: You can claim a tax offset for an income year if you maintain certain people who are 16 years old or older and who receive particular government payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing reconciled the column name with the description or said the amount is an entitlement rather than a benefit.

value_domain: Date, last day of the payment summary period
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B Payment details
variable_description: The last day of the span the payment summary covers, which the payer sets when reporting what it paid the person. The ATO asks the payer to "Show the period during which the payments were made to your worker or payee", and where employment ran all year the period is simply the financial year. It closes the period that the gross payment, tax withheld and allowance amounts on the same row belong to.
value_definition: A calendar date falling within or at the end of the financial year of the summary, reported by the payer in day, month and year form.
limitation: It is not a job end date. A payee who left mid-year and a payee still employed can both show 30 June, and the ATO tells payers they "do not need to show the first and last pay dates for the financial year in this field", so the date cannot be used to time a separation.
rationale: The table is a payment summary extract, and the ATO's instruction for completing the individual non-business payment summary defines the period field that the start and end dates come from.
evidence_quote: Show the period during which the payments were made to your worker or payee.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Period end date' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said whose period it is or warned that it does not mark the end of employment.

value_domain: Date, first day of the payment summary period
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B Payment details
variable_description: The first day of the span the payment summary covers for this payer and payee. The ATO's rule for casual work shows how loose the field is: a payee paid "over various times for the whole year" has the period shown as the whole financial year, and a payee employed for the entire year starts on 1 July. It anchors the earnings on the same row to a stretch of the financial year rather than to a pay run.
value_definition: A calendar date on or after the start of the financial year of the summary, reported by the payer in day, month and year form.
limitation: It cannot be read as the day a job started. Someone hired years earlier still shows 1 July, and a casual with scattered engagements is given the whole year, so job tenure built from this column will be wrong in both directions.
rationale: The table is a payment summary extract, and the ATO's completion instruction defines the period field and the conventions payers use for continuous and casual work.
evidence_quote: over various times for the whole year, show the period as the whole financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Period start date' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the date is a reporting convention rather than the start of a job.

value_domain: Dollar private health insurance offset claimed on the return
value_source: ATO, Claiming the private health insurance rebate
variable_description: The private health insurance rebate a person claimed through their tax return because they had not already taken it as cheaper premiums. The ATO describes the two routes: the rebate can be claimed "through your private health insurance provider (where it will be applied to reduce your private health insurance premiums)" or "when you lodge your tax return - as a refundable tax offset". Because it is refundable, the amount is paid out even where the person owes no tax.
value_definition: Whole dollars of refundable offset for premiums paid on an eligible policy during the year, covering only the part of the entitlement not already delivered as a premium reduction.
limitation: It measures a claiming channel, not a benefit. Most policyholders take the rebate as reduced premiums and never appear in this column, so it cannot be used to count people with private cover or to size the rebate they received.
rationale: The custodian's wording describes the refundable offset for rebate not previously taken as a premium reduction, and the ATO page defines the two claiming routes and the refundable character of the tax return route.
evidence_quote: when you lodge your tax return - as a refundable tax offset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the long custodian label and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the column captures only one of the two ways of getting the rebate.

value_domain: Count of dependent children recorded for private health insurance purposes
value_source: ATO, Income thresholds and rates for the private health insurance rebate
variable_description: How many dependent children the taxpayer reported in the private health insurance part of the return. The count does two jobs in the current system: it decides whether the single or family thresholds apply, since a single person with dependent children "is considered a family and will be income tested using the family income thresholds", and it lifts the family threshold, which "is increased by $1,500 for every Medicare levy surcharge dependent child after the first child". It is a count of children, not of people covered by a policy.
value_definition: A small non-negative integer, self-reported, counting dependent children as defined for the Medicare levy surcharge rather than for family assistance.
limitation: It cannot be read as the number of children on the health policy, which the ATO treats as a different concept, and in the earliest years of the column the rebate itself was not income tested, so the count then bore on surcharge thresholds rather than on the size of any rebate.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a private health insurance dependant children count, and the ATO's threshold page explains what a dependent child count does in the private health insurance rules; the page does not document the field on the 1999-2000 return itself.
evidence_quote: If you have 2 or more children, the family income threshold is increased by $1,500 for every Medicare levy surcharge dependent child after the first child.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the count is used for or how it differs from the people covered by a policy.

value_domain: Dollar private health insurance rebate calculated at assessment
value_source: ATO, Claiming the private health insurance rebate
variable_description: The rebate the ATO worked out for the person when it assessed the return, rather than an amount they claimed. The ATO explains: "If you haven't received your full private health insurance rebate entitlement, we calculate the rebate amount you are entitled to, which becomes payable to you as a refundable tax offset when we assess your tax return." The calculation runs against the income thresholds and against the person's share of the policy, so two adults on one policy can be assessed differently.
value_definition: Whole dollars of refundable offset determined at assessment from the person's income for surcharge purposes, their share of the premiums and the tax claim code they selected.
limitation: It only records rebate flowing to the taxpayer. Where too much was taken as a premium reduction the correction goes the other way and appears as an excess private health insurance liability, so this column alone cannot give the net position between a household and the rebate.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a calculated private health insurance rebate, and the ATO page states that the ATO calculates the entitlement at assessment and how the income test and policy share enter it.
evidence_quote: If you haven't received your full private health insurance rebate entitlement, we calculate the rebate amount you are entitled to, which becomes payable to you as a refundable tax offset when we assess your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Private health insurance rebate' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the figure is calculated by the ATO or that an over-claim is recorded as a liability elsewhere.

value_domain: Date a payment covered by the payment summary was made
value_source: ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Rules of reporting through STP
variable_description: The date attached to the payment behind the summary row, as distinct from the reporting period that the start and end date columns carry. Payroll reporting defines the date from the payer's side: "The pay day is either the payment date stipulated in the electronic transaction to your financial institution or, if you did not specify a date for payment, the date you intend to make the payment into your employee's bank account." It is most meaningful on rows for a single dated payment, such as a termination or lump sum, where a period would say little.
value_definition: A calendar date reported by the payer, falling in or near the financial year of the summary, and paired on the same row with the payment summary type that says what kind of payment it was.
limitation: The registry metadata does not say which payment summary types populate it, so a blank cannot be told apart from a type that never carries a payment date. It is also the payer's intended pay day rather than the day money reached the payee's account, so it can precede receipt.
rationale: The column sits in a payment summary table alongside the period dates and the payment summary type, and the payroll reporting rules define the payment date a payer supplies; no fetchable page documents this PLIDA field directly.
evidence_quote: The pay day is either the payment date stipulated in the electronic transaction to your financial institution or, if you did not specify a date for payment, the date you intend to make the payment into your employee's bank account.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Payment date' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing distinguished it from the period start and end dates on the same row.

value_domain: Dollar tax offset calculated for a government pension or allowance recipient
value_source: ATO, Beneficiary tax offset
variable_description: The offset the ATO worked out for someone receiving a government pension or allowance, so that the payment itself does not generate tax. Nothing is claimed on the form: "We will automatically calculate the tax offset when we process your tax return." Where a person qualifies under more than one of these concessions only one is granted, because "If you are eligible for both offsets, you will receive the one with the highest amount."
value_definition: Whole dollars, calculated from the taxable government payments received and the person's other income, and applied as a non-refundable offset in the assessment.
limitation: It cannot identify the payment behind it, since the pension and the allowance concessions resolve to a single amount and only the larger one survives. Being non-refundable it is also zero for a recipient with no other income, which is the majority of full-rate recipients.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a calculated rebate for pensioners and government allowance recipients, and the ATO page for that offset states that it is calculated automatically and that only the larger of the competing offsets is given.
evidence_quote: We will automatically calculate the tax offset when we process your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Pensioner rebate amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the amount is ATO-calculated or that it collapses two competing concessions into one figure.

value_domain: Tax offset code letter recording the claimant's circumstances
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
variable_description: A code letter recording the living and partnership circumstances that set the rate of the pensioner tax offset. The surviving version of this box, on the seniors and pensioners offset, uses five letters for circumstances such as "You're single, separated or widowed" and living apart because one partner is in a nursing home, with the letter chosen at the taxpayer's circumstances at any time in the year. On the earlier return the pensioner offset stood apart from the senior Australians offset and carried its own code list.
value_definition: A single letter identifying the claimant's circumstances for offset rate purposes, drawn from the code list printed in the instructions for the year of the return.
limitation: The code list for the earlier pensioner offset is not published on the current page, so a letter in this column must not be read against the modern list. It describes household circumstances for offset purposes only, and does not establish who a person lived with.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a pensioner tax offset code, and the current instruction documents the equivalent code box on the successor offset; the earlier code list itself was not found on a fetchable page.
evidence_quote: No, print your code letter from Step 1 in the TAX OFFSET CODE box at question T1 - label N.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Pensioner tax offset code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said what the code describes or warned that the list has been rewritten since.

value_domain: Veteran code letter accompanying the pensioner tax offset claim
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question T1 Seniors and pensioners tax offset
variable_description: A code saying whether the claimant, their spouse or both are a veteran, war widow or war widower, which matters because veterans reach the offset at a younger age. The ATO publishes three values: "V - you're a veteran, war widow or war widower", "W - your spouse is a veteran, war widow or war widower" and "X - both V and W apply to you and your spouse". It qualifies the pensioner offset claim on the same row rather than standing on its own.
value_definition: A single letter, present only where the claimant or their spouse has veteran, war widow or war widower status, and blank otherwise.
limitation: It cannot count veterans in the tax population, because it is recorded only where the person claimed the offset and met its other conditions. It also does not say which department pays the pension, so it is not a substitute for a veterans' affairs record.
rationale: The custodian's wording names a pensioner veteran code, and the ATO instruction for the surviving offset publishes the veteran code box and its three values.
evidence_quote: V - you're a veteran, war widow or war widower
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Pensioner veteran code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, even though the ATO publishes the three code values, and it never said the code is conditional on an offset claim.

value_domain: Dollar averaging adjustment for a primary producer
value_source: ATO, Income averaging for primary producers
variable_description: The result of evening out a primary producer's income across years, which is a tax offset in a good year and extra tax in a bad one. The ATO gives the formula: "The averaging adjustment is the averaging component (step 2) multiplied by the gross averaging amount (step 3) divided by the basic taxable income", and notes that "The amount of your averaging tax offset or extra income tax is calculated automatically." The first adjustment a farmer ever receives is always favourable: it "is always a tax offset (or nil)".
value_definition: Whole dollars produced at assessment, being the difference between tax at basic rates and tax at the comparison rate applied to the averaging component of basic taxable income.
limitation: The sign is what matters and the label does not carry it: the same column holds an offset in one year and complementary tax, which is a liability, in another. It also cannot be read as a measure of farm income volatility, because averaging draws on up to five years of income including non-farm income.
rationale: The custodian's wording names complementary tax and the averaging tax offset together, and the ATO's income averaging page defines the adjustment, its two directions and how it is calculated.
evidence_quote: The amount of your averaging tax offset or extra income tax is calculated automatically. Your notice of assessment will show you the averaging details.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Complementary tax / averaging tax offset' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that one column carries both a benefit and a liability.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 16 label I
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 16 Deferred non-commercial business losses
variable_description: Losses from farm and other primary production activities that the non-commercial loss rules would not let the taxpayer use this year. The instruction builds the label from the two business forms: "Add up any amounts of primary production deferred losses at question 16 - labels F and G.
