limitation: The four columns are a capped view. A person who changed policy several times in a year has rows on an attached schedule that these columns never capture, so summing the four understates their rebate and looks the same as a person with exactly four rows.
rationale: The ATO's private health insurance policy details instructions state the four-row limit on the return and the schedule of additional information used beyond it. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: If you have more than 4 rows of information on your statement, you will need to provide additional information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Your australian government rebate received 4' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that four is a hard limit with a spill-over schedule behind it.

value_domain: Dollar benchmark income used in the ATO's income averaging calculation
value_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
variable_description: The average income the ATO used to work out this taxpayer's averaging adjustment, the benchmark their basic taxable income is measured against. The ATO sets the test against average income: where it is "less than your basic taxable income - you will receive an averaging tax offset", and where it is more, the taxpayer pays extra income tax on the averaging component. It is a calculated figure that never appears on the return, and it sits beside the four earlier-year basic taxable income columns that feed it.
value_definition: A dollar amount derived by the ATO from basic taxable income over a window of up to five years. It is a rate-setting benchmark rather than income the person received in any year.
limitation: It does not tell you the direction or size of the averaging outcome. Whether an offset or extra tax resulted depends on the comparison rate and the averaging component, and the label leaves open whether the value is a primary production average income or the notional income used for special professionals.
rationale: The ATO's income averaging page defines average income, basic taxable income and the comparison that produces an offset or extra tax, which is the calculation this column belongs to. The column name allows a second reading as notional income, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: When your average income is: less than your basic taxable income - you will receive an averaging tax offset
supersedes_rationale: The entry echoed 'Average Income or Notional Income Amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so it did not say the figure is an ATO benchmark used to set a rate rather than income received.

value_domain: Dollar amount of other refundable tax offsets claimed in the supplement
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question T9 Other refundable tax offsets
variable_description: Refundable tax offsets available to the taxpayer from the residual offsets question in the supplement, before they are applied in the assessment. Two claims dominate it: exploration credits, and the special disability trust offset, where the ATO says "if the trustee of the special disability trust has lodged a tax return and paid tax on the net income of the trust, you are entitled to claim the amount of the tax paid by the trustee as a refundable tax offset". Refundable means the offset can produce a refund beyond the tax otherwise payable.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, one total covering every claim made at the question, with a separate code box beside it recording which offset or offsets it holds.
limitation: The amount alone does not say which offset it is; that lives in the code box. Available is not applied, so the figure is what the taxpayer claimed at the question rather than what the assessment ultimately allowed.
rationale: The ATO's T9 instructions define the two offsets in scope, the single total that is written for them and the code box that distinguishes them. Which item number and label letter carried the question in the earlier year of this table is not established, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: If the trustee of the special disability trust has lodged a tax return and paid tax on the net income of the trust, you are entitled to claim the amount of the tax paid by the trustee as a refundable tax offset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Other refundable tax offsets - available' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which offsets fall in the residual question or what refundable means for the taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar total of the primary and non-primary production bad debts columns at P8
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Bad debts
variable_description: Debts the business wrote off as bad during the year and claimed as an expense, primary and non-primary production added together. The ATO sets a threshold on the claim: "before you can claim a bad debt, it must be bad and not merely doubtful", and the debt must previously have been included in assessable income or be a loss from money lending. Accounting provisions for doubtful debts are excluded and are handled through the expense reconciliation instead.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, no cents, equal to the primary production and non-primary production bad debt columns of P8 added together. Partial write-offs and debt-for-equity swap losses are inside it.
limitation: It is not a measure of credit losses arising in the year. The deduction depends on the amount having been booked as income earlier, so a business on a cash basis records nothing here for the same commercial loss, and recoveries of past bad debts turn up as income at another label rather than reducing this one.
rationale: The schedule instructions define the deduction, its conditions, the exclusion of doubtful debt provisions and the two columns that are added to reach the total. The instructions were confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Before you can claim a bad debt, it must be bad and not merely doubtful.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Bad debts - total' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell that the total is the sum of two columns or that provisions are excluded.

value_domain: Dollar balance of the assessment, payable or refundable
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: The bottom line of the assessment: tax payable or refundable after levies, offsets and credits for tax already paid. The ATO describes the notice as showing "tax you owe on your taxable income", "credit you have for tax already paid during the income year" and "tax you need to pay or your refund", and this column is that last figure. It is calculated by the ATO from the lodged return, not written by the taxpayer.
value_definition: A dollar amount, the residual after income tax, the Medicare levy and any surcharge are reduced by offsets and by credits such as tax withheld and franking credits.
limitation: It is the assessment result, not the taxpayer's account position. The ATO issues a statement of account when the account balance differs from the assessment outcome, so penalties, general interest and refunds diverted to other debts sit outside this number.
rationale: The ATO's notice of assessment page lists what the notice contains and separates the assessment outcome from the account balance shown on a statement of account. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: We'll send you a statement of account with your NOA when your account balance is different to the outcome of your assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Tax payable or refundable' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not separate the assessment result from what the person actually owed on their account.

value_domain: Dollar balance payable or refundable, earliest table schema
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: The earliest schema's name for the closing figure of the assessment, the amount payable by or refundable to the taxpayer. It carries the same quantity as BAL_OF_THIS_ASMT_CALCD_AMT in the later withholding and debt tables, so a series spanning both has to be spliced across the two column names. Like its successor it is an ATO calculation, produced when the return is processed.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the early income years of the asset, being income tax and levies less offsets and credits for tax already paid.
limitation: The two schemas are not guaranteed to share a sign convention or the same set of levies and credits, so joining this column to its later twin needs a check at the join year rather than an assumption that the definitions match.
rationale: The ATO's notice of assessment page describes the figure an assessment closes with, which is what both this column and its later-schema twin hold. The page does not name the column, and the equivalence with the later column is inferred from the labels and table vintages, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Your notice of assessment (NOA) is the statement we issue that explains how your tax assessment is calculated.
supersedes_rationale: The entry echoed 'Balance Payable Or Refundable Amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence, so nothing flagged that this is the early-schema version of a column that continues under a different name.

value_domain: Opt-out choice code for backing business investment accelerated depreciation
value_source: ATO, Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation
variable_description: Whether the taxpayer chose to opt out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation for some of their eligible assets, or for all of them. The ATO says "you use your tax return to claim the deduction or to opt out of backing business investment for an asset". Backing business investment applied to the 2019-20 and 2020-21 income years only, and this column appears in a single table vintage.
value_definition: A single character choice code separating an opt-out for some eligible assets from an opt-out for all of them, blank where no opt-out choice was made. The company return instructions use A and B for that pair, but the characters used on the individual schedule are not confirmed. It qualifies the count and value of opted-out assets on the same row.
limitation: It records a choice, not a dollar effect: the deduction forgone by opting out is nowhere in these three columns. A blank cannot be read as opting in either, since small businesses using the simplified depreciation rules could not opt out at all.
rationale: The ATO's backing business investment page confirms the measure, its two income years and that the choice to opt out is made through the return. The A and B code meanings come from the return instructions rather than this page, and the individual schedule label letters are not established, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: You use your tax return to claim the deduction or to opt out of backing business investment for an asset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long question about opting out with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the field is a two-value choice code confined to two income years.

value_domain: Count of assets opted out of backing business investment
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions 2021, 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: How many eligible assets the taxpayer opted out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation for. The ATO's instruction for the matching field on the company return is to "show at W the number of assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation", and the choice is made asset by asset. The label letter on the individual schedule is not confirmed. The count pairs with the total cost of those assets in BBI_ELGBL_AST_OPT_OUT_VAL_AMT on the same row.
value_definition: A whole number of assets. It counts opted-out assets only, not the taxpayer's eligible assets or their depreciating asset holdings generally.
limitation: The count is explicitly forgiving. The ATO says a taxpayer "will not be penalised for specifying an incorrect amount" where a best attempt was made, so it is an estimate offered under a relaxed standard and should not be treated as an asset register.
rationale: The ATO's 2021 return instructions define the number-of-assets field and state the tolerance that applies to it. The instructions are written for the company return, and the equivalent individual schedule label is not established here, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Show at W the number of assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Backing business investment - Number of assets you are opting out for' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the count is a tolerated estimate rather than a verified figure.

value_domain: Dollar cost of assets opted out of backing business investment
value_source: ATO, Company tax return instructions 2021, 9 Capital allowances
variable_description: The total cost of the assets the taxpayer opted out of backing business investment accelerated depreciation for. The ATO's instruction for the matching field on the company return is to "show at X the total cost of the assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation", so it is cost rather than written-down value; the label letter on the individual schedule is not confirmed. It sits beside the count of those assets and the some-or-all choice code.
value_definition: A dollar amount, the summed cost of the opted-out assets in the year the choice was made. Opting out returns those assets to the ordinary decline in value rules.
limitation: Cost is not the deduction given up. The tax effect of opting out depends on each asset's effective life and depreciation method, so this amount cannot be converted into forgone deductions or into a revenue estimate.
rationale: The ATO's 2021 return instructions define the value-of-assets field as total cost and place it alongside the count and the choice code. The instructions are written for the company return, and the equivalent individual schedule label is not established here, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Show at X the total cost of the assets for which you are opting out of Backing business investment - accelerated depreciation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Backing business investment - Value of assets you are opting out for' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is cost rather than value or deduction.

value_domain: De-identified business identifier shared with BLADE
value_source: ABS, Business Longitudinal Analysis Data Environment (BLADE)
variable_description: The de-identified business identifier for the paying entity on this payment summary row, the same key that identifies a business across BLADE. It stands for the employer or payer, not for the individual, so it is the join that lets a person's pay be attached to firm characteristics. The ABS describes BLADE as "an economic data tool combining tax, trade and intellectual property data with information from ABS surveys", and this column is the key those business tables are built on.
value_definition: An opaque numeric identifier standing for one registered business, stable within the asset and shared with the business data environment. It carries no name, address or industry of its own.
limitation: A business identifier is not a firm over time and not a workplace. A restructure retires one identifier and starts another with no link between them, and a large employer that pays through several entities will look like several employers, so job spells and employer counts built on this key alone will break.
rationale: The ABS page describes BLADE and the business data it assembles, which supports the reading that this key is the business identifier the two assets share. The ABS page does not itself state that the key is a de-identified Australian Business Number, so the status stays guessed and the reading of the column as the payer rather than the payee comes from the other columns in the same table.
evidence_quote: an economic data tool combining tax, trade and intellectual property data with information from ABS surveys to provide a better understanding of the Australian economy and businesses performance over time
supersedes_rationale: The entry had no description at all beyond the column name and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said whether the identifier belongs to the person or to the business paying them.

value_domain: Broad industry grouping derived from the register's ANZSIC code
value_source: ABS, Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC)
variable_description: A coarse industry grouping worked out from the register's detailed industry code on the same row, not a separate answer by the taxpayer. The custodian's own wording says it is based on the ABR ANZSIC code, so it adds no information beyond that code and is a convenience for grouping. The finer code sits in ANZSIC_CD_ABR beside it.
value_definition: A short code or label naming a broad industry group. The grouping rule that turns the five-digit register code into this value is not published in the data item list.
limitation: Because the grouping rule is unpublished, it cannot be assumed to equal an ANZSIC division, and two rows in the same broad group may sit in different divisions. Any cross-walk to published ABS industry statistics has to be built and checked, not taken for granted.
rationale: The ABS classification page establishes what ANZSIC is and that it is the classification the underlying code belongs to. Neither the ABS nor the ATO publishes the specific broad grouping used for this derived column, so the status is guessed and the confidence is low.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Broad industry base on abr_anzsic_cd' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the column is derived from its neighbour and adds no independent information.

value_domain: Dollar amount of Medicare levy calculated on the assessment
value_source: ATO, What is the Medicare levy?
variable_description: The Medicare levy the ATO calculated on this assessment, before any surcharge. The ATO states that "the Medicare levy is 2% of your taxable income" and that "we calculate your Medicare levy when you lodge your tax return", so it is an ATO figure rather than a taxpayer entry. The taxpayer's part is the reduction or exemption claim at question M1, which lowers the amount in this column.
value_definition: A dollar amount, two per cent of taxable income, reduced where family income puts the taxpayer in the reduction range and nil where a full exemption applies.
limitation: A zero is not a low income signal. A full exemption for a foreign resident, a person with no Medicare entitlement or certain veterans also gives zero, and the Medicare levy surcharge is a separate liability that is not inside this amount.
rationale: The ATO's Medicare levy page gives the rate, the base and states that the ATO calculates the levy at lodgement, and separates the levy from the surcharge. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: The Medicare levy is 2% of your taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Medicare levy' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is calculated by the ATO or that a zero can mean exemption rather than low income.

value_domain: Dollar basic taxable income for the year before the current one
value_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
variable_description: The taxpayer's basic taxable income for the year immediately before this one, carried into the income averaging calculation. The ATO says "Your basic taxable income is your taxable income excluding: net capital gains", along with certain superannuation lump sums and death benefit termination payments, above-average income of a special professional, and deductions excluded under the non-commercial loss provisions. This is the year the entry test looks at, because averaging does not start until basic taxable income is at least as high as the year before.
value_definition: A dollar amount computed by the ATO for the prior income year on the averaging definition, not on the ordinary taxable income definition.
limitation: It will not match the taxable income assessed for that earlier year. Capital gains, certain lump sums and non-commercial loss deductions are stripped out, so joining it to the earlier year's taxable income column will show differences that are definitional rather than errors.
rationale: The ATO's income averaging page defines basic taxable income and the multi-year window the calculation uses, which is what the four averaging-year columns hold. The mapping of the column suffix to a specific offset year is read off the custodian's label and is not published, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.
evidence_quote: Your basic taxable income is your taxable income excluding: net capital gains, certain superannuation lump sums and death benefit termination payments, above-average income of a special professional, deductions that are excluded under the non-commercial loss provisions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Averaging income - 1st year amount (calculated)' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say which year is meant or that the figure is basic rather than ordinary taxable income.

value_domain: Dollar basic taxable income for two years before the current one
value_source: ATO, Income averaging (primary producers, managing varying income)
variable_description: Basic taxable income for the second year back, the middle of the five-year window income averaging looks over. The ATO describes the purpose plainly: "Income averaging evens out your income and tax payable over a maximum of 5 years to allow for fluctuations." This figure is restated on the averaging definition rather than lifted from what that year's return reported.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year two before the current one, computed by the ATO on the basic taxable income definition used for averaging.
limitation: It does not carry the primary production and non-primary production split, so the averaging component for that year cannot be rebuilt from this column alone and neither can eligibility be checked from it.
rationale: The ATO's income averaging page sets out the five-year window and the definition of the income used in it, which is what these four earlier-year columns supply. The mapping of the suffix to an offset year is read off the custodian's label rather than published, so the confidence stays medium. The page was confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.

value_domain: Count of business activities reported at P3 label B
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P3 Number of business activities

value_domain: Dollar total of the project pool deduction at P8 Reconciliation items
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Business deduction for project pool
variable_description: The year's deduction for capital spending pooled against a business project, primary and non-primary production combined. The ATO explains that "certain capital expenditure you incur after 30 June 2001 which is directly connected with a project you carry on or propose to carry on for a taxable purpose can be allocated to a project pool and written off over the life of the project". Typical project amounts are feasibility studies, site preparation, environmental assessments and community infrastructure.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, a reconciliation item rather than an accounting expense. It is the pool value spread over the estimated project life at 150 per cent, or 200 per cent for pools of amounts incurred from 10 May 2006 for projects starting from that date.

rationale: The schedule instructions define project amounts, the pooling rule, the write-off rates and the primary and non-primary production columns that are added to reach the total. The instructions were confirmed live by a direct HTTPS request; ato.gov.au returns 403 to some automated fetchers.

value_domain: Dollar total business income, primary and non-primary production combined
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Total business income

value_domain: Dollar net loss for the first business loss activity at P9
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P9 Business loss activity details

value_domain: Non-commercial loss type code for the first loss activity
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P9 Type of loss

The codes run 1 to 8, and the last is the deferral outcome: "the above loss codes don't apply. You must defer your loss and complete question 16 in your supplementary tax return." A reported passive investment loss is coded 0 instead.
value_definition: A single digit. Code 1 is assessable income of at least $20,000, code 2 profit in three of the past five years, code 3 real property of at least $500,000, code 4 other assets of at least $100,000, code 5 the Commissioner's discretion or the flood, bushfire and COVID safe harbour, code 6 a professional arts business, code 7 a primary production business with other income under $40,000, and code 8 none of these.

value_domain: Dollar net loss for the second business loss activity at P9

A passive partnership investment loss is coded 67110 by instruction, so that value is a reporting convention rather than a real industry.

Activity 3 exists only where the person reported three separate loss activities, so the column is populated far less often than the activity 1 industry code.

This column is therefore the rarest of the three and marks people with a diversified set of loss-making ventures.

value_domain: Derived dollar amount, estimated net tax attributable to business income
value_source: ATO, Taxation statistics 2014-15, Definitions and calculations
variable_description: The share of a person's net tax that the ATO attributes to their business income, worked out by the ATO rather than written on the return. The ATO defines it as "an estimate of the amount of net tax attributable to net business income" and calculates it as net income or loss from business divided by taxable income, capped at one, multiplied by net tax. It sits beside NET_TAX_AMT and GRS_TAX_AMT in the same withholding and debt table, which are the totals it is carved out of.
value_definition: A dollar amount derived by pro-rating net tax by the proportion of taxable income that comes from net business income at items 15B and 15C, with the proportion set to one where it would exceed one.
limitation: It is an apportionment, not a tax actually assessed on business income, so it cannot be used to say what a person paid on their business. The ATO notes that net tax itself "does not generally equate to the amount of tax payable or refundable as shown on a notice of assessment", and the field is only calculated for taxable individuals with net business income, so a zero can mean either no business or no tax.
rationale: The ATO's taxation statistics definitions page publishes the exact formula and scope of business net tax, and the column sits with the other calculated assessment amounts in the PLIDA withholding and debt table.
evidence_quote: For taxation statistics purposes, business net tax is an estimate of the amount of net tax attributable to net business income. Business net tax is only calculated for taxable individuals with net business income and taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only 'Business net tax' from the custodian with the generic no-value-list sentence repeated, so a reader could not tell that the number is derived by apportionment rather than assessed.

value_domain: ATO business market segment classification
value_source: ATO, Latest estimate and trends for the medium business income tax gap
variable_description: The ATO's own size classification of the business attached to the return, assigned administratively rather than answered by the taxpayer. The ATO's published segments are bounded by group turnover: it defines the medium business population as "companies with a group turnover between $10 million and $250 million", with small business below that band and large business above it. The ATO does not publish the code list used on the individual return, so the categories carried in this column are not documented.
value_definition: A short classification code or label for the ATO market segment. The boundaries are turnover based, but the exact set of values used in this table is not published by the ATO.
limitation: It cannot be treated as a stable size band across years, because segment definitions and thresholds have moved with ATO compliance programmes, and the segment attaches to the ATO's view of the client group rather than to the single business activity reported on this return.
rationale: The ATO publishes the turnover boundaries that separate its business market segments but does not publish a data item list or code frame for the market segment field carried on individual income tax return records, so the mapping is inferred.
evidence_quote: We define the medium business population as: companies with a group turnover between $10 million and $250 million
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Business market segment' from the custodian and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the definition and the limitation, so nothing said the field is an ATO administrative classification with turnover-based boundaries.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P9 label H, activity 1
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P9 Business loss activity details
variable_description: An earlier year's loss on the person's largest loss-making activity that the non-commercial loss rules blocked, now brought forward. The ATO says to "Write the amount of your deferred non-commercial business loss from a prior year for the business activity at P9 – label H". It is quarantined to the same or a similar activity, so it is not a general tax loss and it cannot be set against unrelated wage income.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, no cents, for one business activity only. It can be reduced by net exempt income earned in the current year and is extinguished by bankruptcy or a release from debt.
limitation: The amount is not necessarily deducted this year. It is only usable against income from the same or a similar activity, and if the activity is still in loss the deferred amount is simply carried on again, so a non-zero value is not evidence of a tax benefit received.
rationale: The DIL label names the prior-year deferred non-commercial loss for activity 1, which the ATO defines at P9 label H, including the exempt income and bankruptcy reductions.
evidence_quote: Write the amount of your deferred non-commercial business loss from a prior year for the business activity at P9 – label H in your schedule. Don't show cents. Your prior year deferred non-commercial business loss for a business activity may be reduced if you earned net exempt income in 2024–25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording for activity 1 with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing explained that the loss is quarantined to a similar activity or that it can be reduced by exempt income.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P9 label N, activity 2
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P9 Business loss activity details
variable_description: The earlier-year deferred non-commercial loss brought forward on the person's second-largest loss-making activity, entered on the second activity block at P9. The ATO worked example shows the second block using its own label letters: "Kieren shows the $3,000 deferred non-commercial business loss from 2023–24 at P9 – label N , and the overall net loss of $7,990 at P9 – label O". A value here therefore means the person had at least two separate business activities in loss and a history in this one.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for the second activity block, reduced by any net exempt income and lost on bankruptcy, in the same way as the activity 1 amount.
limitation: It cannot be added to the activity 1 amount to get a person's total deferred losses, because activities beyond the third are never itemised on the schedule; only question 16 in the supplementary return carries the primary production and non-primary production totals.
rationale: The DIL label names the prior-year deferred non-commercial loss for activity 2, and the ATO's worked example on the P9 page identifies the second activity block's labels and confirms the same rules apply.
evidence_quote: Kieren shows the $3,000 deferred non-commercial business loss from 2023–24 at P9 – label N , and the overall net loss of $7,990 at P9 – label O in his Business and professional items schedule for individuals 2025 .
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the custodian's phrase for activity 2 with the generic no-value-list sentence as both fields, so it read as an unexplained duplicate of the activity 1 and activity 3 columns.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P9, activity 3
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P9 Business loss activity details
variable_description: The earlier-year deferred non-commercial loss brought forward on the person's third-largest loss-making activity, the last block the schedule provides. The ATO says a deferred loss is "a deduction when calculating any net profit or loss from the activity in that future income year", so this is a running balance attached to one venture rather than a claim made this year. Rows with a value here belong to people carrying losses in three different activities at once.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for the third activity block, subject to the same reductions for net exempt income and bankruptcy as the other two blocks.
limitation: It is not a deduction claimed. Whether any of it is used depends on the activity's result in the year and on the non-commercial loss rules applying again, so the column records an entitlement carried forward rather than tax relief received.
rationale: The DIL label names the prior-year deferred non-commercial loss for activity 3, which is the third block of P9, and the ATO explains how a deferred loss is taken into account in a later year.
evidence_quote: The deferred loss is a deduction when calculating any net profit or loss from the activity in that future income year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording for activity 3 with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so it said nothing about how a deferred loss is later used.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, capital gains tax event during the year
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 18 Capital gains
variable_description: Whether a capital gains tax event happened to the person during the year, as asked on the earliest version of the return. The ATO instruction is to print X in the Yes box "if you have a capital gain or a capital loss that isn't deferred" and in the No box "if you don't have a capital gain or your capital gains and losses are deferred", so the flag turns on for losses as well as gains. The later table version carries the same question as CGT_EVNT_IND.
value_definition: A two-state indicator for the tick box at the head of the capital gains question. It is answered by the taxpayer, not derived from the amounts reported below it.
limitation: A yes does not mean tax was paid and a no does not mean nothing was sold: rollovers and other deferrals are answered no, the main residence exemption keeps most home sales out, and small gains reduced to zero by losses still answer yes. It is also not comparable in coverage with the later CGT_EVNT_IND column, which belongs to a different form version.
rationale: The ATO instructions for the capital gains question define the yes and no conditions for the CGT event tick box, which is the question this early-version indicator records; the label letter on the older form is not confirmed.
evidence_quote: Yes – Print X in the Yes box at question 18 – label G if you have a capital gain or a capital loss that isn't deferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's 'Capital gain tax event indicator' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said the flag also turns on for capital losses or that deferred events answer no.

value_domain: Derived dollar amount, carry-forward tax offsets applied in the year
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T6 Landcare and water facility
variable_description: The amount of tax offset carried in from earlier years that the assessment actually absorbed this year. It sits with NON_RFNDBL_OFST_USED_AMT and OTHR_OFSTS_USED_AMT in the same deduction and offset table, which are the other calculated offset-applied fields. For individuals the carry-forward offsets are the landcare and water facility offset, for which the ATO says "There is no limit on the number of years you can carry forward any balance", along with the more recent early stage investor and early stage venture capital partnership offsets.
value_definition: A dollar amount worked out during assessment rather than written on the return, being the part of the brought-forward offset balance that this year's tax liability could absorb.
limitation: It is not the balance available: the unused remainder is carried on again and is reported separately, so this column understates a person's offset entitlement. The ATO does not publish a data item for this field, so which offsets are counted in it cannot be confirmed from the return instructions.
rationale: The neighbouring columns in the same table are calculated offset-applied amounts, and the ATO documents the landcare and water facility offset as the individual return's long-standing carry-forward offset, but no ATO page names this particular field.
evidence_quote: There is no limit on the number of years you can carry forward any balance of landcare and water facility tax offset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Carry forward offsets used' from the custodian with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never distinguished the amount used from the balance available.

value_domain: Business status code at P4, ceased or commenced
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P4 Status of business
variable_description: Whether the person shut their main business or started a new one during the year, ticked at P4 of the business and professional items schedule. The ATO says "If you cease your main business during 2024–25, print X at P4 – label C1" and "If you commence a new business during 2024–25, print X at P4 – label C2", and that where both happened only the ceased box is ticked. A blank means the business continued through the whole year.
value_definition: A two-state tick, C1 for a main business ceased and C2 for a new business commenced, with a blank for neither. Where both events occur in the one year the ATO directs that only C1 be used.
limitation: It gives no date, so it cannot be used to time an entry or exit within the year, and because it applies to the main business only, a person who closed a secondary venture shows nothing. The instruction to prefer C1 when both apply also means business starts are undercounted among people who churned businesses in the same year.
rationale: The DIL label 'Status of your business' matches P4 of the business and professional items schedule, where the ATO defines the two tick boxes and the precedence rule.
evidence_quote: If more than one option applies, only print X at P4 – label C1 . If neither option applies, leave both boxes blank.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Status of your business' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the domain is the two ticks or that ceasing takes precedence over commencing.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question 19 label K
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 19 Foreign entities
variable_description: Income of a foreign company the person controls that Australia taxes in their hands even though the company did not pay it out. The ATO says the rules "may apply to income and gains of foreign companies in which you have a direct or indirect controlling interest, or which you effectively control", and directs the taxpayer to "Work out your attributed foreign income from any CFC" and write it at question 19 label K. It is attributed income, not a dividend received, and it sits beside the transferor trust amount at label B.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of attributed foreign income, worked out by the taxpayer under the controlled foreign company rules in the foreign income return form guide, with no cents shown.
limitation: It is not the foreign company's profit and not cash the person received, so it cannot measure offshore income flows; it is the slice the attribution rules assign. The threshold test at label I also means small holdings are excluded entirely, so the column captures controlling interests rather than all foreign company ownership.
rationale: The DIL label names controlled foreign company income at the foreign entities question, and the ATO instructions set out exactly what is worked out and written at question 19 label K.
evidence_quote: Step 2 Work out your attributed foreign income from any CFC. Step 3 Write this amount at question 19 – label K . Don't show cents.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Foreign entities controlled foreign company income' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said the amount is attributed rather than received.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator at question 19 label I
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 19 Foreign entities
variable_description: Whether the person held a direct or indirect interest in a controlled foreign company, ticked yes or no at question 19 label I. The ATO reserves the yes box for control: the taxpayer answers yes only if they, alone or with associates, have "direct or indirect controlling interests totalling 10% or more in a foreign company" or "effective control of a foreign company". A yes here is what unlocks the attributed income amount at label K on the same row.
value_definition: A two-state tick box answered by the taxpayer. The transferor trust question is a separate tick at label W and is not part of this indicator.
limitation: It is not a general measure of foreign share ownership, because holdings below the 10 per cent control test answer no. A yes can also stand with a nil amount at label K, since control does not by itself produce attributable income in a given year.
rationale: The DIL question text matches question 19 label I word for word, and the ATO instructions state the control tests that decide the answer.
evidence_quote: Do you, alone or with associates either have: direct or indirect controlling interests totalling 10% or more in a foreign company effective control of a foreign company?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's question text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said that the yes box requires a 10 per cent controlling interest or effective control.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question 18 label H
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 18 Capital gains
variable_description: All the capital gains a person made in the year added together, before any losses or the capital gains tax discount are applied. The ATO worked example calls it "the amount before deducting any capital losses or applying the CGT discount", and the same label also picks up grossed-up net capital gains distributed through trusts. The reduced figure that reaches taxable income is the net capital gain at label A on the same row.
value_definition: A gross dollar total of current year capital gains from all CGT events, including collectables gains and grossed-up trust distributions, and excluding disregarded gains such as those on a main residence.
limitation: It is not income and it is not comparable with the net capital gain beside it, because the discount, current year losses, earlier year losses and the small business concessions all sit between the two. Losses from collectables and personal use assets are also handled apart from this total, so it cannot be netted by simple subtraction.
rationale: The DIL label names total current year capital gains at the capital gains question, and the ATO instructions define what is added into label H and where it sits in the calculation sequence.
evidence_quote: Firstly, Kathleen writes her total current year capital gains of $3,520 ($3,000 + $520) from her shares at label H Total current year capital gains. This is the amount before deducting any capital losses or applying the CGT discount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Capital gains total current year capital gains' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so a reader could not tell it was gross of losses and of the discount.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question 18 label A
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 18 Capital gains
variable_description: The capital gain that is actually added to the person's assessable income, after losses and the capital gains tax discount have been taken off. The ATO says it "represents the amount you have written at label H Total current year capital gains reduced in accordance with" the concessions that follow, and that where losses reduce gains to zero the taxpayer should "don't put anything at label A Net capital gain". This is the capital gains figure that flows into taxable income.
value_definition: A net dollar amount after current year capital losses, unapplied net capital losses from earlier years, the CGT discount and any small business concessions have been applied in the order the taxpayer chose.
limitation: A blank or zero does not mean no assets were sold: it is the normal result when losses cancel the gains, and it is also what a person with a net capital loss reports, since the loss itself is recorded at label V rather than as a negative here.
rationale: The DIL label names the net capital gain at the capital gains question, and the ATO instructions define label A as the reduced amount and say to leave it blank when gains are reduced to zero.
evidence_quote: The amount of your remaining capital gains becomes your net capital gain, which you write at question 18 – label A Net capital gain in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's 'Capital gains net capital gain' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice over, so it never separated this from the gross total at label H.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator at question 18 label G
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 18 Capital gains
variable_description: The taxpayer's yes or no answer to whether a capital gains tax event happened during the year, on the current form version of the return context table. The ATO lists the common events as selling real estate, shares, units, forestry scheme interests, crypto assets, collectables and personal use assets, and adds events such as an asset being "lost or destroyed" or the person ceasing to be an Australian resident. The gate is wide: the same tick covers gains and losses alike.
value_definition: A two-state tick box at the head of the capital gains question, answered no where the person had no gain or where their gains and losses are deferred.
limitation: It records that something happened, not that anything was taxed, and it cannot be used as a proxy for asset sales: exempt disposals such as the family home are outside it, while events with no sale at all, such as ceasing residency or an asset being destroyed, are inside it.
rationale: The DIL question text matches the ATO's capital gains tick box, and the instructions define both the yes and no conditions and the range of events that count.
evidence_quote: No – Print X in the No box at question 18 – label G if you don't have a capital gain or your capital gains and losses are deferred.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's question text with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing explained which events count or that deferred events answer no.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, forestry scheme interest held as a subsequent participant
value_source: ATO, Guide to capital gains tax 2022, Forestry managed investment scheme interests
variable_description: Whether the person's capital gains tax event was on a forestry scheme interest they had bought from someone else rather than taken up at the outset. The ATO puts it plainly: "You are a subsequent participant if you are not an initial participant. In most cases, this means that you bought your forestry interest from an initial participant." The distinction changes the tax treatment, because a subsequent participant cannot deduct the cost of acquiring the interest and must carry it in the cost base instead.
value_definition: A two-state tick answered as part of the capital gains question, marking that a CGT event related to a forestry managed investment scheme interest held other than as an initial participant.
limitation: It says nothing about the size of the interest or the gain, and a no answer covers two very different people: someone with no forestry interest at all, and an initial participant, whose forestry deductions run through question 23 and the forestry deduction item instead.
rationale: The DIL question text asks whether the CGT event related to a forestry managed investment scheme interest held other than as an initial participant, and the ATO capital gains guide defines the initial and subsequent participant categories and their different treatment.
evidence_quote: You are a subsequent participant if you are not an initial participant. In most cases, this means that you bought your forestry interest from an initial participant.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's long question text with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never explained what an initial participant is or why the distinction matters.

value_domain: Dollar amount, dependant's separate net income
value_source: ATO Legal database, Explanatory Memorandum, Tax Laws Amendment (2009 Measures No. 1) Act 2009, chapter 16
variable_description: The income of the taxpayer's own child who kept house for them, used to scale the now-abolished child-housekeeper tax offset. A child-housekeeper "is any child of the taxpayer who was wholly engaged in keeping house for the taxpayer during the income year", and separate net income is "broadly defined as gross income that the dependant earned or received while being maintained by the taxpayer less expenses" directly charged against it. The offset fell by "$1 for every $4" once that income passed $282, so the amount here is a means test input, not the taxpayer's own income.
value_definition: A dollar amount of another person's income, reported by the taxpayer. Separate net income is wider than taxable income because it takes in some exempt payments, which the explanatory memorandum illustrates with disability support pensions.
limitation: It is a second-hand figure about a household member, so it cannot be joined to that child's own tax record and is only as accurate as the parent's knowledge. It also only exists for the years the dependency offsets ran on separate net income, before adjusted taxable income replaced that test, so a break in the series is a form change and not a change in behaviour.
rationale: The ATO's copy of the explanatory memorandum defines both the child-housekeeper dependant category and separate net income, including the threshold and taper, which is what this reported amount feeds.
evidence_quote: 'Separate net income' is broadly defined as gross income that the dependant earned or received while being maintained by the taxpayer less expenses that are regarded, according to ordinary accountancy and commercial principles, as a direct charge against that income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Child-housekeeper's separate net income' from the custodian with the generic no-value-list sentence as both the definition and the limitation, so nothing said whose income it is or what it was used for.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question 18 label V
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 18 Capital gains
variable_description: Capital losses the person still has left after this year's gains have been reduced to zero, carried on to use against future gains. The ATO says "There is no time limit on how long you can carry forward your net capital loss" and that the balance is written at question 18 label V. Reading it across years gives a running stock of unused losses, since next year's return starts from "the amount at label V at the capital gains question in your last year's tax return".
value_definition: A dollar balance of unapplied net capital losses at year end, including losses from collectables, which can only ever be used against later collectables gains.
limitation: It is a stock rather than a flow, so year-on-year differences mix new losses made with old losses used, and a rise cannot be read as this year's loss. It also mixes ordinary and collectables losses in one number even though they are not interchangeable.
rationale: The DIL label names net capital losses carried forward at the capital gains question, and the ATO instructions define label V and its link to the following year's return.
evidence_quote: You need to keep a record of any unapplied net capital losses from earlier years. You can continue to carry forward these amounts and use them to reduce your future capital gains. There is no time limit on how long you can carry forward your net capital losses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated 'Capital gains net capital losses carried forward' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said it is a closing balance carried between returns.

value_domain: Private health insurance tax claim code, first policy row
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
variable_description: The claim code on the first private health insurance policy line, which tells the ATO whose share of the rebate is being claimed. The codes are A for a single person with no dependants, B for a single person with a dependent person, C where you are claiming your share of the rebate as a member of a couple, D for the matching row from a spouse's statement, E where the spouse is claiming your share, and F where you are covered as a dependent person. The code drives the rebate and the family threshold, so it is a household relationship marker as much as an insurance field.
value_definition: A single letter from A, B, C, D, E and F, entered on the first of up to four policy rows. It pairs with HLTH_FND_CD_1 on the same row, which identifies the insurer.
limitation: It describes the claim, not the cover, so it cannot be used to count insured people; a person with no policy of their own can still show code F, and one policy covering a couple generates a C row and a matching D row on the one return.
rationale: The ATO's private health insurance policy details instructions define each tax claim code and the rule that a code is printed in the claim code box for each policy row transferred from the statement.
evidence_quote: Print the code in the Tax claim code box in your tax return. If you have more than one row of information to transfer from your statement to your tax return that relate to the same membership number, print the same code in the Tax claim code box in each row.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Private health insurance tax claim code 1' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed as both fields, so the six codes and their meanings were nowhere on the page.

value_domain: Private health insurance tax claim code, second policy row
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
variable_description: The claim code on the second private health insurance policy line, which is present when the person's statement runs to more than one row. A second row arises when someone changed insurer or policy during the year, or when a couple's rebate is split across a claim row and the partner's matching row. The ATO requires the same code on every row that shares a membership number, so a change of code between row one and row two normally signals a different policy rather than a change of circumstances.
value_definition: A single letter from A, B, C, D, E and F on the second policy row, paired with HLTH_FND_CD_2 which names the insurer for that row.
limitation: A populated second row is not evidence of double cover: it just as often records the same person's continuous cover across two funds or two benefit codes in the one year. Counting non-blank claim code columns therefore overstates the number of policies held.
rationale: The ATO instructions define the tax claim codes and the row-by-row transfer from the private health insurance statement, which is what generates a second policy row.
evidence_quote: You must provide information about your spouse's private health insurance in the Private health insurance policy details in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Private health insurance tax claim code 2' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave a reader no way to tell it apart from the other three claim code columns.

value_domain: Private health insurance tax claim code, third policy row
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
variable_description: The claim code on the third private health insurance policy line, which only appears for people with unusually fragmented cover. Third rows are typical of a mid-year change of fund on top of a spouse's matching row, since the ATO requires that "the number of rows with Tax claim code D must equal the number of rows with Tax claim code C for the same health insurer ID and membership number". Most returns leave this column blank.
value_definition: A single letter from A, B, C, D, E and F on the third policy row, with HLTH_FND_CD_3 giving the insurer for the same row.
limitation: Its sparseness makes it a poor basis for any rate: a blank is the norm and carries no information about cover, so this column can only be read together with rows one and two rather than on its own.
rationale: The ATO instructions define the claim codes and the pairing rule that produces multiple rows for the same membership number, which is what fills a third row.
evidence_quote: When you finish entering information from your spouse’s statement, the number of rows with Tax claim code D must equal the number of rows with Tax claim code C for the same health insurer ID and membership number.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Private health insurance tax claim code 3' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said why a third row exists or how rarely it is used.

value_domain: Private health insurance tax claim code, fourth policy row
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
variable_description: The claim code on the fourth and last private health insurance policy line the return provides for. Four rows arise where a couple both changed funds during the year, because each claim row taken from one statement has to be matched by a row from the spouse's statement. The four claim code columns are a fixed-width set rather than a list, so a person with five policy lines cannot report them all on the paper return.
value_definition: A single letter from A, B, C, D, E and F on the fourth policy row, matched with HLTH_FND_CD_4 for the insurer on that row.
limitation: Because the return stops at four rows, a value here is a sign that the person's insurance history is at the reporting ceiling, and any policy beyond the fourth is absent from the record entirely rather than being summarised elsewhere.
rationale: The ATO instructions define the tax claim codes and the row-per-statement-line transfer; the four-row ceiling is read from the return's fixed set of policy detail rows rather than stated on the page.
evidence_quote: Print the code in the Tax claim code box in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave 'Private health insurance tax claim code 4' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so it never said that four rows is the reporting ceiling.

value_domain: Three-state indicator, future lodgement expected
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Completing individual information in your tax return
variable_description: The person's own answer to the question "Will you need to lodge an Australian tax return in the future?", which the ATO uses to close a lodgement obligation. It has three states, since the instruction is to "print X in the Yes , Don't know or No box". The ATO lists the situations it is aimed at as future income below the tax-free threshold, only an Australian Government pension, becoming eligible for the seniors and pensioners offset, or moving overseas permanently, and it is also ticked No on a return lodged for someone who has died.
value_definition: A three-state tick, Yes, Don't know or No, answered by the taxpayer or their agent about their expected future lodgement, not about the year being reported.
limitation: It is an intention, not an outcome. People who tick No often lodge again, and a death is recorded here only indirectly through the No box on a deceased estate return, so it cannot be used as a death or emigration marker.
rationale: The ATO's individual information instructions define the question, its three answer boxes and the circumstances it is aimed at, which is the question this final return indicator records.
evidence_quote: Depending on your situation, print X in the Yes , Don't know or No box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Final tax return' from the custodian with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it never said the answer has three states or that it is a forward-looking intention.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator, Australian residency for tax purposes
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Completing individual information in your tax return
variable_description: Whether the person was an Australian resident for tax purposes, which decides their tax-free threshold and rates. The tick is not a citizenship or visa field: the ATO's tests include having "been in Australia continuously for 6 months or more" in the one job and place, and it treats an overseas student on a course longer than six months as a resident. Part-year residents also tick Yes, and are picked up separately at question A2.
value_definition: A two-state tick answered by the taxpayer, with Yes covering both full-year and part-year residency for tax purposes.
limitation: It cannot be used to identify migrants or new arrivals, because a Yes covers a person who has always lived here and a student on a temporary visa alike, and it cannot separate full-year from part-year residents without the part-year threshold question beside it.
rationale: The ATO's individual information instructions set out the residency question, the Yes and No conditions and the residency tests behind them.
evidence_quote: If you're an Australian resident for tax purposes for part of 2024–25, print X in the Yes box and complete question A2 Part-year tax-free threshold in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's question 'Are you an australian resident?' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said this is tax residency or that part-year residents answer Yes.

value_domain: Trading stock valuation method code, C, M or R
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: Which method the business used to value its closing trading stock, printed in the Type box beside the closing stock amount. The ATO gives three: "C cost", "M market selling value" and "R replacement value", and where more than one was used the taxpayer enters the letter that applies to the largest value. A business in its first year, with no closing stock, prints C.
value_definition: A single letter, C, M or R, attached to the closing stock total at P8 label M. It qualifies the amount rather than adding to it.
limitation: It does not identify businesses that valued stock below all three methods for obsolescence, which is disclosed separately at P19, and because the letter reflects only the largest valuation it hides mixed methods within the one business.
rationale: The DIL label 'Closing stock - total - type' matches the Type box at P8, and the ATO instructions define the three code letters and the tie-break rule.
evidence_quote: Step 6 From the list below, choose the letter that matches the method you used to value closing stock. If more than one method was used, select the letter that applies to the largest value: C cost M market selling value R replacement value.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Closing stock - total - type' with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, even though the ATO publishes a three-letter code list for exactly this box.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8 label M, closing stock total
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: The value of trading stock the sole trader still held at 30 June, primary production and other stock added together. The ATO defines it as "the total of the value of all items of trading stock, with the value of each item calculated for tax purposes in accordance with section 70-45 of the ITAA 1997", and requires all stock on hand to be counted "regardless of whether you have paid for the stock". It is a balance sheet quantity sitting inside the expenses block, because the change in stock is what turns purchases into cost of sales.
value_definition: A whole-dollar tax value of stock on hand at year end, excluding any input tax credit component for businesses registered for GST, and shown as the sum of the primary production and non-primary production columns.
limitation: It is not a business expense despite its position on the schedule, and it is not always a genuine year-end count: a small business entity whose stock moved by $5,000 or less may repeat its opening stock figure instead of valuing stock at all, so small movements in this series can be an accounting choice.
rationale: The DIL label 'Closing stock - total' matches P8 label M, and the ATO instructions define what the amount comprises and the simplified trading stock rule that lets small businesses repeat the opening value.
evidence_quote: The amount you show at Closing stock is the total of the value of all items of trading stock, with the value of each item calculated for tax purposes in accordance with section 70-45 of the ITAA 1997.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Closing stock - total' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing warned that the $5,000 simplified rule lets the figure be carried over unchanged.

value_domain: Dollar amount, compulsory trade support loan repayment raised on assessment
value_source: ATO, Study and training support loans, Compulsory repayments
variable_description: The trade support loan repayment the ATO raised on the person's assessment for the year, worked out from their repayment income rather than claimed by them. The ATO says "You don't have to provide loan information in your tax return" and that "we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment". Trade support loans went to apprentices, and the programme has since been renamed the Australian Apprenticeship Support Loan.
value_definition: A dollar amount calculated at assessment, sitting beside the equivalent repayment fields for HELP, SFSS, SSL and ABSTUDY SSL in the same withholding and debt table.
limitation: It is not what the person paid during the year. Employers withhold extra tax against the expected repayment, but the ATO says the balance "doesn’t reduce after each pay cycle; it is only applied as a lump sum after your income tax return is lodged", so this amount times a year count is not a cash flow. A zero can also mean income below the threshold rather than no loan.
rationale: The DIL label names the trade support loan compulsory repayment due, and the ATO explains that compulsory repayments are worked out by the ATO on assessment from the person's repayment income.
evidence_quote: If you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's 'Trade support loan (tsl) compulsory repayment due' with the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the amount is ATO-calculated rather than declared.

value_domain: Dollar amount, excess concessional contributions for the year
value_source: ATO, Concessional contributions cap
variable_description: The amount by which the person's before-tax super contributions passed their cap, which the ATO adds to their assessable income. The ATO says "If you exceed your concessional contributions cap, the excess concessional contributions (ECC) are included in your assessable income" and are "taxed at your marginal tax rate less a 15% tax offset". The ATO works the figure out from fund reporting, not from the return, and will "amend your tax return and send you an amended NOA" when a fund reports late.
value_definition: A dollar amount determined by the ATO from super fund reporting and tax return data, after any unused cap carried forward from the previous five years has been applied.
limitation: It is not a measure of contribution generosity or of a mistake by the taxpayer, since it can be created by an employer's payment timing or a late fund report, and it appears on the record only after the ATO determination, which can arrive after the original assessment. It also does not show whether the person elected to release the amount from their fund.
rationale: The ATO's concessional contributions cap page defines excess concessional contributions, their inclusion in assessable income, the 15 per cent offset and the determination process, which is what this reported amount represents.
evidence_quote: We determine if you exceeded your concessional contributions cap from information reported by your super fund and in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed 'Excess concessional contributions amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said the ATO determines it or that it enters assessable income.

value_domain: Dollar amount at P8 label F, contractor and commission expenses
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: What the sole trader paid for labour and services bought in under contract rather than through wages. The ATO defines these as "expenses for labour and services provided under contract, other than salaries or wages", and lists payments to consultants and contractors, labour-hire arrangements, commissions to people not on a retainer, agency, service, management and consultant fees. It is the contracted-out counterpart to the salary and wage total at P15 on the same schedule.
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of primary production and non-primary production contractor, sub-contractor and commission expenses, shown in the Totals column at P8 label F.
limitation: It is not a complete count of outsourced labour, because the ATO directs external labour recorded in the cost of sales account to be excluded here, accounting and legal fees to go to all other expenses, and payments made without meeting withholding obligations to be left out altogether. A low value can therefore reflect bookkeeping practice rather than less contracting.
rationale: The DIL label matches P8 contractor, sub-contractor and commission expenses, and the ATO instructions define what belongs in the label and what is expressly excluded.
evidence_quote: These are expenses for labour and services provided under contract, other than salaries or wages, for example: payments to self-employed people, such as consultants and contractors, including payments subject to a PAYG voluntary agreement to withhold, and payments made under a labour-hire arrangement
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence as both fields, so nothing named the exclusions that make this an incomplete measure of contracted labour.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question 7 label M
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 7 Australian annuity and superannuation income streams
variable_description: The part of a defined benefit pension that is taxed because the pension exceeds the person's defined benefit income cap. The ATO instructs the taxpayer to work the amount out on its worksheets and "Write the amount from row i at question 7 – label M", and sets the cap for 2024-25 at $118,750. It applies only to capped defined benefit income streams, so it separates old public sector and similar pensions from ordinary account-based pensions reported at labels J and N on the same row.
value_definition: A whole-dollar assessable amount calculated from the tax-free component, taxed element and untaxed element of every capped defined benefit income stream the person received, including lump sums in arrears.
limitation: It is not the pension paid: most of a capped defined benefit pension sits under the cap and never reaches this label, so the column measures the excess above a threshold and cannot be used as a retirement income amount. It also only exists from the year the transfer balance cap rules began, so earlier years are absent by design rather than by non-response.
rationale: The DIL label names the assessable amount from a capped defined benefit income stream, which the ATO instructions place at question 7 label M and define through their worksheets and the defined benefit income cap.
evidence_quote: The amount at row i is your assessable amount from your capped defined benefit income stream. Write the amount from row i at question 7 – label M .
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording with the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so nothing said the amount only arises above the defined benefit income cap.

value_domain: Dollar amount of interest on early payments claimed as a credit
value_source: ATO, Interest on early payments
variable_description: Interest the ATO owes the person for paying a tax debt early, claimed on the return as a credit. The ATO pays it "when you make a payment towards any of the following tax liabilities more than 14 days before the due date", covering income tax, compulsory HELP, VETSL, SFSS, SSL, ABSTUDY SSL and apprenticeship loan repayments. It is small by construction: the ATO "only pay IEP if your interest amount is $0.50 or more".
value_definition: A dollar amount of interest, claimed at the credit for interest on early payments question, that reduces the balance of the assessment. The same interest is assessable income and belongs at the gross interest question as well.
limitation: It is not a general measure of early payment behaviour, because PAYG instalments and amounts withheld by payers are not eligible, and because the ATO automated the calculation for payments made since 1 July 2021, so later years reflect ATO processing rather than taxpayer claiming.
rationale: The ATO's interest on early payments page defines which payments earn the interest, the 14-day rule and the $0.50 minimum, which is the entitlement this claimed credit records; the return's label letter for the claim is not confirmed on that page.
evidence_quote: Interest on early payments (IEP) is interest we pay when you make a payment towards any of the following tax liabilities more than 14 days before the due date
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Credit for interest on early payments - amount of interest' with the generic no-value-list sentence printed twice, so nothing said which payments qualify or that the interest is also assessable income.

value_domain: Dollar amount at question 13 label S, cents shown
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 13 Partnerships and trusts
variable_description: Tax a trustee already paid on the person's share of trust income, claimed back as a credit on their own return. The ATO says to "write the total of your share of credits for tax paid by a trustee at question 13 – label S (show cents)". A trustee pays this tax where the beneficiary is under a legal disability or is not an Australian resident, so the credit marks a particular relationship to the trust rather than ordinary trust income.
value_definition: A dollar and cents amount taken from the statement of distribution or advice issued by the trustee, and claimed as a credit against the person's own tax.
