value_definition: Whole dollars at question T13 label N. It comprises the taxpayer's sole trader net small business income, or their share of a partnership's or trust's net small business income, or both added together.
limitation: It is a purpose-built figure for a now-abolished offset and is not the taxpayer's business income for any other purpose, since ordinary deductions are excluded by instruction. Only lodgers with aggregated turnover under $75,000 completed the item, so the column is a truncated, self-selected slice of small business rather than a population measure, and it stops after 2011-12.
rationale: The DIL label names the entrepreneurs tax offset net small business entity income, and the archived ATO instructions for question T13 give the label letter, the no-deductions rule and the turnover gate for completing the item.
evidence_quote: write the amount of your share of the net small business income at N (do not reduce this amount by any deductions that you are entitled to claim for income tax purposes)
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount excludes ordinary deductions or that only low-turnover claimants appear.

value_domain: Dollar amount of aggregated turnover reported for the entrepreneurs tax offset
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset, label K
variable_description: The turnover of the business the entrepreneurs tax offset was claimed on, measured across the whole related group rather than the taxpayer alone. The ATO defines aggregated turnover as "your annual turnover for the income year plus the annual turnover of any entity connected or affiliated with you at any time during the income year less income derived from dealings between you and any entity connected or affiliated with you." A partner or beneficiary writes the partnership's or trust's turnover here, not their own share of it.
value_definition: Whole dollars at question T13 label K, excluding GST charged and ordinary income from retail fuel sales, and grossed to a full year estimate where the business operated for only part of the year.
limitation: Because a partner writes the entity's turnover rather than a share, adding this column across individuals counts the same business once per partner. The value is also censored by the rules of the item, which was completed only where aggregated turnover was less than $75,000, so the observed distribution stops dead at that point rather than tailing off.
rationale: The DIL label names the entrepreneurs tax offset aggregated turnover, and the archived ATO instructions define aggregated turnover, name the label and gate the item at aggregated turnover of less than $75,000.
evidence_quote: Were you a sole trader with an aggregated turnover of less than $75,000 or did you receive business income from a partnership or trust with an aggregated turnover of less than $75,000?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is an entity-level, group-wide turnover that is censored at $75,000.

value_domain: Dollar amount of entrepreneurs tax offset allowed at assessment
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2012, question T13 Entrepreneurs tax offset
variable_description: The tax break a very small business owner received, worth up to a quarter of the tax on their business income and phased out as the business grew. The ATO defines it as "a tax offset equal to 25% of the income tax liability attributable to the net small business income of a small business entity with an aggregated turnover of $50,000 or less", tapering to nothing at $75,000 of turnover, with a further reduction of 20 cents in the dollar once income passed $70,000 for a single person or $120,000 for someone with a family. The taxpayer did not claim a figure: "We will automatically calculate your ETO from the information you provide at this item and at other items on your tax return."
value_definition: Whole dollars calculated by the ATO from the turnover and net small business income reported at question T13 together with the rest of the return. It is non-refundable and cannot be carried forward or transferred.
limitation: Because the offset is non-refundable, a zero can mean the person had no tax to reduce rather than no entitlement, so the column measures tax position as well as business size. The offset was abolished from 2012-13, so its disappearance is a change in the law and not a collapse in small business activity.
rationale: The archived ATO instructions for question T13 define the offset rate, both taper rules, the automatic calculation and the non-refundable, non-transferable character of the entitlement.
evidence_quote: The entrepreneurs tax offset (ETO) is a tax offset equal to 25% of the income tax liability attributable to the net small business income of a small business entity with an aggregated turnover of $50,000 or less.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Entrepreneurs tax offset' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the amount is ATO-calculated, non-refundable, or that the offset ended.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at item 17 label N of the supplementary tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 17 Net farm management deposits or repayments, label N
variable_description: Farm management deposits a primary producer withdrew inside the normal twelve-month minimum, under the exception for a declared natural disaster or for drought. The ATO instruction is to "Add up early repayments you withdraw during 2024-25 that qualify for the natural disaster or drought exception. Write the total at label N." Keeping the exception separate matters because a normal early withdrawal would strip the deduction claimed when the deposit was made, whereas these withdrawals keep their concessional treatment.
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 17 label N, being repayments made in the year. It sits beside label R, repayments of deposits held twelve months or more, and label D, deposits made, which together produce the net figure at label E.
limitation: The label pools the natural disaster exception and the drought exception, so it cannot tell you which event triggered the withdrawal, and it carries no location. It also records a use of the exception, not distress as such, since the disaster declaration and the Category C assistance are the qualifying facts rather than the farm's own circumstances.
rationale: The DIL label names the early repayment natural disaster component of item 17, and the ATO instructions give the label letter, the completion step and both exceptions that feed it.
evidence_quote: Add up early repayments you withdraw during 2024–25 that qualify for the natural disaster or drought exception. Write the total at label N.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no sense that the column marks a concession being used rather than a farm in trouble.

value_domain: Dollar amount of early stage investor tax offset reported at question T8
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T8 Early stage investor, label L
variable_description: The tax offset a taxpayer earned this year for buying shares in a qualifying early stage innovation company, worth 20% of what they paid. An investor who does not meet the sophisticated investor test is limited to $50,000 of qualifying investment, and the ATO states that "The maximum tax offset (including current year and amounts you carry forward from a prior income year) that you, and your affiliates combined, can claim in 2024-25 is $200,000." Entitlements passed through a partnership or trust are added in at the same label.
value_definition: Whole dollars at question T8 label L, being the current year entitlement after the annual cap is applied. The sibling columns hold the amount actually used, the amount carried into future years and the amount brought in from last year.
limitation: Because the $200,000 cap is applied before the figure is written, it cannot be divided by 20% to recover how much was invested, and any entitlement lost to the cap is not carried forward. It also tells you nothing about the investment's success, since eligibility rests on the company's status at the time the shares were issued.
rationale: The DIL label names the early stage investor amount at question T8, and the ATO instructions give the 20% rate, the sophisticated investor limit, the combined cap and the worked example showing the cap binding before the figure is written.
evidence_quote: The maximum tax offset (including current year and amounts you carry forward from a prior income year) that you, and your affiliates combined, can claim in 2024–25 is $200,000.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Early stage investor' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave no rate, no cap and no way to tell it from the three companion columns.

value_domain: Dollar amount of early stage investor tax offset applied in the current year
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T8 Early stage investor
variable_description: How much of the early stage investor offset actually came off this year's tax bill, which stops at the tax the taxpayer owed. The offset is non-refundable, so the used amount is capped by gross tax payable rather than by the entitlement: in the ATO's own example an investor entitled to $200,000 with $180,000 of tax payable uses $180,000 and carries the remaining $20,000 forward. The figure is worked out at assessment rather than written on the return.
value_definition: Whole dollars, the part of the combined current year and brought-forward entitlement absorbed by tax payable in the income year. It is bounded above by the entitlement recorded at question T8 and by the taxpayer's gross tax.
limitation: A low value can mean either a small investment or a small tax bill, so the column reflects the investor's tax position as much as their investing, and it should not be used as a measure of the incentive's take-up. It is also a derived assessment figure rather than a taxpayer claim, so it will not always match the labels on the lodged form.
rationale: The ATO instructions establish that the offset is non-refundable, that unused amounts carry forward and that the used amount is bounded by tax payable, which is what distinguishes this column from the entitlement column beside it. The published instructions do not name a return label for the used amount, so the reading that it is an assessment output is an inference.
evidence_quote: As Alex's entitlement to the tax offset ($200,000) is greater than the gross tax payable on taxable income ($180,000), the unused portion of the tax offset ($20,000) may be carried forward to future years.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Early stage investor offset used' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said the amount is capped by tax payable rather than by entitlement.

value_domain: Dollar amount of unused early stage investor tax offset carried to later years
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T8 Early stage investor
variable_description: The part of the early stage investor offset that had no tax left to reduce and is pushed into later income years. The ATO says "This tax offset is non-refundable, however you can carry it forward if you don't fully utilise it in 2024-25", and the balance is reported back to the taxpayer on the notice of assessment rather than being written on the return. It is the amount that will reappear as the brought-forward figure in the following year.
value_definition: Whole dollars, being the entitlement for the year less the part absorbed by tax payable. It is produced at assessment, not claimed by the taxpayer.
limitation: It understates unused entitlement, because an amount cut off by the $200,000 annual cap is lost outright and never enters the carry-forward. The balance is also provisional: it is reduced by 30 cents for every dollar of unused net exempt income before it can be claimed next year.
rationale: The ATO instructions state the carry-forward rule, the notice of assessment as the source of the balance, the exempt income reduction and the worked example in which an over-cap amount cannot be carried forward.
evidence_quote: This tax offset is non-refundable, however you can carry it forward if you don't fully utilise it in 2024–25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Early stage investor tax offset carry forward amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say that capped-out entitlement is lost rather than carried.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at question T8 label O of the supplementary tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T8 Early stage investor, label O
variable_description: Unused early stage investor offset brought in from last year, copied by the taxpayer off their earlier notice of assessment. The ATO instruction is to "Write the amount of unused early stage investor tax offset to carry forward from the previous year, reduced by any net exempt income, at question T8 – label O." The taxpayer has to make the exempt income reduction themselves before writing the figure, so the label is a self-assessed transcription rather than a system-supplied value.
value_definition: Whole dollars at question T8 label O, net of a reduction of 30 cents per dollar of unused net exempt income. It represents entitlement from earlier years, not investment made this year.
limitation: It competes with the current year entitlement for the same $200,000 annual ceiling, so a large brought-forward balance crowds out this year's claim rather than adding to it. Because it is transcribed by hand from an earlier assessment, it can disagree with the ATO's own record until the assessment corrects it.
rationale: The DIL label names the amount carried forward from the earlier year at question T8, and the ATO instructions give the label letter, the transcription instruction, the exempt income reduction and the interaction with the annual cap.
evidence_quote: Write the amount of unused early stage investor tax offset to carry forward from the previous year, reduced by any net exempt income, at question T8 – label O.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the figure is self-transcribed or that it consumes the same annual cap.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at question T7 label K of the supplementary tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T7 Early stage venture capital limited partnership, label K
variable_description: The offset a limited partner earned for contributing to a registered early stage venture capital limited partnership, set at a rate of 10%. The rate applies to the smaller of two figures, because the ATO says "If you're a limited partner of an ESVCLP, your amount of the tax offset for each contribution in the ESVCLP is 10% of the lesser of the following": the contribution made during the year, or the investor's share of the eligible venture capital investments the partnership itself made. Only partnerships unconditionally registered on or after 7 December 2015 qualify.
value_definition: Whole dollars at question T7 label K. It comprises entitlements earned as a limited partner of the partnership and entitlements passed through another partnership or a trust, added together.
limitation: It is not simply 10% of the money the investor put in, because the partnership's own deployment of capital can be the binding term, so the column cannot be used to recover contributions. Written notification from the partnership or trustee is the only evidence behind a passed-through amount, so the figure is second-hand for those investors.
rationale: The DIL label names the ESVCLP offset at question T7, and the ATO instructions give the label letter, the 10% rate, the lesser-of rule, the registration date condition and the notification requirement for indirect entitlements.
evidence_quote: If you're a limited partner of an ESVCLP, your amount of the tax offset for each contribution in the ESVCLP is 10% of the lesser of the following:
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Early stage venture capital limited partnership' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it gave neither the rate nor the lesser-of rule that shapes the value.

value_domain: Dollar amount of ESVCLP tax offset applied in the current year
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T7 Early stage venture capital limited partnership
variable_description: How much of the venture capital partnership offset was actually set against this year's tax, which cannot exceed the tax owed. The offset is non-refundable, so entitlement and use come apart whenever the investor's tax bill is smaller than the offset they earned. Anything not used is not lost: the ATO says any unused amount "will show on your notice of assessment for the year ended 30 June 2025" and carries into later years.
value_definition: Whole dollars, the part of the combined current year and brought-forward ESVCLP entitlement absorbed by tax payable in the income year. It is a figure produced at assessment rather than a label on the return.
limitation: A zero here alongside a positive entitlement means there was no tax to reduce, not that no investment was made, so the column cannot stand in for participation in the incentive. Being an assessment output, it also moves when an amendment changes taxable income, unlike the entitlement labels on the lodged form.
rationale: The ATO instructions establish that the ESVCLP offset is non-refundable and that unused amounts appear on the notice of assessment, which is what separates use from entitlement. No published instruction names a return label for the used amount, so the reading that it is an assessment output is an inference.
evidence_quote: This tax offset is non-refundable, however you can carry it forward if it isn't fully utilised in 2024–25.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Esvclp offset used' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never separated the amount used from the amount earned.

value_domain: Dollar amount of unused ESVCLP tax offset carried to later years
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T7 Early stage venture capital limited partnership
variable_description: The venture capital partnership offset left over when tax payable ran out, carried into later income years. The ATO reports it back to the taxpayer rather than asking for it: "Any amount of unused tax offset available to carry forward will show on your notice of assessment for the year ended 30 June 2025." It is the balance that will be transcribed into next year's return at question T7 label M.
value_definition: Whole dollars, being the entitlement for the year less the part absorbed by tax payable. There is no annual dollar ceiling on the ESVCLP offset of the kind that applies to the early stage investor offset.
limitation: The amount that reaches next year is not always the amount recorded here, because it is trimmed by 30 cents for every dollar of unused net exempt income before it can be claimed. A rising balance also signals persistently low tax payable rather than growing venture capital commitment.
rationale: The ATO instructions state the carry-forward rule, name the notice of assessment as the source of the balance and set out the net exempt income reduction that applies before it is claimed.
evidence_quote: Any amount of unused tax offset available to carry forward will show on your notice of assessment for the year ended 30 June 2025.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Esvclp carry forward amount' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say the balance is later reduced by net exempt income.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at question T7 label M of the supplementary tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question T7 Early stage venture capital limited partnership, label M
variable_description: Unused venture capital partnership offset brought in from the earlier year, after the taxpayer has knocked off any reduction for exempt income. The ATO instruction is to "Write the amount of unused ESVCLP tax offset you carry forward from 2023-24, reduced by any net exempt income, at question T7 – label M." The reduction is 30 cents in the dollar of unused net exempt income and the taxpayer applies it themselves before writing the figure.
value_definition: Whole dollars at question T7 label M, transcribed from the earlier year's notice of assessment or amended assessment and adjusted for net exempt income.
limitation: It dates the entitlement to an earlier year, so it cannot be used to place a venture capital contribution in the year the column is populated. Because the taxpayer performs the exempt income reduction before writing it, the figure can differ from the ATO's own carried-forward balance until an assessment reconciles the two.
rationale: The DIL label names the ESVCLP offset carried forward from the earlier year, and the ATO instructions give the label letter, the transcription source and the exempt income reduction the taxpayer must apply.
evidence_quote: Write the amount of unused ESVCLP tax offset you carry forward from 2023–24, reduced by any net exempt income, at question T7 – label M.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say the taxpayer reduces the figure before writing it.

value_domain: Date of an employment termination payment, item 4 of the individual tax return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments
variable_description: The day the employer paid the termination payment, taken off the income statement or payment summary rather than remembered by the taxpayer. The ATO instruction is "Write at Date of payment the payment date on your income statement or payment summary." It is a payment date, not a termination date, and the two can be months apart for a payment made after a dispute or a late settlement.
value_definition: A calendar date on the individual return at item 4, entered alongside the payer's ABN. The domain is open and there is no code list.
limitation: It is deliberately left empty for anyone with two or more termination payments, because those are reported on a schedule and the ATO says "Don't write any date of payment or payer's ABN." A missing date therefore signals multiple payments rather than a gap in the data, and treating it as the date employment ended will misdate a late or disputed payment.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 4 give the source of the date, its position on the form and the rule that suppresses it where an ETP schedule is lodged.
evidence_quote: Don't write any date of payment or payer's ABN.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Employment Termination Payments - date of payment' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not warn that the field is blank by design for multiple payments.

value_domain: Dollar amount of employment termination payment tax offset calculated at assessment
value_source: ATO, How ETP components are taxed
variable_description: The offset that holds the tax on a termination payment down to a concessional rate, worked out by the ATO rather than claimed by the taxpayer. It brings the rate on the taxable component to "17% if you reach your preservation age" or 32% if not, and only up to a cap: the ATO says "Any amount over the relevant cap will be taxed at the top marginal rate of 45% plus Medicare levy of 2%." Which cap applies depends on the ETP code, since codes O and P are tested against the whole-of-income cap as well as the ETP cap.
value_definition: Whole dollars derived at assessment as the difference between tax at the taxpayer's marginal rate and tax at the capped concessional rate on the taxable component. It is not a label the taxpayer completes.
limitation: The offset covers only the part of the payment inside the cap, so a very large redundancy shows an offset that is small relative to the payment and the two cannot be compared directly. It also carries no information about why the payment was made, which lives in the ETP code on the same row.
rationale: The ATO page on ETP taxation gives the concessional rates, the preservation age split, the two caps and the code-based rule that selects between them, which is what determines the offset amount.
evidence_quote: Amounts above the relevant cap are taxed at the top marginal rate of 45% plus Medicare levy of 2%
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Termination payment tax offset' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the offset is ATO-calculated or that it is bounded by a cap.

value_domain: ETP code at item 4 of the individual tax return (R, O, S, P, D, B, N, T, M)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments, ETP code descriptions; and ATO, How ETP components are taxed
variable_description: A single letter saying why the termination payment was made, which then decides how much of it is taxed concessionally. R covers redundancy, early retirement, invalidity and compensation for personal injury, unfair dismissal, harassment or discrimination; O covers everything else, such as a golden handshake or payment in lieu of notice; S and P mark a second payment for the same termination; D, B and N mark death benefit payments by the recipient's dependency status; and T marks a payment to the trustee of a deceased estate. The taxpayer copies the letter rather than choosing it: "You must enter a valid code, find it on your income statement or payment summary." The distinction is not cosmetic, because the ATO's page on how ETP components are taxed says a payment "is subject to the whole-of-income cap, if the code on your end of year statement is O or P".
value_definition: A one-character code taken from the payer's income statement or payment summary. Code M is used instead where the taxpayer received two or more ETPs and lodged an employment termination payment schedule.
limitation: For exactly the people with several termination payments the reason is lost, because code M replaces the substantive codes and the schedule is not carried here. The code is also chosen by the payer, so a redundancy coded O rather than R reflects the employer's judgement and not the character of the payment.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 4 publish the full code table with the circumstances behind each letter, the M code for multiple payments and the cap consequence attached to codes O and P.
evidence_quote: You must enter a valid code, find it on your income statement or payment summary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Type of taxable employment termination payment' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it published no codes and no consequence for having one.

value_domain: Dollar amount, excessive component of an eligible termination payment, to 30 June 2007
value_source: ATO, Other super rates and thresholds, Reasonable benefit limits
variable_description: The part of a 2006-07 termination payment that took the person past their lifetime concessional limit and so lost every concession. Under the pre-2007 regime each person had a reasonable benefit limit, which the ATO describes as being used "to determine the concessional tax rates limits of a reasonable benefit limit (RBL) for a particular financial year", covering both pension and lump sum benefits. Anything above that limit was the excessive component and was taxed at the top rate, which is why the return reported it apart from the rest of the payment.
value_definition: Whole dollars on the 2006-07 individual return, reported separately from the balance of the payment, which the column names on the same row describe as the amount other than the excessive component.
limitation: Reasonable benefit limits were abolished from 1 July 2007, so the column empties out after 2006-07 and that break is a change in the law rather than a change in redundancy behaviour. It is also not comparable with the ETP cap that replaced it, since a reasonable benefit limit was a lifetime measure across a person's whole benefits and the cap applies payment by payment.
rationale: The ATO's superannuation rates page confirms that reasonable benefit limits operated up to 30 June 2007 and published the limits used to work out concessional treatment, which is the framework that produced an excessive component. No live ATO page defines the excessive component itself, so the connection between the label and the limits is drawn rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Up to 30 June 2007, the following table can be used to determine the concessional tax rates limits of a reasonable benefit limit (RBL) for a particular financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label with a stray quotation mark and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing explained the abolished regime that gives the column its meaning.

value_domain: Dollar amount, taxable component of employment termination payments, item 4 label I
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments, label I; and ATO, How ETP components are taxed
variable_description: The assessable part of a termination payment, being what is left once the tax-free amount is stripped out. The instruction is to "Write the taxable component of your ETP, from your income statement or payment summary at question 4 – label I", and the ATO's page on ETP components explains that "After any tax-free amount is deducted from your payment, the balance is the taxable component". The column name preserves the older framing of an amount other than the excessive component, from the reasonable benefit limit regime that no longer applies, but the quantity reported is the taxable component at item 4 label I.
value_definition: Whole dollars taken from the payer's income statement or payment summary and written at item 4 label I. Where the taxpayer received two or more payments it is the sum of the taxable components across all of them.
limitation: It leaves out the tax-free component, so it understates the money the person actually received on leaving a job, sometimes by a large margin for a long-serving redundancy. Where several payments are summed the reason for each is lost, so a genuine redundancy and a golden handshake are indistinguishable inside one figure.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 4 name the label, the source document and the summing rule, and the ATO page on ETP components defines the taxable component as the balance after the tax-free amount.
evidence_quote: Write the taxable component of your ETP, from your income statement or payment summary at question 4 – label I.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Employment termination payments taxable component' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never explained the tax-free amount it excludes or the old wording in the column name.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax withheld from employment termination payments, item 4
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments
variable_description: Tax the employer held back from the termination payment and sent to the ATO on the taxpayer's behalf. The ATO instruction is to "Write the total amount of tax withheld from your ETP, from your income statement or payment summary under Tax withheld at the left of question 4 – label I", so the figure is reported by the payer rather than estimated by the taxpayer. It is a credit at assessment, sitting to the left of the taxable component it was withheld from.
value_definition: Whole dollars taken from the income statement or payment summary. Where two or more termination payments were received the taxpayer adds the withheld amounts across the schedule and reports one total.
limitation: Withholding is not the tax finally paid on the payment: the termination payment offset is applied at assessment, so the final liability can be well below what was withheld. Dividing this column by the taxable component gives a withholding rate, not an effective tax rate.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 4 give the source of the withheld amount, its position on the form and the summing rule for multiple payments, and the ATO page on ETP taxation shows that the concessional rate is delivered at assessment.
evidence_quote: Write the total amount of tax withheld from your ETP, from your income statement or payment summary under Tax withheld at the left of question 4 – label I.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Tax withheld on employment termination payments' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not distinguish withholding from the tax finally assessed.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the 15% excess concessional contributions tax offset
value_source: ATO, Concessional contributions cap
variable_description: A credit that gives back the 15% the super fund already paid when before-tax contributions above the cap are added to the person's taxable income. The ATO explains that excess concessional contributions "are taxed at your marginal tax rate less a 15% tax offset to account for the contributions tax already paid by your super fund." The offset is non-refundable, so it reduces tax payable but never produces a refund on its own.
value_definition: Whole dollars equal to 15% of the excess concessional contributions included in assessable income for the year. It is calculated by the ATO from the determination and applied in the assessment or the amended assessment.
limitation: Its presence dates the breach to the year the contributions were made, not the year the assessment was issued, and the two are often different because determinations arrive after lodgment. Being non-refundable, a nil offset does not mean there was no excess, only that there was no tax left for it to reduce.
rationale: The ATO's concessional contributions cap page states that excess contributions enter assessable income, gives the 15% offset rate, names it as non-refundable and describes the assessment process that produces it.
evidence_quote: These are taxed at your marginal tax rate less a 15% tax offset to account for the contributions tax already paid by your super fund.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Excess concessional contributions offset available' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said what the 15% represents or that it is non-refundable.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the 15% offset on associated earnings from excess non-concessional contributions
value_source: ATO, Non-concessional contributions cap
variable_description: A credit against the notional earnings added to income when someone released after-tax super contributions that went over their cap. Where the person takes option 1 and releases the excess, the ATO includes "your associated earnings in your taxable income" and gives "a non-refundable tax offset of 15% of the associated earnings." The offset attaches to the earnings only; the excess contributions themselves are released to the person rather than taxed as income.
value_definition: Whole dollars equal to 15% of the associated earnings assessed for the year. It is worked out by the ATO from the excess non-concessional contributions determination, not claimed on the return.
limitation: It measures the credit on the earnings and not the cost of the breach, which for someone who leaves the money in the fund is excess contributions tax at the top marginal rate plus Medicare levy. A nil value therefore fits both a person with no excess and a person who chose to be taxed at 47% instead.
rationale: The ATO's non-concessional contributions cap page sets out both options, states that option 1 brings associated earnings into taxable income with a non-refundable 15% offset, and gives the rate that applies under option 2.
evidence_quote: a non-refundable tax offset of 15% of the associated earnings.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Excess non-concessional contributions offset available' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say the offset attaches to earnings rather than to the contributions.

value_domain: Dollar liability for excess private health insurance rebate claimed as a premium reduction
value_source: ATO, Claiming the private health insurance rebate
variable_description: Health insurance rebate the taxpayer already took as a premium discount but was not entitled to on their actual income, recovered as a debt at assessment. The ATO says "If you claim too much private health insurance rebate as a premium reduction, we recover the amount as a tax liability. This liability will be listed on your notice of assessment as an Excess private health insurance refund or reduction (rebate reduced)." It is calculated at assessment against the income tiers, not claimed or self-assessed by the taxpayer.
value_definition: Whole dollars added to the tax assessed. It is the gap between the rebate percentage the insurer applied through the year and the percentage the taxpayer's income for surcharge purposes turned out to support.
limitation: It records a mismatch against income tiers, usually because income rose during the year, and is not evidence of misreporting by the taxpayer or the insurer. It is not necessarily even the taxpayer's own liability: where a spouse does not lodge in time, the ATO shifts that spouse's private health insurance liability onto this person.
rationale: The ATO's page on claiming the rebate uses the same wording as the custodian's label, describes the recovery mechanism, works an example and sets out the spouse transfer rule.
evidence_quote: If you claim too much private health insurance rebate as a premium reduction, we recover the amount as a tax liability.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the assessment line item with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say why the liability arises or that a spouse's debt can land here.

value_domain: Dollar amount of exempt foreign employment income, item 20 label N
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, label N
variable_description: Foreign salary an Australian resident earned that Australia does not tax, as carried on the 2023-24 twelve-month extract of the income tax return. It is the item 20 label N figure, reported net of the non-capital costs of earning it and floored at zero: the ATO says to "write the total that is exempt from tax less any expenses that aren't capital in nature that you incur in earning that exempt income at question 20 – label N. If the amount is a loss, write 0 (zero)." No foreign income tax offset can be claimed on it.
value_definition: Whole dollars converted to Australian currency, reported net of related non-capital expenses. Taxpayers reporting an amount here also attach a schedule of additional information setting the income out.
limitation: Exempt does not mean invisible: the amount lifts the rate applied to the person's other income and counts as the spouse's target foreign income in the family tests, so treating it as income of no consequence understates the tax effect. This column also spells the abbreviation differently from the long-running income tax return column of the same meaning, so stacking years on column name alone will drop one of them.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 20 give the label, the net-of-expenses rule, the zero floor, the schedule requirement and the bar on a foreign income tax offset, and the spouse details instructions confirm the amount counts as target foreign income.
evidence_quote: If any of your foreign employment income is exempt from tax, write the total that is exempt from tax less any expenses that aren't capital in nature that you incur in earning that exempt income at question 20 – label N.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Exempt foreign employment income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no warning that a near-identical column name exists on the other income tax return tables.

value_domain: Dollar amount of exempt foreign employment income, item 20 label N
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 20 Foreign source income and foreign assets or property, label N
variable_description: Salary earned working overseas that Australia exempts from tax because the foreign posting ran long enough, reported on the main income and loss table. Length of service is the gate: "If your period of continuous service in a foreign country was 90 days or less, your foreign employment income isn't exempt from tax. If it was 91 days or more, your foreign employment income will generally be exempt from tax." The exemption is narrow, reaching relief work financed from a declared developing country relief fund, employment by a prescribed charitable or religious institution, deployment as a member of an Australian Government disciplined force and Austrade-approved projects, rather than expatriate employment generally.
value_definition: Whole dollars at item 20 label N, converted to Australian currency and reduced by the non-capital expenses of earning the income, with a loss written as zero.
limitation: It is not a measure of overseas work: a posting of 90 days or less produces nothing here even though the income was foreign and the person was abroad, and taxable foreign employment income goes to item 20 label U instead. Because it is net of expenses, it also cannot be read as gross foreign salary.
rationale: The ATO instructions for question 20 state the 91 day continuous service test, the exemption's narrow scope and the net-of-expenses reporting rule, which together fix what the label counts and what it misses.
evidence_quote: If your period of continuous service in a foreign country was 90 days or less, your foreign employment income isn't exempt from tax. If it was 91 days or more, your foreign employment income will generally be exempt from tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Foreign source income exempt foreign employment income' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that a short posting produces a zero here.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Reconciliation items label H
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Reconciliation items
variable_description: The net add-back that turns the sole trader's booked expenses into the expenses tax law allows. The ATO defines it as a difference: "Your expense reconciliation adjustment is your total expense add-backs less your total expense subtractions." Add-backs are accounting entries that are not deductible, chiefly depreciation, provisions and income tax expense; subtractions are tax deductions that never appear in the accounts, chiefly decline in value. It is the figure that stands between total expenses on the same row and net business income.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount covering the primary production and non-primary production adjustments together. It can be negative, in which case the return marks it with an L in a separate loss box rather than a minus sign.
limitation: The sign lives in a separate loss indicator, so an unsigned value read on its own can be wrong by twice its size. A zero does not mean the accounts and the tax return agree, because many sole traders keep their books on a tax basis and have nothing to reconcile.
rationale: The DIL label names the total expense reconciliation adjustment, a defined step of the ATO business and professional items schedule. The P8 reconciliation items instructions define the adjustment, list what goes into each side and give the worksheet that produces it.
evidence_quote: Your expense reconciliation adjustment is your total expense add-backs less your total expense subtractions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Expenses, Totals column
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: Everything the sole trader's business spent in the year as booked in its accounts, before any tax adjustment. The ATO builds it by adding "all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses" and the same run down the non-primary production column. It therefore equals the two expense columns on the same row added together, and it is an accounting figure rather than a deduction total.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount running from cost of sales through to all other expenses, self-assessed from the taxpayer's own books. A negative total is marked with an L in a loss box.
limitation: Subtracting this from total business income does not give taxable business income; the expense reconciliation adjustment on the same row is what makes the two agree. Expenses of personal services income reported at P1 are excluded, so a contractor caught by the personal services income rules shows less here than they actually spent.
rationale: The DIL label names the P8 total expenses figure, and the ATO expenses instructions give the exact addition that produces it and the range of expense lines it spans.
evidence_quote: Add up all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Expenses label T
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: Business expenses the sole trader booked against activities other than farming, fishing or forestry. The ATO builds it by adding "all the expenses you have written in the Non-primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses" and putting the result at label T. For most sole traders this column carries the whole expense figure and the primary production column beside it is blank.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount spanning cost of sales, foreign resident withholding expenses, contractor, superannuation, bad debts, lease, rent, interest, depreciation, motor vehicle, repairs and all other expenses for non-primary production activities.
limitation: A person running both a farm and a shop allocates expenses between this column and the primary production column by their own judgement, so the split is self-assessed rather than measured. The column also gives no count of businesses, so one figure can cover several unrelated activities.
rationale: The DIL label names the non-primary production total expenses figure at P8, and the ATO expenses instructions set out the addition that produces label T.
evidence_quote: Add up all the expenses you have written in the Non-primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses . Write the total at label T .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Expenses label S
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: Business expenses the sole trader booked against farming, fishing or forestry activities. The ATO instruction is to "Add up all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses" and write the result at label S, after working through the primary production worksheet. A non-zero value is a reasonable marker that the person carried on a primary production business in the year.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount covering the same expense lines as the non-primary production column but for primary production activities only, self-assessed and drawn from the primary production worksheet.
limitation: A non-zero value says the person claimed primary production expenses, not that farming was their main activity or their main source of income, so a hobby-scale operation and a large farm look the same here. Farm management deposits, which are the main tax instrument farmers use to smooth income, are handled at item 17 and are not in this figure.
rationale: The DIL label names the primary production total expenses figure at P8, and the ATO expenses instructions give the addition that produces label S and point to the primary production worksheet.
evidence_quote: Add up all the expenses you have written in the Primary production column, from Cost of sales down to and including All other expenses . Write the total at P8 – label S in your schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item A5 label X
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item A5
variable_description: The value of distributions the person received on which a trust, partnership or company had already paid family trust distribution tax. The ATO says "You don't include in your assessable income any part of a distribution to you on which family trust distribution tax has already been paid", so the money never reaches taxable income. It is collected anyway because the Medicare levy surcharge test adds it back, and a spouse copies it into the spouse income section of their own return.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, being the distributions that would have been assessable less any expenses that would have been deductible against them. It covers property and the free use of assets as well as cash, and is left blank when the result is zero or negative.
limitation: The amount is outside taxable income, so a reader who adds it to taxable income has built a different concept from the one the return reports and from the one used in tax statistics. A zero or negative result is left blank rather than written as a number, so blanks mix people with no such distribution and people whose deductible expenses exceeded it.
rationale: The DIL label names the amount on which family trust distribution tax has been paid, which is a single labelled question on the ATO supplementary return. The instructions give the calculation, the exclusion from assessable income and the reason the ATO still collects it.
evidence_quote: You don't include in your assessable income any part of a distribution to you on which family trust distribution tax has already been paid, and which would otherwise be assessable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar and cent amount reported at tax return item 13 label Q
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 13 Part F
variable_description: The person's share of franking credits that reached them through a partnership or trust rather than through shares they held themselves. The ATO instruction is to "Write the amount of your share of any allowable franking credits which you're entitled to claim as a franking tax offset through a partnership or trust at question 13 – label Q." The claim only stands where the matching franked distribution is at label O, U or C on the same row, and where the holding period and related payments rules are satisfied.
value_definition: A dollars-and-cents amount, self-assessed from the distribution statement the partnership or trust issued, covering imputation credits received indirectly only.
limitation: It is the credit claimed rather than the credit the trust or partnership was entitled to pass on, and a trust in overall tax loss passes on none at all. Franking credits on directly held shares sit at item 11 and are absent here, so this column understates a person's total imputation credits.
rationale: The DIL label names the share of franking credit from franked dividends, which is a single labelled question in Part F of item 13. The ATO instructions define what the label carries and the conditions on claiming it.
evidence_quote: Write the amount of your share of any allowable franking credits which you're entitled to claim as a franking tax offset through a partnership or trust at question 13 – label Q .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign investment fund and foreign life policy income (income years to 2009-10)
value_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, chapter 4
variable_description: Income attributed to the person from a foreign investment fund or foreign life assurance policy, a measure that stops after 2009-10. The ATO now states flatly that "The FIF measures have been repealed and do not apply to taxpayers from 2010–11." Until then Part XI of the ITAA 1936 taxed Australian residents on income accumulating inside a foreign company or trust they did not control, whether or not any of it was paid out. The column appears only in the 2009-10 extract for that reason.
value_definition: A whole-dollar accruals amount worked out under Part XI of the ITAA 1936 and reported in the foreign entities item of the supplementary return. It is an attribution, not a cash receipt.
limitation: A zero cannot be read as no offshore fund holdings: a long list of exemptions, including the balanced-portfolio and active-business exemptions, removed a holding from attribution altogether. The column disappearing after 2009-10 records a repeal, not taxpayers giving up offshore investment.
rationale: The DIL label names FIF and FLP income, which was a labelled amount in the foreign entities item until the measures were repealed. The ATO guide chapter states the repeal and the year it took effect, and describes what the measures attributed.
evidence_quote: The FIF measures have been repealed and do not apply to taxpayers from 2010–11.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator for an interest in a foreign investment fund or foreign life assurance policy
value_source: ATO, Foreign investment funds guide 2010, chapter 2
variable_description: A yes or no flag for whether the person held an interest in a foreign investment fund or a foreign life assurance policy. The ATO's definition is very wide: "A FIF is any foreign company or foreign trust." A foreign life assurance policy is one issued by an entity that was not an Australian resident at any time in the income year. The flag sat beside the attributed income amount in the foreign entities item and, like it, stops after 2009-10.
value_definition: A single self-assessed flag on the supplementary return, answered before the taxpayer works out any attributable amount.
limitation: A yes does not imply an attributed amount, since the exemptions removed the income while leaving the interest in place, so the flag and the income column on the same row need not agree. A no is not proof of no offshore holding either, because an interest in a controlled foreign company was a separate question on the same row.
rationale: The DIL label is the FIF or FLP interest question from the foreign entities item. The ATO guide chapter defines both terms and the exclusions that decide who answers yes.
evidence_quote: A FIF is any foreign company or foreign trust .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Australian income year (year ending 30 June)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025
variable_description: The Australian income year the return covers, running 1 July to 30 June and named by its closing year. The ATO's 2025 instructions are the instructions for 2024-25, so a value of 2025 means the year ended 30 June 2025. Every income, deduction, offset and levy amount on the same row belongs to that year.
value_definition: A year value naming the income year of the lodgement. It is the reference period for the row, not a point in time.
limitation: It is not the year the return was lodged or processed, and late or amended lodgements can arrive years afterwards; the form received date on the same row is what carries that. It is also not a calendar year, so joining to calendar-year sources without apportionment mixes two different twelve-month windows.
rationale: The ATO publishes one set of individual tax return instructions per income year, and the 2025 edition covers 2024-25, which fixes the naming convention this column follows.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished the income year from the lodgement date.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item 17 label E
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 17
variable_description: The net movement in the person's farm management deposits: repayments taken out less deductible deposits put in. The ATO's step is to "Add up the amounts you show at labels N and R , and subtract the amount you show at label D", where N and R are early and ordinary repayments and D is deductible deposits. Repayments count as assessable income in the year they are made, so a positive figure adds to taxable income and a negative one reduces it.
value_definition: A whole-dollar signed net flow for the year, assembled from the deposit and repayment labels on the same row. A negative result carries an L in a loss box.
limitation: It is a flow, not a balance, so nothing here says how much the person has on deposit or how long it has been sitting there. Non-deductible deposits are excluded from the deposit side, so a farmer can move money into the scheme without this figure moving at all.
rationale: The DIL label names the net farm management deposits or repayments amount, a single labelled question on the supplementary return. The ATO instructions give the arithmetic and the treatment of repayments as assessable income.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts you show at labels N and R , and subtract the amount you show at label D .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Count of dependent children reported at tax return item M1 label Y
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item M1
variable_description: The number of dependent children the person counted when claiming a Medicare levy reduction based on family income. The ATO instruction is to "Write the number of your dependent children (from worksheet 2 – row e ) at question M1 – label Y . If you have none, write 0 (zero)." A dependent child must be an Australian resident the person maintained and must fall under the adjusted taxable income limits for the year. Each child raises the family income threshold at which the levy starts to bite.
value_definition: A small non-negative integer, self-assessed against the ATO's dependency and income tests for that income year.
limitation: The counting rule depends on partnering status, so it is not a household child count: a person single or separated on 30 June counts only children for whom family tax benefit was paid, while a partnered person counts all of them. People who do not claim the reduction leave the label blank, so a missing value is not evidence of childlessness.
rationale: The DIL label names the Medicare levy reduction dependent children and students count, which is a single labelled question at item M1. The ATO instructions define a dependent child, give the counting rules and state the label.
evidence_quote: Write the number of your dependent children (from worksheet 2 – row e ) at question M1 – label Y . If you have none, write 0 (zero).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of attributed foreign investment fund and foreign life policy income under the mid-2000s foreign entities column name
value_source: ATO, Fund income tax return 2010 instructions, item 13 label D
variable_description: Income attributed to the person under the foreign investment fund rules, carried under the earlier foreign entities column name used in the mid-2000s extracts. The ATO describes the matching label as follows: "Attributed income of a FIF or FLP is the income attributed to the taxpayer from FIFs or FLPs, calculated in accordance with Part XI of the ITAA 1936." The 2009-10 extract renames the same quantity, and the rules were repealed from 2010-11.
value_definition: A whole-dollar accruals amount computed under Part XI of the ITAA 1936, covering both foreign investment funds and the investment component of certain foreign life policies.
limitation: Because the column was renamed between extract vintages, stacking years on the variable name alone drops either the earlier or the later half of an already short series. Attributed income is also not a distribution, so it cannot stand in for money the person actually received from offshore.
rationale: The DIL label names FIF and FLP income in the foreign entities item of the 2006-07 extract. The ATO instruction for the corresponding label on the fund return defines the attributed amount and the legislation it is worked out under.
evidence_quote: Attributed income of a FIF or FLP is the income attributed to the taxpayer from FIFs or FLPs, calculated in accordance with Part XI of the ITAA 1936.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item D11 label Y
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item D11
variable_description: The tax-free slice of a foreign pension or annuity, deducted because it returns the person's own contributions to them. The ATO explains that "That part of your annual pension or annuity income that represents a return to you of your personal contributions is free from tax", and calls that slice the deductible amount of the undeducted purchase price. It only makes sense alongside the gross foreign pension declared at item 20 on the same return.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction, normally the undeducted purchase price divided by a life expectancy factor, or a fixed country percentage such as 8% of a United Kingdom State Pension or 25% of a Dutch pension.
limitation: It is a deduction against foreign pension income rather than income itself, so adding it to an income measure inflates the total. Because several country formulas are a fixed percentage of the gross pension, the amount often moves mechanically with the pension and says nothing about what the person actually contributed.
rationale: The DIL label names the deductible amount of the undeducted purchase price of a foreign pension or annuity, which is item D11 on the supplementary return. The ATO instructions define the undeducted purchase price, the calculation and the country-specific rates.
evidence_quote: That part of your annual pension or annuity income that represents a return to you of your personal contributions is free from tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator reported at tax return item 20 label P
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 20 Part I
variable_description: A yes or no flag for whether the person held overseas assets worth A$50,000 or more at any point in the year. The return asks it directly: "At any time during 2024–25, do you own or have an interest in assets outside Australia that have a total value of A$50,000 or more?" It is answered at item 20 label P and carries no dollar value at all.
value_definition: A single flag against a fixed A$50,000 threshold applied to the combined value of all assets located outside Australia, self-assessed by the taxpayer.
limitation: The threshold is not indexed, so the same flag stands for less real wealth every year and the share flagged drifts upward with asset prices alone. It also cannot separate a person just over A$50,000 from one with millions offshore, and anyone below the line is indistinguishable from a person with no foreign assets.
rationale: The DIL label is the foreign property indicator, which is the item 20 label P question. The ATO instructions give the question wording, the threshold and the fact that only a yes or no is recorded.
evidence_quote: At any time during 2024–25, do you own or have an interest in assets outside Australia that have a total value of A$50,000 or more?
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of foreign-sourced employee share scheme discounts reported at tax return item 12
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 12
variable_description: The part of the person's employee share scheme discount that came from a foreign employer or a foreign scheme. The ATO folds these into the scheme totals rather than treating them as extra income, telling taxpayers to add up the discounts "including amounts on your Employee share scheme statements" and "any foreign source discounts you receive" at each of the taxed-upfront and deferral labels. The column is therefore a memorandum subset of the discount figures on the same row, not an addition to them.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount already counted inside the taxed-upfront and deferral discount labels on the same row, sourced from the foreign employer's written advice where no Australian employee share scheme statement exists.
limitation: Adding it to the item 12 discount totals double counts, because it is a component of them rather than a separate income stream. The number is a discount measured at a taxing point, so it does not record what the shares were eventually worth or whether the person ever sold them.
rationale: The DIL label names employee share schemes foreign source discounts. The ATO item 12 instructions establish that foreign source discounts are added into the taxed-upfront and deferral totals, which fixes this column as a component of those amounts.
evidence_quote: Add up all the discount amounts you receive from taxed-upfront schemes eligible for reduction , including: amounts showing on your Employee share scheme statements any foreign source discounts you receive.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar and cent amount reported at tax return item 20 label O
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 20 Part H
variable_description: Credit for foreign tax the person already paid on income that Australia also taxes, claimed as the foreign income tax offset. The ATO caps the simple case: "Write the total amount of foreign tax paid at question 20 – label O . Show cents. This amount can't be greater than $1,000." Above $1,000 the taxpayer works through the offset limit in the Guide to foreign income tax offset rules, so the number becomes a limited entitlement rather than raw foreign tax paid. The ATO notes the offset was "formerly foreign tax credits", which is where the column name comes from.
value_definition: A dollars-and-cents offset amount, equal to total foreign tax paid where that is $1,000 or less, and equal to a calculated offset limit above that point.
limitation: The column changes meaning at $1,000, so it is a clean measure of foreign tax paid only below the threshold and a capped entitlement above it. Unused foreign income tax offset cannot be carried forward and nothing on the row records how much was forgone.
rationale: The DIL label names the foreign income tax offset at item 20. The ATO instructions give the label, the $1,000 threshold, the two ways the amount is worked out and the former name of the offset.
evidence_quote: No – Write the total amount of foreign tax paid at question 20 – label O . Show cents. This amount can't be greater than $1,000.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator reported at tax return item 19 label W
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 19 Part B
variable_description: A yes or no flag for whether the person ever transferred money, property or services to a non-resident trust. The ATO explains that the transferor trust measures "may apply if, at any time, you directly or indirectly transfer or cause the transfer of property (including money) or services to a non-resident trust." The question reaches back over the person's whole history rather than the income year, and a yes is followed by an attributed foreign income amount on the same row.
value_definition: A single lifetime flag covering direct and indirect transfers to a trust that has no Australian resident trustee and no Australian central management and control at any time in the year.
limitation: It is not a flag for holding an offshore trust interest: a beneficiary who never transferred anything answers no, and a person who controls a foreign company answers the separate controlled foreign company question instead. Because the question covers any time in the past, a yes need not relate to anything that happened in the reference year.
rationale: The DIL label is the foreign transfer indicator, which is item 19 label W. The ATO instructions give the question, the definition of a non-resident trust and what follows a yes answer.
evidence_quote: The transferor trust measures may apply if, at any time, you directly or indirectly transfer or cause the transfer of property (including money) or services to a non-resident trust.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Whole hours reported at the BPI schedule label S under 'How long did it take you to complete this schedule?'
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, About these instructions
variable_description: The hours the person says it took to prepare and complete the business and professional items schedule. The ATO explains why it asks: "We are committed to reducing the costs involved in complying with your tax obligations. Your response to this item will help us monitor these costs." The count is meant to cover reading instructions, collecting information, making calculations and putting the business's affairs in order for the agent, plus the agent's own time, rounded up to the nearest hour.
value_definition: A whole-hour count for one schedule, combining the taxpayer's time and their tax agent's time.
limitation: It is a compliance-cost self-report rather than a measured duration, and where an agent prepares the schedule the client's hours are the agent's estimate of someone else's effort. It covers the business schedule alone, so it is not the time taken over the whole tax return and cannot be compared with return-level compliance-cost figures.
rationale: The DIL label names the hours to complete the business and professional items section. The ATO instructions state the label, the purpose of the question and exactly which activities the taxpayer should count.
evidence_quote: We are committed to reducing the costs involved in complying with your tax obligations. Your response to this item will help us monitor these costs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Lodgement receipt date
value_source: ATO, Your notice of assessment
variable_description: The date the ATO received the lodgement, which is not the date the person sent it. The gap can be large on paper: the ATO aims to process paper lodgements within 50 business days "from the date we receive the lodgment (paper lodgments may take up to 7 weeks to show on our systems)", against 12 business days online. Read against the financial year on the same row, the date separates on-time self-lodgers from agent-lodged and late returns.
value_definition: A date stamped when the return entered ATO systems, not when the taxpayer signed, posted or transmitted it.
limitation: It measures ATO intake as much as taxpayer behaviour, so the paper-against-online gap makes part of any lag an artefact of lodgement channel rather than a person being late. It also cannot distinguish an original return from one re-received after a correction, so a very late date may reflect an amendment.
rationale: The variable is lodgement metadata rather than a return label. The ATO page on the notice of assessment describes the receipt of a lodgement and the delay between sending and appearing in ATO systems, which is what makes a received date different from a lodgement date.
evidence_quote: by paper, we aim for processing within 50 business days (10 weeks) from the date we receive the lodgment (paper lodgments may take up to 7 weeks to show on our systems)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing distinguished a received date from the date the taxpayer lodged.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item 18 label X
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 18
variable_description: Credit for tax a purchaser withheld from the person when they sold property under the foreign resident capital gains withholding rules. The ATO says the rules apply "to certain transactions entered into on or after 1 July 2016", so the column is empty in earlier years as a matter of law. The buyer withholds and remits the amount, the ATO tells the seller it has been received, and the seller claims it back at item 18 label X.
value_definition: A whole-dollar credit against tax, recorded from ATO advice to the seller rather than worked out by the taxpayer. It is deliberately kept out of the business withholding credits at item 15.
limitation: Its presence means a property transaction was caught by the rules, not that the seller was a foreign resident, because Australian residents who did not give the purchaser a clearance certificate also have amounts withheld. Nothing on the row gives the sale price, the gain or whether the seller ended up with a refund.
rationale: The DIL label names the capital gains credit for foreign resident capital gains withholding amounts, which is item 18 label X. The ATO instructions state the start date of the rules, who withholds and where the credit is claimed.
evidence_quote: Foreign resident capital gains withholding applies to certain transactions entered into on or after 1 July 2016.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item D14 label F
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item D14
variable_description: A deduction for payments the person made into a forestry managed investment scheme. The ATO allows it only where "the forestry manager advises you that the FMIS satisfies the 70% direct forestry expenditure rule in Division 394 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997." An initial participant loses the deduction if they dispose of the interest within four years of the income year of their first payment, and borrowing costs, interest, stamp duty and GST are excluded.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction covering initial and ongoing scheme payments for an initial participant, and ongoing payments only for a subsequent participant.
limitation: It records the deduction claimed, not the money invested: a subsequent participant's acquisition cost is outside it, as is any borrowing used to fund the payment. A clawback on early disposal lands in a different year, so a large claim here is no guarantee the deduction survived.
rationale: The DIL label names the forestry managed investment scheme deduction, which is item D14 on the supplementary return. The ATO instructions give the label, the eligibility test and the excluded payments.
evidence_quote: You can only claim a deduction at this question if the forestry manager advises you that the FMIS satisfies the 70% direct forestry expenditure rule in Division 394 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 .
