supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item 23 label A
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 23
variable_description: Income the person received from a forestry managed investment scheme, including thinning and harvest proceeds. The ATO directs the taxpayer to show "the total income from forestry interests you hold in an FMIS" at item 23 label A, and to bring in the market value of the interest, rather than any cash, where a capital gains tax event ends or reduces their holding. It is the income leg of the same investment the D14 deduction pays for.
value_definition: A whole-dollar total covering thinning receipts and, where a capital gains tax event happens, the market value of the interest given up or the reduction in its market value.
limitation: Much of the amount can be a market valuation rather than money received, so it is not a cash flow measure and a large figure need not mean a large payout. It only reaches this item where a deduction was claimed or claimable, so scheme investments with no deduction history are invisible here.
rationale: The DIL label names forestry managed investment scheme income, which is item 23 on the supplementary return. The ATO instructions define what the label carries for initial and subsequent participants.
evidence_quote: Show at question 23 – label A the total income from forestry interests you hold in an FMIS from the following activities: Initial participants Subsequent participants .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Expenses label U
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Expenses
variable_description: Expenses the sole trader incurred directly in earning income that was subject to foreign resident withholding. The ATO puts them in the non-primary production column only, saying "You'll not have any primary production expense amounts at this question", and carries the figure to the totals box at label U. It is the deduction side of the gross foreign resident withholding payments reported on the same row.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount excluding anything relating to foreign resident capital gains withholding, and already included in the total expenses figure on the same row.
limitation: Because it is inside total expenses, adding the two together counts the same spending twice. The allocation of costs to one income stream is the taxpayer's own, so a business with mixed income can put very different amounts here without changing anything real.
rationale: The DIL label names the total foreign resident withholding expenses, which is P8 Expenses label U. The ATO instructions give the label, the single column it uses and the exclusion of capital gains withholding.
evidence_quote: Write your total non-primary production foreign resident withholding expenses at Foreign resident withholding expenses (excluding capital gains) in the Non-primary production column, P8 Expenses in your schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar and cent amount reported at tax return item 13 label A
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, item 13 Part F
variable_description: The person's share of tax withheld inside a partnership or trust under the foreign resident withholding rules. The ATO directs it to item 13 label A where the distribution includes income the person derives "as a foreign resident from which an amount of tax is withheld because of the operation of the foreign resident withholding rules". In the current form the same label also absorbs non-resident withholding tax and managed investment trust withholding, so the box is now wider than its original wording.
value_definition: A dollars-and-cents credit, being the person's share of amounts withheld before the partnership or trust distributed the income, claimed against their own assessment.
limitation: The label widened over time to take in managed investment trust and non-resident withholding, so a series stacked across years is not one consistent quantity even though the column name never changed. The figure is a credit, not income, and the underlying gross distribution is at labels O, U or C on the same row.
rationale: The DIL label names the share of credit for amounts withheld from foreign resident withholding, which is item 13 label A. The ATO Part F instructions define what the label now carries and show that it also absorbs two other withholding types.
evidence_quote: derive as a foreign resident from which an amount of tax is withheld because of the operation of the foreign resident withholding rules, then write the total amount of these credits for amounts withheld at question 13 – label A (show cents)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item D9 label J
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item D9
variable_description: The total the person claimed as a deduction for gifts and donations. The claim is tightly bounded: "To claim a deduction for gifts or donations you make, you need a receipt from an organisation that has a deductible gift recipient (DGR) status", and the gift must be $2 or more. Contributions to registered political parties, independent candidates and independent members go here too. Donations made under a salary sacrifice arrangement, and payments where the giver got something in return, cannot be claimed at all.
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of deductible gifts, taking in workplace giving already shown on the income statement and up to $10 of unreceipted bucket donations.
limitation: It measures deductible giving, not giving: donations to non-deductible causes, crowdfunding appeals and religious tithing sit outside it, so it understates generosity by an unknown and probably uneven amount. It is a self-assessed claim, so it records what was put on the return rather than what was substantiated.
rationale: The DIL label names gifts or donations, which is item D9. The ATO instructions state the receipt and deductible gift recipient requirement, the $2 floor, the political contribution rules and the exclusions.
evidence_quote: To claim a deduction for gifts or donations you make, you need a receipt from an organisation that has a deductible gift recipient (DGR) status.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of beneficiary tax offset applied in the assessment
value_source: ATO, Beneficiary tax offset
variable_description: The part of the beneficiary tax offset that was actually used to reduce the person's tax, not the part they were entitled to. The offset exists so that certain Australian Government allowances attract no tax when they are the person's only income. Nothing here is claimed by the taxpayer: "We will automatically calculate the tax offset when we process your tax return." Because the offset is not refundable, the used amount is capped by the tax otherwise payable.
value_definition: A whole-dollar offset amount worked out by the ATO from the qualifying Australian Government allowance and payment income declared on the return and the person's other taxable income, then limited to the tax that would otherwise be payable.
limitation: It is the offset used, so it understates entitlement whenever tax payable is the binding constraint, and it is exactly zero for the people whose incomes are lowest. Where a person qualifies for both this and the seniors and pensioners tax offset only the larger one is applied, so a zero can mean the other offset won rather than that no entitlement existed.
rationale: The DIL label names the government allowance beneficiary tax offset used, and the ATO page for that offset states who receives it, that the ATO calculates it, that tax must be payable for it to be used, and how it interacts with the seniors and pensioners offset.
evidence_quote: We will automatically calculate the tax offset when we process your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Whole-dollar gross payment amount on the PAYG payment summary - individual non-business
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Gross pay the employer reported for the person on a PAYG payment summary, before any tax was withheld. The ATO tells payers to "Include all salary, wages, bonuses and commissions you paid your payee as an employee, company director or office holder. Include the total gross amount before amounts are withheld." Anything shown separately on the summary as an allowance, a lump sum payment or a reportable fringe benefits amount stays outside this figure, and salary-sacrificed amounts are left out entirely.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount for one payer over one reported period, reported by the employer rather than the employee, alongside a period start and end date on the same row.
limitation: It covers one job over one period, so a person with several employers has several rows and no single row is their annual employment income. Because salary sacrifice is stripped out before reporting, the figure understates what the employer paid for the person and understates their pre-sacrifice earnings by an amount that never appears anywhere on the row.
rationale: The table this variable sits in carries the individual non-business income type, lump sum A to E and total allowances fields of the PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, and the ATO instructions for that form define the gross payments box.
evidence_quote: Include all salary, wages, bonuses and commissions you paid your payee as an employee, company director or office holder. Include the total gross amount before amounts are withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item 10 label L
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 10
variable_description: All the interest the person received or was credited from Australian sources during the year. The ATO requires it gross of withholding: where a bank took TFN amounts because no tax file number was given, "You must show these amounts as gross interest in your tax return." Interest distributed through a partnership or trust belongs at item 13 instead, and foreign interest at item 20. Joint account holders show only their own share.
value_definition: A whole-dollar total across all Australian sources, taking in ATO interest on early payments and overpayments and interest on children's accounts the person effectively controls.
limitation: It is not all the interest a household earned: cash management trust and other trust distributions sit elsewhere, and totals under $1 are not written at all. The share of a joint account is self-allocated, so two people can split the same account unevenly and neither return shows the account balance.

evidence_quote: TFN amounts are amounts of tax withheld by financial institutions because you didn't give them your TFN or ABN. TFN amounts show on your statement or document as 'Commonwealth tax' or 'TFN withholding tax'. You must show these amounts as gross interest in your tax return.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income, labour hire and specified payments totals box

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at tax return item 1, Income column
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, item 1
variable_description: The person's total salary and wages for the year, added across every income statement and payment summary. The ATO scopes item 1 as income "from salary or wages where tax was withheld", which takes in commissions, bonuses, part-time and casual work, parental leave pay, and lost-wage payments under income protection, sickness and accident or workers compensation arrangements. Allowances are excluded and belong at item 2. The label is a calculated total, so it aggregates the payer rows rather than naming one employer.

supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label O

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label N
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: Labour hire and specified payments the sole trader attributed to farming, fishing or forestry work. rationale: The DIL label names gross labour hire or other specified payments, primary production, which is P8 Income label N. The ATO income instructions state directly that the label is expected to be left blank.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label B
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income

value_domain: Dollar amount reported in the primary production column of the P8 foreign resident withholding income row
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: Farming, fishing or forestry income the sole trader reported as subject to foreign resident withholding. The current schedule has no such box: the ATO gives only a non-primary production step, saying "Add up all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule derived from non-primary production activities that have an F in the Type box", and the total is transferred straight from label B. The column appears in the 2006-07 extract with a handful of occurrences and does not carry forward, so it reads as an artefact of the older form layout.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label F
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: Non-farm contracting income the sole trader received under a pay as you go voluntary agreement to have tax withheld. The ATO defines the pair as "the total income you receive that is subject to a voluntary agreement to withhold tax and include the tax withheld", and label F is the non-primary production half. A voluntary agreement is an arrangement between a payer and an independent contractor who has quoted an ABN, and the credit is claimed at item 15 label D.
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount inclusive of withheld tax, built by adding payment summary schedule rows typed V that came from non-primary production activities.
limitation: A voluntary agreement is optional for both parties, so the column measures contracting income where the two sides chose to withhold rather than contracting income generally. Contractors doing identical work without an agreement show the same money as other business income, which makes this a poor base for estimating self-employment.
rationale: The DIL label names gross payments under a voluntary agreement, non-primary production, which is P8 Income label F. The ATO income instructions define the amount and the ATO payment summary guidance defines a voluntary agreement.
evidence_quote: The amounts you show at P8 Income – labels E and F is the total income you receive that is subject to a voluntary agreement to withhold tax and include the tax withheld.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income label E
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: Farming, fishing or forestry income the sole trader received under a pay as you go voluntary agreement to withhold tax. It is built by adding "all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule derived from primary production activities that have a V in the Type box." The primary production half is kept separate because that income later runs through the income averaging rules.

limitation: The primary production classification is the taxpayer's own, applied when they complete the payment summary schedule, so the split can shift between years without anything real changing. A blank does not distinguish a person with no voluntary agreement from one who put all of it in the other column.
rationale: The DIL label names gross payments under a voluntary agreement, primary production, which is P8 Income label E. The ATO income instructions give the exact addition and the type-box coding.
evidence_quote: Add up all the Gross payment amounts on your completed payment summary schedule derived from primary production activities that have a V in the Type box. Write the total at P8 Income – label E in your schedule.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of tax on taxable income before offsets
value_source: ATO, Reference material for Taxation statistics 2023-24, Calculating net tax
variable_description: Tax on the person's taxable income at the rate scale, before any tax offsets and before the Medicare levy. The ATO's own arithmetic for individuals starts from this figure: "Net tax = Tax on taxable income + Extra income tax − Total non-refundable tax offsets + Medicare levy + Medicare levy surcharge − Remaining foreign income tax offset". Gross tax is the first term, so the gap between it and net tax is the entire offset and levy structure. The ATO calculates it from the return rather than the taxpayer entering it.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount produced by applying the resident or foreign resident rate scale for that income year to taxable income, together with any extra income tax.
limitation: It is not what the person paid: offsets, the Medicare levy, the surcharge and withholding credits all sit between this and the assessment outcome, so someone with a large gross tax can still finish the year with a refund. Rate scale and threshold changes mean the same taxable income produces different gross tax in different years, so the column is not comparable over time without adjusting for the schedule.
rationale: The DIL label is gross tax, and the ATO taxation statistics reference material sets out the individual net tax formula in which tax on taxable income is the opening term, which fixes where gross tax sits in the assessment.
evidence_quote: Net tax = Tax on taxable income + Extra income tax − Total non-refundable tax offsets + Medicare levy + Medicare levy surcharge − Remaining foreign income tax offset
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount reported at BPI schedule P8 Income, voluntary agreement totals box
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 Income
variable_description: All income the sole trader received in the year under pay as you go voluntary agreements to withhold tax. It is the totals box of the pair: "Add up the amounts you show at P8 Income – labels E and F , and write the total in the adjacent Totals box." The figure is gross of the tax withheld, and the person claims the withheld amount back at item 15 label D on the supplementary return.
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross total combining the primary production and non-primary production voluntary agreement labels on the same row.
limitation: It is the sum of the two columns beside it, so using all three together counts the same dollars repeatedly. It cannot be turned into a count of agreements or payers, because one figure covers however many the person had.
rationale: The DIL label names the total gross payments under a voluntary agreement at P8. The ATO income instructions give the addition that produces the totals box and where the credit is claimed.
evidence_quote: Add up the amounts you show at P8 Income – labels E and F , and write the total in the adjacent Totals box.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Number of days with a spouse in the income year
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details
variable_description: How much of the income year the person had a spouse, where the relationship did not run the whole year. The return records dates rather than a count: if the person did not have a spouse for the full year they "print X in the No box at label L and write the dates you have a spouse in 2024–25 at labels M and N." This column carries the length of that period. Spouse covers married, registered and de facto relationships alike.
value_definition: A day count derived from the from and to dates at labels M and N, bounded by the 1 July to 30 June income year.
limitation: Only the last spouse of the year is described, so a person with two relationships in one year has the earlier one hidden entirely. A full-year relationship leaves the dates blank, so a missing value is not a zero-days case and the full-year flag on the same row is what separates the two.
rationale: The DIL label names part-year spouse days, and the ATO spouse details instructions give the labels the dates are written at, the trigger for writing them and the last-spouse rule.
evidence_quote: If you don't have a spouse for the full income year, print X in the No box at label L and write the dates you have a spouse in 2024–25 at labels M and N .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Yes or no indicator reported at tax return spouse details label L
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details
variable_description: Whether the person had a spouse for the whole income year. The instruction is direct: "If you have a spouse for the full income year, 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025, print X in the Yes box at label L." A no sends the person to the date labels on the same row. The ATO uses the answer with spouse income to work out the private health insurance rebate, the seniors and pensioners tax offset, any Medicare levy reduction and the Medicare levy surcharge.
value_definition: A single flag for a full-year spouse relationship, covering married, registered and de facto partners under the ATO's definition.
limitation: It is not a partnership status variable for the whole population: a person with no spouse at any time leaves the entire section blank, so blanks mix single people with people who simply did not complete it. The ATO definition turns on a registered relationship or living together on a genuine domestic basis, which will not always match how a household survey would classify the same couple.
rationale: The DIL label is the full-year spouse question, and the ATO spouse details instructions give the label, the wording, the alternative path and what the ATO uses the answer for.
evidence_quote: If you have a spouse for the full income year, 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025, print X in the Yes box at label L .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of compulsory study and training loan repayment raised on the assessment
value_source: ATO, Compulsory repayments
variable_description: The compulsory study and training loan repayment the ATO raised on the person's assessment for that year. The taxpayer does not work it out: "If you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment." Repayment income is wider than taxable income, adding reportable fringe benefits and total net investment loss.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount computed by the ATO from repayment income against the thresholds and rates for that income year, and added to the assessment rather than reported on the return.
limitation: It is not what the person paid across the year: employers withhold extra amounts against the loan through pay as you go, and those withholdings appear as tax withheld rather than here. A zero has three distinct causes that cannot be told apart, being no loan, income below the threshold, and a Medicare levy reduction that switches the obligation off.
rationale: The DIL label names the Australian HELP assessment debt raised for the year. The ATO compulsory repayments page states that the ATO calculates the repayment, puts it on the notice of assessment, and defines repayment income and the exemptions.
evidence_quote: If you have a loan when you lodge your tax return and your repayment income is above the minimum repayment threshold, we will work out your compulsory repayment and include it on your notice of assessment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of outstanding collectable study and training loan debt
value_source: ATO, Compulsory repayments

The column name expands to higher education loan programme collectable debt outstanding amount. It is an ATO account balance rather than anything the taxpayer writes on the return, and it does not move with each pay: "Your loan balance doesn't reduce after each pay cycle; it is only applied as a lump sum after your income tax return is lodged."

rationale: The DIL label names the HELP collectable debt outstanding amount. The ATO compulsory repayments page describes the outstanding loan balance, when employer withholdings are applied to it, and its relationship to compulsory and voluntary repayments.
evidence_quote: Your loan balance doesn't reduce after each pay cycle; it is only applied as a lump sum after your income tax return is lodged.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of outstanding repayable study and training loan balance (2017-18 extract)
value_source: ATO, Compulsory repayments

Voluntary repayments are additional to the compulsory one and "will not impact your compulsory repayment" while a balance remains and repayment income is above the threshold, so paying extra reduces the balance without reducing the amount raised on the assessment. Several columns in these extracts describe a loan balance and the custodian's wording repeats across them.

A balance cannot be read as debt incurred in the year, because it accumulates over a whole study history.
rationale: The DIL label names the HELP outstanding repayable amount. The ATO compulsory repayments page describes how the outstanding balance behaves under compulsory and voluntary repayments.
evidence_quote: You can also make additional voluntary repayments . These repayments will not impact your compulsory repayment if: you still have an outstanding loan
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Dollar amount of repayable HELP debt (2020-21 extract)
value_source: ATO, Compulsory repayments
variable_description: The balance of the person's HELP debt that remains repayable, as named in the later extracts. The compulsory repayment is worked out against this balance and stops when the balance clears; the threshold has since moved, and "From the 2025–26 income year, you only need to make a compulsory repayment when your repayment income exceeds $67,000", calculated only on income above that point. The column is a later name for the outstanding balance rather than a new quantity.

value_domain: Registered private health insurer identifier (ATO health insurer ID)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
variable_description: A code identifying the health insurer that held the person's private health insurance policy. The return copies it straight from the insurer's statement: "Transfer the health insurer ID at label B on your statement to label B Health insurer ID in your tax return." The ATO uses the policy details to work out the person's share of the private health insurance rebate, which becomes either a tax offset or a liability. This is the single-policy version of the field carried in the 2009-10 extract.

rationale: The DIL label names the private health insurance health fund identifier. The ATO instructions for the private health insurance policy details section give the label, its source on the insurer's statement and what the ATO does with it.
evidence_quote: Transfer the health insurer ID at label B on your statement to label B Health insurer ID in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Registered private health insurer identifier for the first policy row (ATO health insurer ID)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
variable_description: The health insurer code on the first private health insurance row of the person's return. A person can report up to four rows and the ATO insists they stay apart: "Transfer all rows of information separately to your tax return, as they appear on your PHI statement. Don't combine the rows of information." Most statements show two rows for a single policy split at 1 April, so the first and second codes often name the same insurer.
value_definition: A short insurer code taken from the first row of the private health insurance statement, sitting alongside the membership number, premiums, rebate received and benefit code for that row.
limitation: Two populated code columns usually mean two premium periods for one policy rather than two insurers, so counting non-blank codes overcounts policies. A blank second code is not evidence that nothing changed during the year, since a person with more than four rows lodges the rest on a separate schedule.
rationale: The DIL label names the first private health insurance health fund identifier. The ATO instructions describe the multiple rows, the rule against combining them and the pre and post 1 April split.
evidence_quote: Transfer all rows of information separately to your tax return, as they appear on your PHI statement. Don't combine the rows of information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Registered private health insurer identifier for the second policy row (ATO health insurer ID)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
variable_description: The health insurer code on the second private health insurance row of the person's return. A second row usually exists because the rebate percentage changes on 1 April: "One row relates to premiums you pay and rebates you receive before 1 April, and the other row relates to premiums you pay and rebates you receive on or after 1 April." It names a genuinely different insurer only where the person switched funds or held more than one policy.
value_definition: A short insurer code taken from the second row of the private health insurance statement, with its own membership number, premiums, rebate and benefit code on the same row.
limitation: Where the person did change insurer this column names the later fund but nothing records when the change happened, so it cannot be used to date a switch. It is also blank for someone who held one policy for part of the year only, so a blank cannot be read as continuous single-fund cover.
rationale: The DIL label names the second private health insurance health fund identifier. The ATO instructions explain why a statement carries two rows and what each row covers.
evidence_quote: In most cases, there will be 2 rows of information on your PHI statement. One row relates to premiums you pay and rebates you receive before 1 April, and the other row relates to premiums you pay and rebates you receive on or after 1 April.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label as its description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said what the number means for a taxpayer.

value_domain: Health insurer identifier reported at label B, third policy row
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
variable_description: The insurer shown on the third row of the taxpayer's private health insurance statement, copied onto the return. The ATO instruction is "Transfer the health insurer ID at label B on your statement to label B Health insurer ID in your tax return", and each row covers one policy for one premium period, so a typical single-policy household fills only the first two rows. A code here therefore usually means a second policy, a change of insurer during the year, or cover held by more than one member of the family.
value_definition: A short insurer code issued by a registered private health insurer, one per statement row. The paper return holds four rows; anything beyond that goes on a separate schedule of additional information.
limitation: It names the insurer and nothing about the cover. The level of hospital or extras cover, the people insured and the excess are all absent, and a blank third code means the person had fewer than three statement rows rather than no insurance.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the private health insurance policy details question defines the health insurer ID label, states that rows are transferred one by one, and caps the return at four rows, which is what makes a third row meaningful.
evidence_quote: Transfer the health insurer ID at label B on your statement to label B Health insurer ID in your tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said what a health fund identifier is or why the return numbers them one to four.

value_domain: Health insurer identifier reported at label B, fourth policy row
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Private health insurance policy details
variable_description: The insurer shown on the fourth and last policy row the return itself can hold. The ATO tells taxpayers with more rows than this to lodge a schedule: "If you have more than 4 rows of information on your statement, you'll need to provide a Schedule of additional information". A value here marks a taxpayer with a complicated year of cover, most often two policies each split across the 1 April premium change. It is the same kind of insurer code as the first three columns, not a different classification.
value_definition: A short insurer code issued by a registered private health insurer, in the fourth of the four policy rows the return provides.
limitation: Because the return runs out of rows at four, this column is also where truncation begins: a person with five or more rows has the rest on paper, so the set of insurer codes on the row is not necessarily the person's full set of policies for the year.
rationale: The same ATO instruction defines the health insurer ID and states the four-row limit and the overflow schedule, which is what separates the fourth column from the third.
evidence_quote: If you have more than 4 rows of information on your statement, you'll need to provide a Schedule of additional information .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that this is the last policy row on the form and that further policies spill onto a schedule.

value_domain: CGT exemption, rollover or additional discount code (single letter)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 18 Capital gains, label M
variable_description: A letter naming which capital gains tax concession the taxpayer used, chosen from a fixed list of exemptions and rollovers. The ATO says to "Write in the code box at label M the code from the following list that represents the CGT exemption, rollover or additional discount that produced the largest amount of capital gain or capital loss deferred or disregarded". The list runs from the small business concessions (A to D) through scrip for scrip and demerger rollovers to the main residence exemption (I) and a catch-all X.
value_definition: A single letter from the ATO's published CGT exemption and rollover list, valid only where the yes-or-no column on the same row is set. Codes were added over time, so the letters available in a year follow that year's instructions.
limitation: Only one code is recorded even when several concessions were applied, and the code is chosen by size of the amount deferred or disregarded rather than by importance. It also carries no dollar figure, so it cannot tell you how much gain the concession removed.
rationale: The ATO's item 18 instructions publish the code list for this exact label and state the rule for choosing between codes when more than one applies.
evidence_quote: Write in the code box at label M the code from the following list that represents the CGT exemption, rollover or additional discount that produced the largest amount of capital gain or capital loss deferred or disregarded.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the code comes from a published list, or that a taxpayer using several concessions reports only the largest.

value_domain: Yes or no answer at question 18 label M
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 18 Capital gains, label M
variable_description: Whether the taxpayer applied any capital gains tax exemption or rollover during the year, answered yes or no. The ATO's test is that you tick yes "If you applied an exemption or rollover to disregard, defer a capital gain or capital loss or you qualified for and applied the additional affordable housing discount to reduce a capital gain". A yes is what makes the code column on the same row meaningful; the two are answered together at the one label.
value_definition: A two-state self-assessed indicator against question 18 label M. The set of concessions that count as a yes widened over time, most recently with the affordable housing discount.
limitation: A yes says a concession was claimed, not that it was correct or that the Commissioner accepted it, and there is no dollar amount attached. A no can still sit beside a large net capital gain, because the ordinary 50% discount is not an exemption or rollover for this purpose.
rationale: The item 18 instruction defines the yes condition for label M and pairs it with the code box, which is the neighbouring column.
evidence_quote: If you applied an exemption or rollover to disregard, defer a capital gain or capital loss or you qualified for and applied the additional affordable housing discount to reduce a capital gain, write X in the Yes box at question 18 Capital gains – label M in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which concessions count as a yes, or that the 50% general discount is not one of them.

value_domain: Compulsory study and training loan repayment worked out for the year (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Study and training loan repayment thresholds and rates
variable_description: The compulsory repayment towards an Australian study or training loan that the ATO worked out from the taxpayer's repayment income for the year. It is a calculated figure, not a claim: the ATO says that from 2025-26 "your compulsory repayment is calculated only on the income above the minimum repayment threshold". The word maximum in the label reads as the amount before it is trimmed to whatever the person still owes, so it can exceed the repayment actually raised. Read it with the repayment income column on the same row, which is what the rate scale is applied to.
value_definition: A dollar amount produced by applying the year's repayment rate scale to repayment income. Until 2024-25 the scale applied a single percentage to the whole of repayment income; from 2025-26 it applies marginal rates to the part above the threshold, so the level of the amount is not comparable across that change.
limitation: It is not the balance of the loan, and it is not what reached the loan account: an actual repayment is capped at the outstanding debt, and voluntary repayments and the extra tax withheld through the year are recorded elsewhere. A zero can mean no loan at all or a loan with income below the threshold.
rationale: The ATO page publishes the repayment rate scale, the definition of repayment income the scale runs on, and the fact that the ATO rather than the taxpayer works the repayment out. The reading of maximum as the pre-cap figure is an inference from the label and is flagged as such.
evidence_quote: From the 2025–26 income year, compulsory repayments are calculated using marginal rates. This means your compulsory repayment is calculated only on the income above the minimum repayment threshold.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is calculated by the ATO from the rate scale rather than reported by the taxpayer.

value_domain: Repayment income for study and training loans (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Study and training loan repayment thresholds and rates
variable_description: The income figure the ATO uses to decide whether a study or training loan repayment is due and how large it is. It is deliberately wider than taxable income: "Your repayment income amount is calculated by adding up all of the following amounts" - taxable income, reportable fringe benefits, total net investment loss, reportable super contributions and exempt foreign employment income. Someone who negatively gears or salary sacrifices therefore has a repayment income above their taxable income on the same return.
value_definition: A dollar amount built from five components of the return, all added back before the thresholds are applied. It is worked out for every lodger, whether or not they hold a loan.
limitation: It is a test income, not a measure of cash received, so it double counts nothing but includes amounts the person never had in hand, such as a rental loss added back. It also says nothing about the loan itself, so it cannot distinguish a HELP debt from a VET Student Loan or an apprenticeship loan.
rationale: The ATO rates page defines repayment income by listing its components and shows the thresholds it is compared against, which is exactly what this column holds.
evidence_quote: Your repayment income amount is calculated by adding up all of the following amounts: taxable income (excluding any assessable First Home Super Saver (FHSS) released amounts), reportable fringe benefits (regardless of the exempt status of your employer), total net investment loss (including net rental losses), reportable super contributions, exempt foreign employment income amounts.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that repayment income adds fringe benefits, investment losses and super contributions back onto taxable income.

value_domain: Cost of intangible depreciating assets first deducted (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, intangible depreciating assets first deducted
variable_description: The cost of intangible business assets, such as patents, in-house software and mining rights, that the sole trader began writing off for the first time this year. The ATO asks for "the cost of all intangible depreciating assets that you're claiming a business deduction for decline in value for the first time", and says not to reduce that cost for private use. It is an investment measure rather than a deduction: the deduction itself sits in the business expense labels.
value_definition: A dollar amount summed across all of the person's businesses, at full cost before any apportionment for non-taxable use. Assets under $1,000 put into a low-value pool are included here as well.
limitation: A small business entity using the simplified depreciation rules leaves this label blank however much software or intellectual property it bought, so a zero does not mean no intangible investment. The item number on the schedule has moved between editions, so it cannot be used to line the column up across years.
rationale: The schedule instruction defines what this label holds, states the cost basis, and says small business entities using simplified depreciation do not complete it.
evidence_quote: At P17 Intangible depreciating assets first deducted you need to show the cost of all intangible depreciating assets that you're claiming a business deduction for decline in value for the first time .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the figure is a cost of newly deducted assets rather than a deduction, or that simplified-depreciation users skip it.

value_domain: Termination value of intangible depreciating assets (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, termination value of intangible depreciating assets
variable_description: What the business got for intangible assets it stopped holding or using during the year, such as software or a patent sold, lost or scrapped. The ATO defines the amount as follows: "Generally, the termination value is the amount you receive or are deemed to receive for the asset that you stop holding or using." Non-cash consideration counts at market value, and a non-arm's length sale is brought back to market value. It pairs with the first-deducted cost column as the disposal side of the same asset class.
value_definition: A dollar amount summed over all intangible assets disposed of across the person's businesses, gross of any balancing adjustment. It is proceeds, not profit.
limitation: The gain or loss on disposal is not here: the balancing adjustment worked out against the asset's adjustable value is dealt with in the reconciliation labels. Assets in the general small business pool, low-cost assets written off immediately, and software in a development pool are all excluded, so this understates disposals for a pooling business.
rationale: The schedule instruction defines termination value for this label and lists what is excluded from the total.
evidence_quote: Generally, the termination value is the amount you receive or are deemed to receive for the asset that you stop holding or using.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that termination value is disposal proceeds, or which pooled assets are left out of the total.

value_domain: Deceased estate flag on the return
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, completing individual information
variable_description: Whether this return was lodged on behalf of someone who had died, rather than by the taxpayer. The ATO's instruction is that "If you're completing a tax return for someone who has died: write Deceased estate on the top of page 1 in the tax return", and the executor or administrator signs it. The return still covers the person's own income up to the date of death.
value_definition: A flag on the return record, set where the return is lodged for a person who has died. Its natural companion is the answer to whether an Australian return will be needed in future, which the same instruction says to mark as no.
limitation: It marks the return, not the death: there is no date of death here, and a final return can be lodged in the financial year after the person died, so the flag can appear in a later year than the death. Income the estate earns after death goes on a separate trust return and never appears on this row.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the individual information section is where the deceased estate marking is defined and says who signs the return.
evidence_quote: If you're completing a tax return for someone who has died: write Deceased estate on the top of page 1 in the tax return
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the flag marks a return lodged by an executor rather than a recorded date of death.

value_domain: ATO salary and wage occupation code (6 digits)
value_source: ATO, Salary and wage occupation codes
variable_description: The occupation the taxpayer nominated for their main wage or salary job, as a six-digit code. The ATO requires that you "provide an accurate description of the main salary and wage occupation at question 1 of the individual tax return and insert the appropriate 6-digit code", and where a person has more than one job the code describes the one that pays most. The codes follow the ABS occupation classification, so an ambulance officer is 411111 and an unlisted job is 999000.
value_definition: A six-digit code from the ATO's published salary and wage occupation list, keyed to the ANZSCO structure. Codes are revised year to year as the published list is reissued.
limitation: It covers wage and salary work only, so a sole trader, a retiree or an investor with no employment income carries no meaningful code, and 999000 is a genuine answer rather than a missing value. Because the taxpayer or their agent picks the code, it records how the job was described at lodgment, not an audited occupation.
rationale: The ATO publishes the code list for this label and states the six-digit format, the main-job rule and the not-listed fallback.
evidence_quote: You must provide an accurate description of the main salary and wage occupation at question 1 of the individual tax return and insert the appropriate 6-digit code from the list at question 1 – label X .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the code is six digits from a published ATO list and describes only the person's main wage job.

value_domain: Sex or gender recorded on the ATO client record
value_source: ATO, Update your gender (tax file number registration details)
variable_description: The sex the ATO holds for the taxpayer, carried onto the return record from their tax file number registration rather than asked as a question on the form. The register is not limited to two states: "You also have the option to record your gender (sex) as indeterminate in your ATO record." Changing it requires documents such as a passport, a birth certificate or a practitioner's statement, so the value is sticky and lags a person's own change.
value_definition: A short code for sex or gender as registered with the ATO. Male, female and indeterminate are the states the ATO documents; the stored characters are not published.
limitation: It is a registration attribute, not a statement made in the year of the return, so it can be out of date and it changes only when the person lodges documents. It is also not a sex recorded at birth nor a Census-style gender question, so it should not be treated as either.
rationale: The ATO page on updating gender establishes that the ATO holds sex or gender against the tax file number record, names indeterminate as an available state, and sets out the evidence needed to change it. That the income tax return record inherits the value rather than asking the question is an inference from the return forms, which carry no such question.
evidence_quote: You also have the option to record your gender (sex) as indeterminate in your ATO record.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said where the value comes from, or that the ATO records a third state alongside male and female.

value_domain: Decoded sex or gender label from the ATO client record
value_source: ATO, Update your gender (tax file number registration details)
variable_description: The sex or gender the ATO holds for the taxpayer, stored as a readable label rather than as a code. The underlying record is the ATO's own registration attribute, which the ATO will change only on documentary evidence and which can also be set to indeterminate. It appears in a later year of the return tables than the coded column, and where both appear they are two renderings of one field rather than two variables.
value_definition: A decoded text label for sex or gender, such as the words the ATO uses for male, female and indeterminate. The exact strings are not published.
limitation: Decoding hides a distinction the code kept: an unknown, a not-stated and a genuine indeterminate can all resolve to similar text, so the label cannot be used to count non-binary registrations. Comparing it across years to the coded column risks reading a change of storage as a change of population.
rationale: The same ATO page supports what the underlying register holds and how it is changed. That the DCD suffix marks a decoded rendering of the coded column is an inference from the pair of variables sitting in the same table family.
evidence_quote: We can't change your recorded gender (sex) over the phone unless we have recorded it incorrectly from an identity document supplied at registration.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that this is the decoded twin of the coded sex column rather than a separate measure.

value_domain: Medicare levy reduction amount (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
variable_description: The dollar amount by which this person's Medicare levy was cut because family income was low, worked out by the ATO rather than claimed. The ATO states plainly: "We work out the reduction for you, using your spouse details and number of dependent children." Eligibility rests on the combined taxable income of the person and their spouse and on how many dependent children they have, which is why the label describes an individual share of a family entitlement.
value_definition: A dollar amount subtracted from the 2% levy on taxable income, tapering to zero as family taxable income rises through the year's threshold band.
limitation: A reduction is not an exemption: a person exempt on medical or foreign residence grounds records that at a different label and can show nothing here. The amount also gives no reading of family income, because two families at different incomes inside the taper can produce the same reduction.
rationale: The M1 instruction sets out the family taxable income test, the dependent children count and the fact that the ATO calculates the reduction from the spouse details on the return.
evidence_quote: We work out the reduction for you, using your spouse details and number of dependent children.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the reduction is calculated by the ATO from family taxable income, or how it differs from an exemption.

value_domain: Spouse's gender as reported in the spouse details section
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The gender the taxpayer reported for their spouse in the spouse details section of their own return. The instruction is explicit about the categories: "Print X in the relevant box for your spouse's gender (male, female or indeterminate). Indeterminate includes non-binary." The ATO asks for it to help match the spouse to their own record, so it sits with the spouse's name, date of birth and taxable income on the same row.
value_definition: A three-state code for male, female or indeterminate, reported by the taxpayer about another person. It exists only on returns where a spouse is declared for part or all of the year.
limitation: It is a report about someone else, so it can disagree with what the spouse records on their own return, and it is not evidence of how the spouse identifies. Its absence means no spouse was declared for the year, which is not the same as being single on 30 June.
rationale: The spouse details instruction names the three categories for this exact box and explains why the ATO collects it.
evidence_quote: Print X in the relevant box for your spouse's gender (male, female or indeterminate ). Indeterminate includes non-binary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that a third category exists or that the answer is given by the taxpayer about their spouse.

value_domain: Franking credit amount at question 11 label U (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 11 Dividends
variable_description: The company tax already paid on the taxpayer's franked dividends, reported at the franking credit label and known in older wording as an imputation credit. The ATO defines it as follows: "Franking credits are amounts of tax paid by the company that are allocated to your dividend or distribution." It counts twice on the return, once as assessable income and once as a credit: "You also receive a tax credit on your tax assessment for an amount equal to the franking credits."
value_definition: A dollar amount taken from dividend statements, added to the franked and unfranked dividend labels on the same row and also carried to the credits side of the assessment.
limitation: It is not a payment the person received, so treating it as cash income overstates their means, and treating it as tax paid by them attributes a company's tax to a household. It is also not automatic: the holding period, related payments and dividend washing rules can deny it, and the label does not record whether they applied.
rationale: The question 11 instruction defines franking credits, states that they are both assessable and creditable, and names the rules that can deny them.
evidence_quote: Franking credits are amounts of tax paid by the company that are allocated to your dividend or distribution.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is company tax attributed to the shareholder and appears on both sides of the assessment.

value_domain: Small business share of taxable income used for the offset (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
variable_description: The part of the person's taxable income the ATO attributed to unincorporated small business, used to work out their small business income tax offset. The ATO describes the mechanism as follows: "The offset is worked out based on the proportion of tax payable relating to your total net small business income", built from sole trader net small business income plus any share from a small business partnership or trust. The proportion is capped at one, so this amount never exceeds taxable income on the same row.
value_definition: A dollar amount derived by the ATO from the return, not a label the taxpayer fills in. It is net of business deductions, excludes salary, wages and net capital gains, and is treated as zero when the business made a loss.
limitation: It is a calculation input, not income the person can spend, and it is not added to taxable income anywhere. It also exists only for years and turnovers in which the offset ran, so a blank can mean an ineligible business rather than none: the turnover threshold was $2 million in 2015-16 before rising to $5 million.
rationale: The ATO offset page defines net small business income, the proportion used and the eligibility thresholds by year, which is what this derived column measures.
evidence_quote: The offset is worked out based on the proportion of tax payable relating to your total net small business income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is an ATO-derived input to the small business income tax offset rather than reported income.

value_domain: Total income or loss on the return (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Subtotal
variable_description: Everything the taxpayer declared as income for the year, added up before any deduction is taken off. The return works down from it: the ATO says to "subtract the amount at Total deductions from the amount at Total income or loss" and write the result at Subtotal, which after earlier-year losses becomes taxable income. It gathers the twelve income questions on the main return and the supplement total on the same row.
value_definition: A dollar amount, the sum of the income labels across the main return and the supplement, which can be negative and is then flagged as a loss.
limitation: It is a gross figure, so it is not a measure of what the household kept: a sole trader with $400,000 of turnover-driven income and $390,000 of deductions looks wealthy here and poor at taxable income. It also excludes non-assessable amounts such as most redundancy tax-free components and many government payments, so it is not total receipts either.
rationale: The subtotal instruction states the arithmetic relationship between this line, total deductions and the rest of the assessment, which is what fixes its meaning as a pre-deduction total.
evidence_quote: subtract the amount at Total deductions from the amount at Total income or loss
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the figure is measured before deductions and sits above taxable income in the return's arithmetic.

value_domain: Income reconciliation adjustment at P8 label X (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 reconciliation items
variable_description: The bridge between the business's accounting income and its taxable income, added or subtracted at the reconciliation label. The ATO puts the arithmetic simply: "Your income reconciliation adjustment is your total income add-backs less your total income subtractions." Add-backs are assessable amounts missing from the accounts, such as balancing adjustments on asset disposals; subtractions are book income that is exempt or not assessable. The figure is the total of the primary production and non-primary production columns and can be negative.
value_definition: A dollar amount, signed, that is the net of add-backs and subtractions across both production columns. Its sibling column at label H does the same job for expenses.
limitation: It measures a difference between two accounting bases, so its size says nothing about the size of the business, and a large adjustment is a sign of accounting treatment rather than of profitability. A zero does not mean the accounts and the tax law agreed, because add-backs and subtractions can cancel out.
rationale: The P8 reconciliation instruction defines the adjustment, lists the add-backs and subtractions that make it up, and names the label it is written at.
evidence_quote: Your income reconciliation adjustment is your total income add-backs less your total income subtractions.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount reconciles accounting profit to taxable income and can be negative.

value_domain: Total supplement income or loss (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, Total supplement income or loss
variable_description: The income total from the supplementary return, covering the parts of a person's affairs the main return does not reach. The ATO builds it by adding "all the income amounts in the right-hand column of questions 13, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23 and 24" and subtracting the losses from partnerships and trusts, farm deposits, foreign income and rent. It is then carried to label I on the main return, which is where it joins wages, interest and dividends in total income or loss.
value_definition: A dollar amount, signed, that nets the supplement's income and loss questions. It is present only where the person lodged a supplementary return.
limitation: It is a mixed bag rather than a category: business, rent, capital gains, foreign income and one-off other income all land in the one number, so a change in it cannot be read as a change in any of them. A blank means no supplement was lodged, not that the person had no investments.
rationale: The ATO instruction lists exactly which supplement questions are added and subtracted to form this line and where it is transferred.
evidence_quote: Add up all the income amounts in the right-hand column of questions 13 , 17 , 18 , 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 , 23 and 24 in your supplementary tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which questions feed the total, or that losses on the supplement are netted off within it.

value_domain: Financial year of the return (income year)
value_source: ATO, Foreign income return form guide, glossary entry Income year
variable_description: The financial year the return reports on, which for individuals runs from 1 July to 30 June. The ATO's own definition allows for exceptions: an income year "is, in effect, a 12-month period ending on 30 June, or a 12-month period ending on another date where the Commissioner has approved that other date under section 18 of the Act". It is the year the income was earned, not the year the return was lodged or assessed.
value_definition: A year identifier for a 1 July to 30 June period, usually stored as the ending year or as a paired label such as 2010-11.
limitation: It is not a lodgment date and not a payment date, so a return for an early year can be lodged years late and still carry that year here. Amended assessments also keep the original income year, so a row cannot tell you which version of the assessment it reflects.
rationale: The ATO glossary gives the statutory meaning of an income year, including the substituted accounting period exception, which is what this column identifies.
evidence_quote: An income year - or year of income - is, in effect, a 12-month period ending on 30 June, or a 12-month period ending on another date where the Commissioner has approved that other date under section 18 of the Act.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the year is the year income was earned rather than the year the return was lodged.

value_domain: Yes or no answer on internet selling
value_source: ATO, Trust tax return instructions 2014, question 4 Did you sell any goods or services using the internet?
variable_description: Whether the business used the internet to take orders, take payment or deliver what it sold, answered yes or no on the business and professional items schedule. The ATO drew the line at transacting rather than having a web presence: you tick no if you used the internet only to "advertise your goods or services, give support to your customers, buy your stock, do your banking". The question ran on the individual, partnership and trust returns and was dropped from the schedule in later years.
value_definition: A two-state self-assessed indicator. The cited wording is the trust return's version of the identically worded question, because the individual schedule's own page has been retired from the ATO site.
limitation: It is a yes-or-no about method, so it measures neither how much was sold online nor whether the business had a website; a shop taking one order by email answers the same as a full online retailer. Because the question was removed from the schedule, a blank in later years means the question was not asked rather than that the answer was no.
rationale: The ATO page for the identically worded question on the trust return sets out both the yes conditions and the narrower no conditions, which is what fixes the meaning of the individual schedule's label. The individual schedule's own instruction page for this item is no longer served.
evidence_quote: Print X in the No box at Q , if you used the internet only to: advertise your goods or services, give support to your customers, buy your stock, do your banking.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said where the line between selling online and merely advertising online was drawn.

value_domain: Interest deductions claimed at question D7 (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question D7 Interest income deductions
variable_description: What the taxpayer claimed as the cost of earning interest income, such as account fees and interest on money borrowed to invest. The ATO ties the claim to the income it produced: "To claim a deduction for interest income expenses, you must incur expenses in earning interest from any source in Australia." Deductions against dividends go to the next question instead, and interest costs inside a business, a rental property or a trust distribution are claimed elsewhere again.
value_definition: A dollar amount claimed against the gross interest label on the same return. Joint account holders show only their own share.
limitation: It is a self-assessed claim, not an audited expense, and it is not the interest the person paid on their home or their business loans. The narrowness matters: the interest on a margin loan against shares belongs at the dividend question, so a small figure here does not mean small investment borrowing.
rationale: The D7 instruction defines the deductible expenses for this label and states which interest costs belong at other questions.
evidence_quote: To claim a deduction for interest income expenses, you must incur expenses in earning interest from any source in Australia.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which costs qualify or that dividend-related interest belongs at a different question.

value_domain: Combined interest and dividend deductions on the earlier return (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, questions D7 and D8
variable_description: One combined claim for the costs of earning both interest and dividends, as the earlier editions of the return recorded them in a single item. The current return splits the same ground across two questions, D7 for interest income deductions and D8 for dividend deductions, and the ATO's apportionment rule shows they are treated as one pool of investment cost: a shared computer's decline in value is claimed "once, at either question D7 or D8". A series that spans the split therefore has to add the two later columns to match this one.
value_definition: A dollar amount covering account fees, investment advice and borrowing costs against both interest and dividend income, before the return separated the two.
limitation: It cannot be decomposed: nothing in the row says how much of the claim belonged to shares as against deposits, which is exactly the split later returns record. Comparing it directly with the later interest-only column understates the earlier years' investment costs.
rationale: The current D7 and D8 instructions define the two deductions and show that the ATO treats them as one apportionment pool, which is what makes a combined earlier column readable. That this column is the combined earlier item is inferred from the custodian's own label wording rather than from a published page.
evidence_quote: you can claim only the proportion of the decline in value relating to managing those investments once, at either question D7 or D8
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the column combines two claims the later return reports separately.

value_domain: Overseas interest expenses at P8, total column (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses
variable_description: Interest the business paid to overseas lenders, totalled across its primary production and non-primary production activities. The schedule keeps two columns and one total: "Add up your primary production and non-primary production overseas interest expenses and write the total at label R." It is deliberately separated from interest paid within Australia, which sits in its own label on the same schedule, because overseas interest carries withholding and thin capitalisation consequences.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, the sum of the two production columns on the expenses page of the schedule. Label letters have moved between editions of the schedule.
limitation: It is business interest only, so a sole trader's investment or home borrowing never reaches it, and it does not say whether withholding tax was paid or whether a debt deduction was later denied. A denial under the thin capitalisation rules is added back in the reconciliation labels, leaving this figure unchanged.
rationale: The P8 expenses instruction names this label, states that it is the total of the two production columns, and separates it from interest paid within Australia.
evidence_quote: Add up your primary production and non-primary production overseas interest expenses and write the total at label R .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount totals two production columns, or why overseas interest is reported apart from domestic interest.

value_domain: Yes or no answer on interests in foreign entities
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 19 Foreign entities
variable_description: Whether the taxpayer had a controlling interest in a foreign company or had moved property or services to a non-resident trust. The controlled foreign company test is a control test, not an income test: the ATO asks whether you have "direct or indirect controlling interests totalling 10% or more in a foreign company" or effective control of one. The transferor trust question is answered separately at the same item, and each yes opens an attributed income label beside it.
value_definition: A self-assessed indicator against the foreign entities question. On the current return the two limbs are two boxes; this column carries the answer without separating them.
