limitation: A yes says control or a transfer existed, not that any income was attributed, and a taxpayer can answer yes with a nil attributed amount. Simply holding foreign shares, a foreign bank account or an interest below the control threshold produces a no, so it is not a marker of foreign investment.
rationale: The question 19 instruction sets out both limbs of the foreign entities question, the 10% control test and the attributed income labels that follow a yes. Which limb a single combined indicator reflects is not published, and that is stated rather than assumed.
evidence_quote: direct or indirect controlling interests totalling 10% or more in a foreign company
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the question turns on a 10% control test and on transfers to non-resident trusts.

value_domain: Australian interest expenses at P8, total column (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses
variable_description: Interest the business paid to Australian lenders, totalled across primary production and non-primary production. The schedule adds the two columns into one figure: "Add up your primary production and non-primary production interest expenses within Australia and show the total at label Q." For most sole traders it is the largest financing cost on the schedule and the counterpart to the overseas interest label beside it.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, the sum of the two production columns. It is the deduction claimed in the accounts, before any reconciliation adjustment.
limitation: It says nothing about how much was borrowed or at what rate, and it excludes non-business interest, which is claimed at the personal deduction questions instead. Because a sole trader can hold the same loan for mixed purposes, the split between this label and personal interest reflects the taxpayer's own apportionment.
rationale: The P8 expenses instruction names this label and states that it is the total of the primary production and non-primary production columns.
evidence_quote: Add up your primary production and non-primary production interest expenses within Australia and show the total at label Q .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is a business financing cost totalled over two production columns.

value_domain: Income from investment, partnership and other sources at question A3 label F (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question A3 Government super contributions
variable_description: The taxpayer's non-employment income, worked out for the government super co-contribution test rather than for tax. The ATO's step is to "Transfer the amount at row y to question A3 - label F Income from investment, partnership and other sources", gathering interest, dividends, franking credits, trust and partnership distributions, foreign income, rent and life insurance bonuses. It sits opposite the employment and business income label, and the pair decide whether at least 10% of total income came from work.
value_definition: A dollar amount assembled from worksheets rather than transcribed from a single label, covering the investment and other income components of total income for co-contribution purposes.
limitation: It is not a component of taxable income and does not appear in the assessment, so adding it to income labels elsewhere on the return double counts. A zero can be a genuine nil or a code the taxpayer prints when the worksheet result is nil, so it cannot be read as an absence of investments.
rationale: The A3 instruction defines this label, lists the income types the worksheet collects for it, and explains the 10% employment income test it serves.
evidence_quote: Transfer the amount at row y to question A3 – label F Income from investment, partnership and other sources . If row y is 0 (zero), print C in the CODE box at label F .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is assembled for the super co-contribution income test rather than for the assessment.

value_domain: Small business share of income tax liability used for the offset (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Small business income tax offset
variable_description: The part of the person's basic income tax liability the ATO attributed to small business income, which is the base the offset percentage is applied to. The ATO caps what comes out of it: "Your offset will be your rate of offset of the following amount, up to the limit of $1,000." It is the tax counterpart of the small business share of taxable income on the same row, and the offset rate applied to it rose from 5% in 2015-16 to 16% from 2021-22.
value_definition: A dollar amount of tax, derived by the ATO from the return by multiplying basic income tax liability by the small business proportion, which is capped at one.
limitation: It is not the tax the person actually paid on their business, because the offset itself, other offsets, the Medicare levy and loan repayments all sit outside it. Nor is it the offset: the offset is a percentage of this amount and stops at $1,000, so two taxpayers with very different figures here can receive the same offset.
rationale: The ATO offset page sets out the calculation, the rate by year and the $1,000 cap, which together define what this derived tax figure is used for.
evidence_quote: Your offset will be your rate of offset of the following amount, up to the limit of $1,000.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the figure is an intermediate step in the small business income tax offset, not the offset or the tax paid.

value_domain: Total PAYG tax withheld reported on the return (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, Total tax withheld
variable_description: All the tax that payers took out of the person's income during the year and sent to the ATO, added up on the return. The ATO defines the line as follows: "Total tax withheld is the pay as you go (PAYG) withholding amounts withheld during the year by the payer from the amounts you declare as income at questions 1 to 9." It is a credit against the assessment rather than a tax, so a refund is the gap between it and the tax finally worked out.
value_definition: A dollar amount, the sum of the withheld column beside the first nine income questions. It covers wages, allowances, lump sums, termination payments, government payments and annuities.
limitation: It is not the person's tax for the year, and it is not the whole of what they remitted: PAYG instalments are credited separately and are explicitly kept off the return, and withholding on interest or dividends for a missing tax file number sits at those questions. Extra amounts withheld for a study loan are inside this figure and cannot be separated from ordinary withholding.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the line, names the questions that feed it and says instalments are not to be shown on the return.
evidence_quote: Total tax withheld is the pay as you go (PAYG) withholding amounts withheld during the year by the payer from the amounts you declare as income at questions 1 to 9.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the line is a credit built from the withheld column of the first nine questions rather than the person's tax.

value_domain: Landcare, water facility, fencing and fodder storage deduction at P8 label W (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 reconciliation items
variable_description: Capital spending on land and water improvements that farmers and some other businesses may write off, reported as one total on the business schedule. The ATO combines four things in the label: "Add up your primary production and non-primary production deductions for landcare operations, water facilities, fencing assets and fodder storage assets and write the total at label W." Landcare covers works such as levees, drainage and fencing to keep stock off degraded land, and it is deductible in the year it is incurred where the business is a primary producer.
value_definition: A dollar amount, the total of the primary production and non-primary production columns. Fencing and fodder storage components are available to primary producers only; landcare and water facilities can also reach a rural land irrigation water provider.
limitation: The four components cannot be told apart in the one figure, so it cannot be used to measure water infrastructure spending on its own. It is also a deduction rather than an outlay, and the immediate write-off means a single year's figure can reflect several years of building work finished at once.
rationale: The P8 reconciliation instruction defines each component of the label, states who can claim it, and gives the totalling rule for the two production columns.
evidence_quote: Add up your primary production and non-primary production deductions for landcare operations, water facilities, fencing assets and fodder storage assets and write the total at label W .
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that four different concessions are added into one label, or that the deduction is immediate rather than depreciated.

value_domain: Lease expenses at P8, total column (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Business and professional items schedule instructions 2025, P8 expenses
variable_description: What the business paid to lease plant, vehicles or premises during the year, totalled across primary production and non-primary production. The ATO draws a boundary that matters for anyone reading the figure as equipment finance: "Expenses you incur under a hire purchase agreement aren't lease expenses." Hire purchase is dealt with in the reconciliation labels instead, and a lease can also be caught by the thin capitalisation debt deduction rules.
value_definition: A dollar amount, the sum of the two production columns for lease payments claimed in the accounts.
limitation: It cannot separate a property lease from a car or equipment lease, so it is not a measure of business premises cost. Because hire purchase and chattel mortgage arrangements are excluded, a business that finances its plant that way can show nothing here while carrying substantial equipment.
rationale: The P8 expenses instruction defines the label, excludes hire purchase and states the totalling rule for the two production columns.
evidence_quote: Expenses you incur under a hire purchase agreement aren't lease expenses.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said what counts as a lease expense, or that hire purchase is excluded from the label.

value_domain: Life assurance bonus tax offset (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 22 Life insurance companies and friendly societies bonuses
variable_description: The tax offset that comes automatically with a life insurance or friendly society bonus declared on the return. The rule is fixed and the calculation is not the taxpayer's: "You'll get a tax offset equal to 30% of the amount you show at this question. We'll work out this tax offset for you." The 30% matches the tax the life company has already paid on the earnings inside the policy, so the offset is there to stop the same income being taxed twice.
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to 30% of the assessable bonus reported at question 22, worked out by the ATO rather than claimed.
limitation: It is a non-refundable offset, so a person with little tax payable does not receive the full 30% as cash, and the recorded amount can therefore overstate the benefit. It also cannot be read as a measure of policy earnings, because only part of a bonus is assessable in the ninth and tenth years of a policy.
rationale: The question 22 instruction states the 30% rate, that the ATO calculates the offset, and how much of a bonus is assessable in each policy year.
evidence_quote: You'll get a tax offset equal to 30% of the amount you show at this question. We'll work out this tax offset for you.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the offset is a fixed 30% of the declared bonus and is calculated by the ATO.

value_domain: Life insurance and friendly society bonuses at question 22 label W (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual supplementary tax return instructions 2025, question 22 Life insurance companies and friendly societies bonuses
variable_description: The assessable part of a bonus received on a life insurance policy or friendly society bond cashed in within ten years of starting it. How much counts depends on when it is taken: the whole bonus in the first eight years, "two-thirds of the bonus amount you receive in 2024-25 if you receive it during the 9th year of the policy", and one-third in the tenth year. Bonuses after the tenth year, and bonuses paid because the insured person died or surrendered the policy through illness or hardship, are not declared at all.
value_definition: A dollar amount already reduced to the assessable fraction for the policy year, so it is smaller than the bonus the person received in years nine and ten.
limitation: It is not the investment return on the policy and not the amount received: the two-thirds and one-third steps mean the same cash bonus produces different figures depending on timing. A blank is common even for policyholders, because a policy held past ten years produces no entry.
rationale: The question 22 instruction states the qualifying conditions, the fractions assessable by policy year and the exclusions, which is what the label holds.
evidence_quote: two-thirds of the bonus amount you receive in 2024–25 if you receive it during the 9th year of the policy
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is a tapered fraction of the bonus rather than the bonus itself.

value_domain: Local government area, ASGS non-ABS structure
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area the taxpayer's address falls in, coded to the ABS geography for the year on the table's name. It is a statistical approximation rather than the legal boundary: "Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory." It sits with the other geography columns from the same address, so it is the coarser partner of the statistical area codes on the same row.
value_definition: A code and name from the ASGS non-ABS structures, built from whole mesh blocks. LGA boundaries are reissued each year as councils change, and unincorporated areas have no council.
limitation: It is a place, not a jurisdiction the taxpayer dealt with, and the ABS warns that these approximations "should only be used for statistical purposes", so it must not be used to allocate rates or council entitlements. Because the address is the one the ATO held at the time, a person who moved mid-year is counted wholly in one council area.
rationale: The ABS standard defines local government areas as a non-ABS structure approximated from mesh blocks and states the statistical-use limitation.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory. ABS approximations of administrative boundaries do not match official legal boundaries and should only be used for statistical purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the boundaries are mesh block approximations of gazetted council areas rather than the legal boundaries.

value_domain: Deduction for the long-life small business pool (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Partnership tax return instructions 2010, item 5 Business income and expenses
variable_description: The write-off claimed on long-lived business assets that were pooled under the simplified small business depreciation rules. The pool held the slow-depreciating end of the asset base: "a long-life small business pool for depreciating assets with an effective life of 25 years or more", and the ATO's formula is "Long-life small business pool deduction = opening pool balance ($) X 5%", with half that rate in an asset's first year. Assets carried over from a general or long-life pool under the earlier simplified tax system kept the same treatment.
value_definition: A dollar amount, 5% of the opening pool balance plus 2.5% of assets first used during the year. It is one pooled figure, not an asset-by-asset calculation.
limitation: The individual assets behind the figure cannot be recovered, and disposals reduce the pool rather than showing up as a separate loss or gain. The pool is no longer available and the ATO now refers to it as formerly available, so a long run of this column stops without the underlying assets disappearing.
rationale: The 2010 partnership instructions publish the long-life pool definition, the 5% rate and the half rate in the first year, and the same pool and rate applied to sole traders through the business and professional items schedule.
evidence_quote: Long-life small business pool deduction = opening pool balance ($) X 5%
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said what the long-life pool held, at what rate it was written off, or that it has since closed.

value_domain: Lodgment channel for the return
value_source: ATO, How to lodge your tax return
variable_description: How the return reached the ATO: prepared by the taxpayer online, lodged through an agent, or sent in on paper. The ATO's own channels are myTax for self-preparers, a registered tax agent - "they are the only people that can charge a fee" - and the paper return lodged by mail, for which the ATO says most refunds issue within 50 business days. The channel matters for reading the rest of the row, because agent-lodged returns follow a later due date and pre-filled online returns carry fewer keying errors.
value_definition: A code for the lodgment channel. The ATO's public channels are self-prepared online, registered tax agent and paper, with older years including the retired e-tax software; the stored code list is not published.
limitation: It records the path the form took, not who did the work, so a taxpayer who pays an accountant to prepare a return they then lodge themselves is counted as a self-preparer. It also cannot date the lodgment, so it does not distinguish an on-time return from a late one.
rationale: The ATO page enumerates the lodgment channels available to individuals and what each involves, which is the domain this column codes. The mapping from the ATO's channel names to the stored codes is not published and is not asserted.
evidence_quote: Use a registered tax agent to prepare and lodge your tax return, they are the only people that can charge a fee.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which lodgment channels exist or why the channel changes how the return should be read.

value_domain: Low and middle income tax offset applied against tax (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Low and middle income earner tax offsets
variable_description: How much of the low and middle income tax offset was actually used to reduce the person's tax, as against how much they were entitled to. The offset was never claimed on the return: "You don't need to do anything to claim this tax offset, except lodge your tax return for the relevant year. We work out the offset after you lodge." It ran for four years only, and "The 2021-22 income year was the last year for the LMITO - it isn't available for 2023 onwards."
value_definition: A dollar amount, the part of the entitlement absorbed by tax payable. Entitlement ranged from $255 to $1,080 for 2018-19 to 2020-21 and from $675 to $1,500 for 2021-22.
limitation: Because it is the used amount, it understates entitlement for anyone whose tax payable was smaller than their offset, and it falls to zero for a person with no tax to pay however low their income. The offset was also non-refundable and unused amounts were never paid out, so the column cannot be read as a transfer received.
rationale: The ATO page states that the offset was calculated after lodgment, that it only reduces tax payable to zero, and the years it operated, which is what separates a used amount from an entitlement.
evidence_quote: The 2021–22 income year was the last year for the LMITO – it isn't available for 2023 onwards.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the offset was calculated by the ATO, ran only from 2018-19 to 2021-22, and could not be refunded.

value_domain: Low income tax offset (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Low income tax offset
variable_description: The low income tax offset worked out for the taxpayer from their taxable income, which reduces the tax they pay but is never paid as cash. Nothing is claimed for it: "We will work out your offset and reduce your tax payable by this amount", and it appears on the notice of assessment under non-refundable offsets. The current scale gives $700 up to a taxable income of $37,500 and tapers to nothing at $66,667; earlier years had different amounts and a separate low income offset for seniors.
value_definition: A dollar amount derived by the ATO from taxable income alone. The taper is a two-stage formula, so the amount is a deterministic function of taxable income within a year.
limitation: Its value cannot be compared across years without the year's scale, because the maximum and the cut-out have both moved, and for a time it interacted with the separate middle income offset. Being non-refundable, a positive amount here does not mean the person received money; it means tax that would otherwise have been payable was not.
rationale: The ATO page publishes the offset's income scale, states that the ATO calculates it after lodgment, and states that it cannot be refunded.
evidence_quote: We will work out your offset and reduce your tax payable by this amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is derived from taxable income by the ATO and cannot be refunded.

value_domain: Lump sum payment in arrears tax offset available (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Lump sum payment in arrears
variable_description: The lump sum payment in arrears offset the ATO worked out that the taxpayer was entitled to, before any of it was applied. The offset exists because back pay is taxed in the year it lands: "Lump sum payments in arrears (LSPIA) are assessable in the income year you receive the payment", which can push someone into a higher bracket for income they earned years earlier. The ATO calculates the entitlement from the year-by-year breakdown the payer supplies.
value_definition: A dollar amount produced by comparing tax on the arrears in the year received against tax had it been taxed in the years it accrued. It arises only where the arrears are at least 10% of threshold test income.
limitation: An available amount is an entitlement, not a benefit received, so it overstates what the person gained wherever their tax payable was smaller. It also does not identify what the back payment was for, so an underpayment settlement, a delayed pension and a reinstatement after suspension all look the same here.
rationale: The ATO page defines the offset, the assessability rule that creates the need for it, the 10% threshold test and the fact that the ATO works the amounts out from the return.
evidence_quote: Lump sum payments in arrears (LSPIA) are assessable in the income year you receive the payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said why the offset exists or that the available amount is an entitlement rather than a benefit.

value_domain: Lump sum payment in arrears tax offset applied against tax (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Lump sum payment in arrears
variable_description: How much of the lump sum payment in arrears offset was actually absorbed by the person's tax for the year. It is the applied twin of the available column on the same row, and the difference between them is entitlement that went unused because there was not enough tax to offset. The ATO does not publish the working: "As the calculations are complex and relate to each individuals' personal circumstances, there currently is no online calculator or detail we provide to explain the outcome."
value_definition: A dollar amount, at most equal to the available offset on the same row and at most the tax otherwise payable.
limitation: A zero here is ambiguous: it can mean no arrears were received, or that an entitlement existed but no tax was payable to apply it against. Because the ATO publishes no breakdown of the calculation, the used amount cannot be reproduced from the other columns on the return.
rationale: The ATO page establishes that the offset is calculated by the ATO from information in the return and that no explanation of the outcome is published, which is what separates an applied amount from an entitlement.
evidence_quote: As the calculations are complex and relate to each individuals' personal circumstances, there currently is no online calculator or detail we provide to explain the outcome.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is the part of the offset absorbed by tax payable rather than the entitlement.

value_domain: Lump sum payment in arrears tax offset entitlement, later table (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Lump sum payment in arrears
variable_description: The entitlement to the lump sum payment in arrears offset, sitting beside the column that records how much of it was used. Qualifying is a threshold test rather than a claim: "The eligible LSPIA amount must be 10% or more of your threshold test income in the income year you receive it" once earlier-year accruals and leave paid on termination are taken out. From 1 July 2024 the same arrears can also carry a Medicare levy exemption and a surcharge offset, which are separate amounts again.
value_definition: A dollar amount of entitlement for the income year, sitting on the same row as the used amount so that the two can be differenced.
limitation: It repeats a quantity the registry also holds under an older name in an earlier table, so summing the two across years counts one entitlement twice. It also covers the income tax offset only, not the Medicare levy exemption or the surcharge offset that the same arrears may attract.
rationale: The ATO page defines the offset and its 10% threshold test and lists the separate Medicare concessions that accompany it. That this column and the earlier available column are the same quantity under two names is inferred from the custodian's identical wording for both.
evidence_quote: The eligible LSPIA amount must be 10% or more of your threshold test income in the income year you receive it
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is the entitlement paired with the used column, or that it overlaps an identically described column in an earlier table.

value_domain: Lump sum A on the payment summary (dollars)
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused leave paid out on leaving a job, reported by the employer outside gross payments because it is taxed on its own basis. The ATO defines lump sum A as unused long service leave "that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993", unused holiday pay accrued before 18 August 1993, and any post-1993 unused leave paid with a genuine redundancy, early retirement or invalidity payment. Ordinary unused leave outside those cases is inside gross payments instead, not here.
value_definition: A dollar amount the payer shows in the lump sum A field for the income year, never inside gross payments. It carries a type code of R or T on the same statement.
limitation: It is a third-party report, so an employer's misclassification lands here uncorrected, and it is not a measure of leave taken or accrued. The accrual dates mean two people with identical payouts can report very different amounts here purely because of when their leave built up.
rationale: The ATO payment summary instructions define each lump sum type for the payer, which is where these amounts originate before they reach the return.
evidence_quote: unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which leave payments fall into lump sum A or that the accrual date decides it.

value_domain: Lump sum B on the payment summary (dollars)
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused long service leave from the oldest accrual period, paid out on leaving a job. The ATO defines lump sum B for payers as "Amounts you paid for unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978", and it is the whole payment as the employer reported it, even though only 5% of it is ever assessable. The return records the 5% rather than the whole, so this column and the return's lump sum B figure differ by a factor of twenty.
value_definition: A dollar amount, the full lump sum B payment reported by the employer for the income year, kept out of gross payments.
limitation: It is now a rare and shrinking amount because it depends on service before August 1978, so a zero says nothing about a person's long service leave. Reading it as taxable income overstates the tax effect twentyfold, since only 5% enters the assessment.
rationale: The ATO payment summary instructions define lump sum B for the payer by its accrual cut-off, and the individual return instructions set out the 5% treatment.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that lump sum B is pre-1978 long service leave and that only 5% of it is assessable.

value_domain: Lump sum D on the payment summary (dollars)
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The tax-free part of a redundancy payout, reported by the employer but never taxed in the employee's hands. The ATO defines lump sum D as "The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment", and the individual return instructions tell taxpayers not to include it anywhere on their return. It is the best single marker in this table of an involuntary job loss on redundancy terms.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the income year, set by a base amount plus a per-year-of-service amount that the ATO indexes each year, so the same redundancy yields different tax-free amounts in different years.
limitation: It is only the tax-free slice: the rest of the redundancy payout is an employment termination payment reported on a separate summary, so this column understates what the person received. It also cannot confirm the job ended involuntarily, since the payment must meet the genuine redundancy tests to be reported here at all.
rationale: The ATO payment summary instructions define lump sum D as the tax-free component of a genuine redundancy or early retirement scheme payment and direct employment termination payments to a separate summary.
evidence_quote: The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that lump sum D is a tax-free redundancy component and is excluded from the return.

value_domain: Lump sum E on the payment summary (dollars)
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Back pay for work done more than a year earlier, and return-to-work payments, reported separately from ordinary wages. The ATO defines lump sum E as "Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments." Separating it is what lets the ATO work out the lump sum payment in arrears offset, since the whole amount is taxed in the year it is paid.
value_definition: A dollar amount reported by the employer for the income year, kept out of gross payments and declared by the taxpayer at the other income question.
limitation: The years the pay relates to are not in this column, so the arrears cannot be reassigned to the years they were earned without the payer's separate breakdown. A large amount also does not imply a large offset, because the offset depends on the 10% threshold test and on the person's income in the earlier years.
rationale: The ATO payment summary instructions define lump sum E for the payer, and the return instructions direct these amounts to the other income question rather than to the lump sum question.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that lump sum E is back pay accrued more than twelve months earlier and is taxed in the year received.

value_domain: Assessable 5% of employer lump sum B at question 3 label H (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 3 Employer lump sum payments
variable_description: The taxable sliver of an old-style long service leave payout, being one twentieth of what the employer paid as lump sum B. The ATO's step is arithmetic: add up the lump sum B amounts on the payment summaries, then "Divide the total by 20. This is because only 5% is taxable." So the return carries the assessable 5%, while the payment summary tables carry the whole payment.
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to 5% of total lump sum B payments for the year, self-calculated by the taxpayer or their agent from payment summaries.
limitation: Multiplying it by twenty recovers the payment only if every lump sum B was reported and divided correctly, which is a keying step that the ATO does not verify against the payer data on this label. A zero is the usual case now, because lump sum B depends on service before August 1978.
rationale: The question 3 instruction gives the exact calculation for the label and states why only 5% is included.
evidence_quote: Divide the total by 20. This is because only 5% is taxable.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the figure is one twentieth of the payment, not the payment itself.

value_domain: Employer lump sum A at question 3 label R (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 3 Employer lump sum payments
variable_description: The unused leave paid out on leaving a job that the taxpayer declared on their return, added across every payment summary for the year. The ATO's step is to "Add up all lump sum A amounts on your income statements and payment summaries" and write the total at label R. Unlike lump sum B, the whole amount is assessable, and the type code printed beside it governs how it is taxed.
value_definition: A dollar amount aggregating all lump sum A amounts across employers for the income year. It is accompanied by a type code and by its own tax withheld figure.
limitation: It is the taxpayer's transcription of employer reports, so a missing payment summary quietly reduces it, and it is not an employment termination payment: redundancy pay itself is declared at the following question. Multiple job endings in one year are added together and cannot be separated.
rationale: The question 3 instruction defines what is declared at label R, how it is aggregated across payers, and what belongs at the following question instead.
evidence_quote: Add up all lump sum A amounts on your income statements and payment summaries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the label totals unused leave payouts across all employers and excludes termination payments.

value_domain: Tax withheld from lump sum A at question 3 (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 3 Employer lump sum payments
variable_description: The tax employers took out of the taxpayer's unused leave payouts, reported in the withheld column beside the lump sum A amount. The ATO instructs the taxpayer to "Add up the total tax withheld from lump sum A amounts on your income statements and payment summaries" and warns against double counting: "Don't include any amounts of tax withheld you include at any other question, such as question 1 or 2." It feeds the total tax withheld line and is therefore a credit, not a tax.
value_definition: A dollar amount, the sum across payers of tax withheld from lump sum A payments only. It sits in the left-hand withheld column of question 3.
limitation: It is not the tax finally borne on the leave payout, which is settled at assessment against the concessional rate, so a person can be refunded much of it. Because the split between this column and the wages withholding depends on how the taxpayer transcribed the summaries, misallocation between them changes neither the assessment nor the total.
rationale: The question 3 instruction defines this withheld column, tells taxpayers how to aggregate it and warns against including withholding reported at other questions.
evidence_quote: Add up the total tax withheld from lump sum A amounts on your income statements and payment summaries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is a withholding credit specific to lump sum A rather than tax finally payable on it.

value_domain: Tax withheld from lump sum B at question 3 (dollars)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 3 Employer lump sum payments
variable_description: The tax employers took out of old-style long service leave payouts, written in the withheld column beside the 5% assessable figure. The instruction is to "Add up the total tax withheld from lump sum B amounts on your income statements and payment summaries", so the amount is all the tax the payers withheld from lump sum B payments, while the income label beside it shows only one twentieth of those payments.
value_definition: A dollar amount, the sum across payers of tax withheld from lump sum B payments. The ATO requires payers to include everything they withhold from lump sum payments in total tax withheld, so it is a credit like any other withholding.
limitation: The withheld figure and the assessable figure beside it are not on the same base, so the ratio between them is not a tax rate and cannot be read as one. The column is also nearly always nil, because lump sum B itself depends on long service leave accrued before August 1978.
rationale: The question 3 instruction defines the withheld column for lump sum B and separately defines the divided-by-twenty income label, which is what makes the difference in bases visible.
evidence_quote: Add up the total tax withheld from lump sum B amounts on your income statements and payment summaries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the withholding is measured on the whole payment while the income label beside it is measured on 5% of it.

value_domain: Lump sum A type code (R or T)
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Why the unused leave payout was made, as a single letter that decides how it is taxed. The payer sets it and the taxpayer copies it onto the return: "R - if the payment was made for a genuine redundancy, invalidity or under an early retirement scheme", and "T - if the payment was made for any other reason." The code, not the amount, is therefore what separates a redundancy from an ordinary resignation on this row.
value_definition: A one-letter code, R or T, valid only where a lump sum A amount is present. The ATO instructs payers to leave the box empty when there is no lump sum A.
limitation: It classifies the payment, not the separation, so a person made redundant can still show T where the payer coded it that way, and the code cannot be checked against any other column on the row. An empty code means no lump sum A was paid rather than an unknown reason for leaving.
rationale: The ATO payment summary instructions define the two valid codes and when the type box is left blank, and the individual return instructions repeat the same choice at question 3.
evidence_quote: R – if the payment was made for a genuine redundancy, invalidity or under an early retirement scheme. T – if the payment was made for any other reason.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said what the R and T codes mean or that they decide the rate of tax on the payout.

value_domain: Dollar amount of PAYG tax withheld, item 24 label E
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question 24 Other income
variable_description: Tax already withheld by the payer from a back-payment of salary, wages or a pension that covers an earlier year. The ATO instructions for question 24 say: "If you received lump sum payments in arrears, write the amount of tax withheld from these payments at question 24 - label E." The taxpayer copies the figure from a payment summary or income statement, so it is a payer-reported number rather than a self-assessed one, and arrears from a superannuation income stream go to question 7 instead.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of PAYG withholding, shown separately from the arrears income itself, which sits in the category 1 box at label Y on the same return.
limitation: It is a credit against tax, not the size of the back-payment, and it says nothing about which earlier years the arrears related to. The lump sum payment in arrears tax offset, which the ATO works out to undo the bracket effect, is a different quantity and is not in this column.
rationale: The custodian label names other income tax withheld on lump sum payments in arrears, which is a single defined box at question 24 of the supplementary return, and the ATO instructions state exactly what goes in it.
evidence_quote: If you received lump sum payments in arrears, write the amount of tax withheld from these payments at question 24 - label E.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's abbreviated wording and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said this was a withholding credit rather than income.

value_domain: Dollar amount, total loss recorded on the return
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals 2008 (NAT 2541)
variable_description: A total loss amount held against the return, present only in the 2006-07 to 2008-09 income and loss tables. The individual return records losses by writing a positive figure in the box and printing L in the adjacent LOSS box, so the ATO's data model needs a separate field to carry the magnitude of a negative total. Its neighbours on the same row are total income or loss and taxable income or loss, both of which use that LOSS-box convention.
value_definition: A dollar amount with no sign, whose negative reading is carried by a companion indicator rather than by the number itself.
limitation: No published ATO label matches this wording, so which total the loss belongs to is not established, and the field cannot be paired confidently with a specific return item. Three tables carry it and none of the later ones do, so it cannot support a series.
rationale: No ATO label is named 'loss amount total'. The reading rests on the return's LOSS-box convention and on the columns that sit beside it in the same table, not on a published definition.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's wording and repeated the generic sentence twice; it now at least records that the field is an unsigned loss magnitude of uncertain scope.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at D10 label L
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question D10 Cost of managing tax affairs
variable_description: The deduction a person claimed for going to court or the tribunal over their own tax affairs. The ATO instructions say litigation costs "include: court fees, Administrative Appeals Tribunal fees, solicitor, barrister and other legal costs", and the same question splits into interest charged by the ATO at label N and all other tax-management expenses at label M. The amount is self-assessed and first appeared as its own label on the 2017-18 return, when D10 was broken into three boxes.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction claimed at one of the three D10 boxes, comprising fees and legal costs incurred in disputing or appealing a tax matter.
limitation: A claim is not proof of a dispute reaching a tribunal or court, since the same box absorbs preparatory legal advice, and the deduction is allowed on the taxpayer's own say-so unless audited. The column exists in the 2015-16 and 2016-17 tables, before the three-box split, so any values there were not collected under this label and cannot be compared with later years.
rationale: The label is a defined box at question D10, and the current ATO instructions set out what belongs in it and how it is separated from the other two D10 components.
evidence_quote: You can claim a deduction for the litigation costs you incurred in managing your tax affairs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's label text with the generic no-value-list sentence in both the definition and limitation slots, so it did not say what a litigation cost is or when the label began.

value_domain: Dollar amount claimed at D6 label K
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question D6 Low-value pool deduction
variable_description: The deduction a person claimed for the decline in value of cheap work or rental assets that were grouped into a single pool. The ATO defines the entry price: "Low-cost assets are depreciating assets that cost less than $1,000", and a low-value asset is one whose opening adjustable value has fallen below $1,000. The pool is written down at 37.5% a year, or 18.75% in the year an asset joins it, so the claim is a formula output rather than an amount spent.
value_definition: A whole-dollar deduction, being the pooled decline in value for the year multiplied by the taxpayer's estimated business or work-use percentage for each asset.
limitation: It cannot be read as spending on equipment this year, because the pool carries assets bought in earlier years and applies a fixed rate to the closing balance. A person who claims here is barred from claiming the same assets at D1 to D5 or at the rent question, so a zero can mean the assets were claimed elsewhere.
rationale: D6 is a single defined label with published thresholds and pooling rates, and the ATO instructions give both the definition of a low-cost asset and the calculation.
evidence_quote: Low-cost assets are depreciating assets that cost less than $1,000.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label 'Low value pool deduction' and gave the generic sentence twice, so it never explained the $1,000 threshold or that the amount is a pooled write-down.

value_domain: Dollar amount of carried-forward tax offset claimed at label T
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question T6 Landcare and water facility
variable_description: The unused landcare and water facility tax offset from earlier years that a person applied against this year's tax. The ATO says the question "applies only if your income tax liabilities from earlier years have not absorbed all of the excess or unused landcare and water facility tax offset available to you", and that "there is no limit to the number of years you can carry forward any balance". The item number moved over time, from T11 on the 2011 supplementary return to T6 on the 2024 one, but the label letter T stayed put.
value_definition: A whole-dollar non-refundable tax offset, drawn from a balance struck in an earlier assessment rather than from expenditure incurred this year.
limitation: A figure here is not evidence of landcare or water facility investment in the reference year, because only carried-forward balances reach this label. It also cannot be summed across years without double counting the same original entitlement.
rationale: The T6 instructions define the label as a carry-forward claim and state the eligibility test, which is exactly what the custodian's label names.
evidence_quote: There is no limit to the number of years you can carry forward any balance of landcare and water facility tax offset.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label name and printed the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so a reader could not tell that this is a carry-forward and not a current-year claim.

value_domain: Dollar balance of unused tax offset carried to later years
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question T6 Landcare and water facility
variable_description: The landcare and water facility offset still unused after this year's tax was worked out, which the person can carry into later years. The ATO tells taxpayers where to find it: "The amount of your excess or unused tax offset is shown on your notice of assessment or amended notice of assessment". It is therefore an assessment output rather than a return label, and it is the closing stock matching the opening claim held in LWF_TAX_OFST_AMT.
value_definition: A whole-dollar closing balance, reduced by any offset absorbed this year and by 30 cents for each dollar of unused net exempt income.
limitation: It is a stock at a point in time, so adding it across years counts the same entitlement repeatedly, and a fall between years does not by itself mean the offset was used because exempt income can also erode it. Missing years in the table series mean the balance cannot always be tracked continuously.
rationale: The T6 page names the carried-forward balance, says where it is reported and gives the exempt-income reduction rule, which is the quantity the custodian's abbreviated label describes.
evidence_quote: The amount of your excess or unused tax offset is shown on your notice of assessment or amended notice of assessment for the year ending 30 June 2023.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the truncated custodian text 'L care water reb cr fwd amount' with the generic sentence twice, which told a reader nothing about what a carried-forward balance is.

value_domain: ASGS mesh block code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The mesh block covering the address the ATO held for the taxpayer, present only in the 2022-23 context table. The ABS defines them as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" which "form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)". The custodian's description names the ASGS 2016 edition, and the LGA, SA1 and SA2 columns on the same row are that one address coded to coarser units of the same standard.
value_definition: A mesh block identifier from the ASGS, assigned by geocoding a single address; ASGS Edition 3 has 368,286 of them including 114 non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: A mesh block marks land use, not a household or a population, and the ABS notes that SA1 is generally the smallest unit at which Census data is released, so counts at mesh block level can be unstable or suppressed. The address is the one on the return, so it locates the person at lodgment rather than through the income year.
rationale: The ABS is the publisher of the classification the value comes from and defines the unit; the ATO does not publish a definition because the geography is added by the ABS after linkage.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's fragment 'Asgs 2016 meshblock' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing on the page said whose address the mesh block was or how small the unit is.

value_domain: ASGS 2021 mesh block code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The 2023-24 version of the taxpayer's address mesh block, coded to the ASGS 2021 boundaries used across that table. The SA1, SA2, SA3 and SA4 columns beside it all carry the same 2021 suffix, and the row also holds a truncated hash of the address register identifier, so the set is one address geocoded to a single ASGS edition. The ABS describes mesh blocks as areas that "broadly identify land use such as residential, commercial, primary production and parks".
value_definition: A mesh block identifier from ASGS Edition 3 (July 2021 to June 2026), the edition whose boundaries the 2021 Census was output on.
limitation: The custodian's description text still reads ASGS 2016 while the column name and every sibling column say 2021, so the carried metadata contradicts the schema and should not be used to date the boundaries. Boundaries also changed between editions, so this column and the earlier MB column are not the same areas.
rationale: The ABS defines the unit, and the ASGS edition is read from the column naming used consistently across the 2023-24 table rather than from the stale description text.
evidence_quote: They broadly identify land use such as residential, commercial, primary production and parks.
supersedes_rationale: The entry inherited the same 'Asgs 2016 meshblock' text as the older column and repeated the generic sentence, so the edition conflict was invisible and the two mesh block columns looked identical.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net medical expenses tax offset
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals (supplementary section) 2008 (NAT 2679), item T9
variable_description: The offset a person received on out-of-pocket medical expenses above the annual threshold, held only for the 2006-07 and 2007-08 tables. The 2008 supplementary return carried the entitlement as item T9, printed as the "20% tax offset on net medical expenses over the threshold amount", so only the excess above the threshold attracted relief and only at twenty cents in the dollar. The gross expense figure it was worked out from is a separate column, MDCL_EXPNSS_NET_TOTL_AMT.
value_definition: A whole-dollar offset amount equal to a fixed percentage of net medical expenses above the year's threshold, after reimbursements from Medicare and health funds are taken off.
limitation: It measures relief, not health spending, and a zero is ambiguous between no expenses and expenses that never cleared the threshold. Only two tables carry it, and the offset was later restricted and then abolished, so it cannot anchor a long series of medical costs.
rationale: No live ATO page remains for this retired offset, so the label wording comes from the ATO's own supplementary return form for 2011, which still carried the item and its percentage.
evidence_quote: T9 20% tax offset on net medical expenses over the threshold amount
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording with a stray closing quotation mark and the generic sentence twice, so it never said the offset was a percentage of the excess over a threshold.

value_domain: Dollar amount of net medical expenses reported at label X
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals (supplementary section) 2016 (NAT 2679), item T5
variable_description: The medical expenses a person reported for the offset test, after subtracting refunds from Medicare and private health funds. What counted narrowed sharply: by 2016 the label read "Total net medical expenses for disability aids, attendant care or aged care", where earlier years accepted general medical and dental costs. The figure is self-assessed from receipts, and the offset the ATO then worked out sits in MDCL_EXPNSS_TAX_OFST_AMT.
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of eligible expenses net of reimbursements, reported at label X of the supplementary return's medical expenses item.
limitation: It is not household health spending, because reimbursed amounts are stripped out and, from 2015-16, only disability aids, attendant care and aged care qualified, so a series across that change measures two different things. People with expenses below the threshold had no reason to report accurately, or at all.
rationale: The custodian's label names the total net medical expenses box, and the ATO's own return forms show both the label letter and how its scope was narrowed.
evidence_quote: T5 Total net medical expenses for disability aids, attendant care or aged care
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Total net medical expenses' and gave the generic sentence twice, so the narrowing of scope after 2012-13, which breaks the series, was not recorded anywhere.

value_domain: Dollar amount of medical expenses offset worked out by the ATO
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals (supplementary section) 2019 (NAT 2679), item T5
variable_description: The medical expenses offset the ATO calculated as available to the taxpayer, as distinct from the expenses they reported. The offset was progressively wound back and the 2019 supplementary return was the last to carry a medical expenses item, printed there at item T5 as "Total net medical expenses for disability aids, attendant care or aged care"; the 2020 form carries no medical expenses item at all. The column nevertheless persists in tables through to 2023-24, where it should be empty.
value_definition: A whole-dollar non-refundable offset amount derived by the ATO from the reported net expenses, the applicable threshold and the applicable rate for the year.
limitation: It is not a claim and not a payment; it is what was available, so it can exceed the tax actually reduced when the person had little tax to pay. Because the column outlives the offset by several years, a zero in a late table reflects abolition rather than a taxpayer circumstance.
rationale: The ATO's own return forms bracket the life of the offset, showing a medical expenses item on the 2019 supplementary return and none on the 2023 one, which dates the column's useful range.
evidence_quote: T5 Total net medical expenses for disability aids, attendant care or aged care
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Medical expenses offset available' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not separate the offset from the expenses and did not flag that the column runs on past the offset's abolition.

value_domain: Count of days, 0 to 366, at M1 label V
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
variable_description: The number of days in the year for which a person claimed to owe no Medicare levy at all. The ATO instruction is direct: "Write the number of days you were covered for a full exemption at question M1 - label V." Three categories qualify, covering defence and veteran medical entitlement, foreign residency and people not entitled to Medicare benefits, and the half-exemption days claimed under the same item sit in a separate column.
value_definition: A whole number of days from 0 to 366, capped so that overlapping qualifying periods are counted once and any overlap between full and half periods is treated as full.
limitation: It records what the taxpayer claimed, not what was allowed, since the ATO says it works out the entitlement afterwards. It also does not say which of the three exemption categories applied, so defence personnel, foreign residents and people without Medicare entitlement are indistinguishable here.
rationale: M1 label V is a single defined box and the ATO instructions state the counting rule, the 366-day cap and the overlap treatment.
evidence_quote: The maximum total number of days you can claim is 366. If you have overlapping qualifying periods, count the days in those overlapping periods only once.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label and printed the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so neither the 0 to 366 range nor the claim-not-assessment status was stated.

value_domain: Medicare levy exemption claim type code (M1 CLAIM TYPE box)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
variable_description: A one-letter code printed beside the full-exemption days box to flag a particular kind of claim. For 2023-24 the ATO gives a single instruction for it: "If you were a temporary resident for Medicare purposes and have a Medicare Entitlement Statement from Services Australia covering a period in 2023-24 (see Category 3), then print C in the CLAIM TYPE box." Everyone else leaves it blank, so the column is mostly empty by design and appears only from the 2009-10 table onward.
value_definition: A single character drawn from a very short list, sitting beside the day counts at M1 rather than carrying an amount of its own.
limitation: A blank does not mean no exemption was claimed, because most claimants are told to leave the box empty, so the code cannot be used to identify who was exempt. It also does not distinguish the medical, foreign resident and no-Medicare-entitlement categories from one another.
rationale: The M1 instructions describe the CLAIM TYPE box that sits with label V and give the one code currently in use, which is the box the custodian's label names.
evidence_quote: If you don't fall within this category, leave the CLAIM TYPE box blank.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Medicare levy full exemption - claim type' with the generic sentence twice and no values, so a reader had no way to know the box is deliberately blank for most claimants.

value_domain: Count of days, 0 to 366, at M1 label W
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M1 Medicare levy reduction or exemption
variable_description: The number of days for which a person claimed to owe only half the Medicare levy, typically because a dependant was not covered by their own exemption. The ATO instruction is: "Write the number of days you were covered for a half exemption at question M1 - label W." A half exemption normally arises through a family agreement with a spouse over shared dependants, so this column often depends on the other partner's circumstances rather than the taxpayer's own.
value_definition: A whole number of days from 0 to 366, counted so that any day that also qualifies for a full exemption is recorded as full rather than half.
limitation: Full and half days cannot simply be added to get a total exempt period, since the levy relief differs by a factor of two, and the overlap rule pushes shared days into the full column. Like the full-exemption count, this is a claim rather than the ATO's assessed entitlement.
rationale: M1 label W is a defined box, and the ATO instructions describe both the count and the family-agreement circumstances that produce a half rather than a full exemption.
evidence_quote: If a full exemption period overlaps a part exemption period, count the overlapping days as a full exemption period.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the label and gave the generic sentence twice, so it did not explain what half exemption means or why the days cannot be added to the full-exemption days.

value_domain: Dollar amount of spouse's taxable income reported for the Medicare levy tests
value_source: ATO, Tax return for individuals 2001 (NAT 2541), Spouse details - married or de facto
variable_description: The spouse's taxable income as reported by the taxpayer, held only in the 1999-2000 to 2005-06 income and loss tables. The spouse details pages of the returns of that era collect "Spouse's 2000-01 taxable income" and require it only in defined cases, one being that the person completed the Medicare levy reduction item. The figure is therefore third-hand, written by one partner about the other, and it feeds the family-income test that reduces or removes the levy.
value_definition: A whole-dollar figure of the spouse's taxable income for the same income year, reported on the taxpayer's return rather than taken from the spouse's own assessment.
limitation: A blank does not mean the person had no spouse or that the spouse had no income, only that no item on the return triggered the requirement to report it. Because one partner writes down the other's figure, it can disagree with the spouse's own lodged taxable income.
rationale: The ATO return form of the period defines the spouse income box and lists the items, including the Medicare levy question, that make it compulsory; no live ATO page covers the retired layout.
evidence_quote: You only need to complete spouse's 2000-01 taxable income if: - you had a spouse on 30 June 2001 AND you completed item M1
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed only the custodian's title-case wording with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say whose income this is, who reported it, or when reporting was required.

value_domain: Dollar amount of assessed Medicare levy
value_source: ATO, Taxation statistics 2023-24, Reference material, Calculating net tax
variable_description: The total Medicare levy the ATO assessed on the person for the year, after any reduction or exemption. It is one of the terms the ATO adds when it works out an individual's net tax: "Net tax = Tax on taxable income + Extra income tax - Total non-refundable tax offsets + Medicare levy + Medicare levy surcharge - Remaining foreign income tax offset". The column appears only from the 2020-21 tables, and it is a calculated result, not anything the taxpayer wrote on the return.
value_definition: A dollar amount computed by the ATO from taxable income at the year's levy rate, then adjusted for the low-income reduction and for any full or half exemption days claimed at M1.
limitation: A zero cannot be read as an exemption, because a low income, a family-income reduction or no taxable income all produce the same result, and the M1 day counts are needed to tell them apart. The surcharge is a separate liability and is not included here.
rationale: The ATO's taxation statistics reference material sets out where the Medicare levy sits in the individual net tax calculation, which identifies this column as the assessed levy rather than a return label.
evidence_quote: Net tax = Tax on taxable income + Extra income tax - Total non-refundable tax offsets + Medicare levy + Medicare levy surcharge - Remaining foreign income tax offset
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Total Medicare levy liability' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not distinguish an assessed amount from a claimed one or place it in the net tax calculation.

value_domain: Dollar amount of assessed Medicare levy surcharge
value_source: ATO, Paying the Medicare levy surcharge
variable_description: The extra levy the ATO charged a person for going without private patient hospital cover while earning above the surcharge threshold. The ATO explains what it bites on: "The MLS rate of 1%, 1.25% or 1.5% is levied on: your taxable income, total reportable fringe benefits, and any amount on which family trust distribution tax has been paid." It is calculated by the ATO, prorated by the days the person reported as not liable at M2 label A, and it sits on top of the ordinary Medicare levy.
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to the applicable surcharge rate applied to the surcharge base, scaled to the part of the year for which the person was liable.
limitation: A zero does not identify people with hospital cover, since income below the threshold, an exemption or no taxable income all give zero, and cover has to be read from the private health insurance columns instead. The rate depends on combined family income, so the amount reflects a spouse's circumstances as well as the taxpayer's.
rationale: The ATO surcharge page states the rates and the base the surcharge is levied on, which defines the quantity the custodian's label names.
evidence_quote: The MLS rate of 1%, 1.25% or 1.5% is levied on: your taxable income, total reportable fringe benefits, and any amount on which family trust distribution tax has been paid.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Medicare levy surcharge' and printed the generic sentence twice, so nothing said what the surcharge applies to or that a zero is uninformative about hospital cover.

value_domain: Count of days, 0 to 366, at M2 label A
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M2 Medicare levy surcharge
variable_description: The number of days a person declared they were not liable for the Medicare levy surcharge. The ATO instruction is: "Write at question M2 - label A the number of days for which you don't have to pay MLS", and a person with no liability for the whole year writes 366. The question is compulsory for every taxpayer, so the column is populated even for people far below the surcharge threshold.
value_definition: A whole number of days from 0 to 366, entered by the taxpayer, that scales the surcharge the ATO then calculates.
limitation: A full-year value cannot be read as holding private hospital cover, because everyone under the income threshold also writes the full year, and the two reasons are not distinguished. It records a taxpayer's own conclusion about liability, which the ATO may override on assessment.
rationale: M2 label A is a single compulsory box and the ATO instructions state exactly what number goes in it and the values for the two extreme cases.
evidence_quote: If you don't have to pay MLS for any days during the period 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024, write 366 at question M2 - label A.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's long label with the generic sentence twice, so it never noted the compulsory nature of the question or that a full-year value confounds cover with low income.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the base the surcharge rate was applied to
value_source: ATO, Paying the Medicare levy surcharge, and Medicare levy surcharge income, thresholds and rates
variable_description: The amount of a person's income that the surcharge rate was actually charged on, held only in the 2022-23 and 2023-24 tables. The ATO describes that base as "your taxable income, total reportable fringe benefits, and any amount on which family trust distribution tax has been paid", which is narrower than income for surcharge purposes. Income for surcharge purposes decides whether the surcharge applies and at which rate, and it also folds in net investment losses, reportable super contributions and a spouse's income.
value_definition: A dollar amount equal to taxable income plus reportable fringe benefits plus any family trust distribution tax amount, before the 1%, 1.25% or 1.5% rate is applied.
limitation: It is not the income test that decides liability, so using it as a threshold measure will misclassify people whose investment losses or super contributions push their surcharge income higher. It is an individual base even though the rate that hits it was set by combined family income.
rationale: The ATO surcharge pages separate the base the rate is levied on from income for MLS purposes, which is the distinction the custodian's label turns on.
evidence_quote: We use a special definition of income (called income for MLS purposes) to work out if you have to pay the MLS and the rate you will pay. This income is different from your taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Amount subjected to medicare levy surcharge' with the generic sentence twice, leaving the reader to assume it was the surcharge income test, which it is not.

value_domain: Dollar amount of the Medicare levy surcharge lump sum in arrears tax offset
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2024, question M2 Medicare levy surcharge
variable_description: Relief the ATO grants where a surcharge liability arose only because a back-payment covering earlier years landed in this year's income. The ATO sets out the spouse case at M2: "If you are liable for MLS only because your spouse has shown a lump sum payment in arrears at question 20 ... or question 24 ... you may be entitled to a tax offset up to the amount of MLS you have to pay. We will calculate the tax offset for you." The column runs from the 2015-16 tables onward and is worked out by the ATO, not claimed at a label.
value_definition: A dollar offset capped at the surcharge otherwise payable, granted where arrears income rather than ordinary income took the household over the surcharge threshold.
limitation: It cannot be used to find everyone who received arrears, because it appears only where the arrears actually created a surcharge liability and the taxpayer supplied the supporting schedule. It offsets the surcharge alone and does not undo the extra ordinary tax or Medicare levy the arrears caused.
rationale: The M2 instructions describe the offset, its cap and the fact that the ATO calculates it, which matches the custodian's label naming a surcharge lump sum in arrears offset.
evidence_quote: you may be entitled to a tax offset up to the amount of MLS you have to pay. We will calculate the tax offset for you.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's run-on title with the generic sentence twice, so nothing said that this is ATO-calculated relief capped at the surcharge payable.

value_domain: ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 4 code
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4
variable_description: The SA4 covering the business address a sole trader gave for their main business, on ASGS 2016 boundaries. It runs from the 2010-11 to the 2019-20 tables. The address comes from the Business and professional items schedule, where the taxpayer writes the street address of the main business, so it locates the enterprise rather than the person. The ABS says SA4 "boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities".
value_definition: An SA4 identifier from the ASGS main structure, the largest sub-state region in that structure, geocoded from a single reported business address.
limitation: It shows only the main business where a person ran several, and for a mobile or home-based trade the registered address can be an accountant's or a home office far from where work was done. The taxpayer's own residential geography is in different columns and the two should not be conflated.
rationale: The ABS publishes the classification and defines what an SA4 represents; the address it is coded from is the business address item on the ATO schedule that accompanies the return.
evidence_quote: SA4 boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Business address of main business - SA4' with the generic sentence twice, so it did not say whose address this is or which ASGS edition applies.

value_domain: ASGS Statistical Area Level 4 code, 2021 edition
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4
variable_description: The main business SA4 as recoded to the ASGS 2021 boundaries, present only in the 2020-21 context table. It replaces the 2016-edition column of the same content at the point where the ABS moved to Edition 3, so a business that did not move can still change code between the two columns.
